Your day is built around travel between properties: routine repairs, make-readies on vacant homes, move-in and move-out inspections, and onboarding audits when new properties come into the portfolio. HVAC, plumbing, and electrical work are all in scope. You'll also audit vendor work, which means you need a real eye for quality because if a contractor cut corners, you're the one who catches it before it becomes a bigger problem.

Work orders and communication run through mobile apps, so comfort with a smartphone isn't optional. A company vehicle and gas card are provided, which removes the wear-and-tear concern that comes with field-heavy roles.

The schedule is full-time with no on-call rotation and no weekend requirement. That's genuinely uncommon at this pay range in property maintenance, and it reflects a deliberate staffing model rather than an afterthought.

Who Fits This Role Well

The requirements here are straightforward:

  • HVAC Type II Certification (required); Universal Certification is preferred
  • Valid driver's license with a clean enough record to operate a company vehicle
  • Ability to work independently across multiple sites without daily supervision
  • Comfort using mobile tools for work orders, updates, and field communication
  • Physical capability for the role: lifting up to 50 lbs, bending, climbing, outdoor conditions
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Authorization to work in the U.S. (no visa sponsorship available)

Strong candidates tend to be people who can triage on the spot. In a scattered-site model, you'll sometimes arrive at a property and find something that wasn't on the work order. The technicians who do well here are the ones who troubleshoot accurately, document clearly, and don't need to be managed closely to stay productive. Self-direction isn't a soft skill in this context. It's the core of how the job functions.

Pay runs $25 to $30 per hour depending on experience, certifications, and location factors. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k, generous PTO plus 12 paid holidays, paid parental leave, volunteer time off, and monthly subsidies for wellness and home office or cell phone expenses.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Benton)
job.description:
Prometheus has been holding apartments in the Bay Area since 1965, which means they've seen more market cycles than most operators care to count. As the largest privately held apartment owner in the region, with a portfolio pushing 13,000 units across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle, they're not a startup figuring things out. The infrastructure is there. So is the expectation that you'll use it.

The Benton community in Santa Clara is looking for a Leasing Consultant, though Prometheus calls the role a Neighbor Ambassador internally. The title shift reflects something real about how they operate. This isn't a straight traffic-to-application conversion job. You're handling the full customer-facing experience: touring future residents, walking them through the leasing process, and staying involved after move-in to make sure people actually feel settled. On the admin side, you're preparing rental agreements, pulling market surveys, posting availability, and producing the kind of property-level reporting that keeps operations honest.

Weekend availability is required, full stop. The schedule runs with regular weekdays off, and Prometheus pays a weekend shift premium on top of the base hourly rate of $25.00 to $26.25. Add a $200 per-lease incentive, a discretionary semi-annual bonus, and additional bonuses tied to lease-up performance, referrals, and training coaching, and the compensation picture is more layered than most leasing roles at this level. Benefits include 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision for employees and eligible dependents, 401(k) with employer matching, and tenure-based housing discounts that become more meaningful the longer you stay.

On the candidate side, Prometheus is open about hiring across industries. Prior leasing experience isn't listed as a requirement. What they're actually screening for is harder to fake: comfort in a sales and service environment, genuine follow-through with people, and the kind of self-direction that doesn't need a manager standing nearby to stay productive.

One thing worth knowing about leasing roles at well-capitalized, vertically integrated owners like Prometheus: the exposure is broader than at a fee-management shop. Because acquisitions, development, value-add renovations, and operations all sit under one roof, leasing staff at the property level tend to see more of how the full business works. For someone early in a property management career, that context compounds quickly. Leasing consultants who absorb the operational side of the role, not just the customer-facing piece, tend to move into assistant manager and then manager positions faster than those who treat it as a pure sales job.

What You Bring

  • Experience in customer service, sales, or a client-facing environment (industry doesn't have to be property management)
  • Comfort managing competing tasks across leasing, admin, and resident communication
  • Availability on weekends as a standard part of your schedule
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • A track record of following through, not just initiating

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

This position pulls on three skill sets simultaneously: leasing, financial administration, and people management. You're converting prospects into residents, tracking delinquency and posting payments, and stepping into the Community Manager's seat when they're out. All three happen in the same week, often the same day.

Strong candidates already know how to read a ledger, handle a collections call without escalating tension, and close a tour. The financial side here is real work: ledger audits, payment posting, delinquency follow-up, and supporting reporting for regional leadership. If numbers aren't your thing, this role will feel harder than it should.

What You'll Be Doing at Hawthorne at Stillwater

Day to day, you're supporting leasing activity at this garden-style community in Sneads Ferry. That means responding to leads, conducting tours, processing applications, and keeping renewals moving on schedule. Occupancy is a shared goal, and your leasing activity directly affects it.

On the financial side, you'll oversee rent collection, post payments, scan checks, and run weekly delinquency follow-ups. You'll also conduct regular ledger reviews to catch billing errors and verify account accuracy before they become bigger problems.

You'll manage the community's social media presence, keep common areas and the leasing office presentable, and handle resident concerns with composure. When the Community Manager is unavailable, you run point.

  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months of prior assistant community manager experience preferred
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP designation is a plus
  • Availability for some Saturdays (10 AM to 4 PM) and occasional evenings for resident events

What's Distinctive Here

Hawthorne ranks among the top 50 multifamily management companies nationally, with deep roots in the Southeast. For this role specifically, they offer a structured career path program with real intent behind it: Assistant Community Manager to Community Manager is a stated trajectory, backed by a Learning and Development team. That's worth noting if upward mobility matters to you.

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, and paid parental leave options.

The Sneads Ferry market sits near Camp Lejeune, which creates a steady, military-affiliated renter base. That population tends toward shorter lease terms and higher turnover, so MTM management and renewal retention skills get real exercise here.

job.title: Market Maintenance Technician (Part-Time)20 hours per
job.description:
This part-time role at Dexter Street Commons in Pawtucket covers the full range of day-to-day physical plant work that keeps a residential property running and looking well-maintained. At 20 hours per week, the schedule is flexible, but the work itself is varied and hands-on.

What You'll Actually Do

Most of your time goes toward completing maintenance requests as they come in: repairing doors, locks, tiles, and handrails, swapping out light fixtures, installing smoke detectors, and handling appliance repairs. Cosmetic work is a real part of this position too. Painting units, replacing window screens, and similar make-ready tasks are regular responsibilities, not occasional add-ons. You'll also need to stay sharp on documentation, keeping paperwork and invoices organized for the work you complete.

The role requires availability for emergency situations, including flood response and back-to-back move-ins. Even at part-time hours, those moments call for someone who stays composed and moves quickly. You'll coordinate with outside contractors and vendors, which means you need to know enough about the trades to hold a productive conversation with specialists and verify that work meets the property's standards.

What You Bring

  • At least six months of hands-on trade or building maintenance experience
  • Working familiarity with electrical and mechanical systems at a repair level
  • Comfort identifying safety concerns and acting on them without waiting to be told
  • Specialized trade background in plumbing, electrical, HVAC, or roofing is a meaningful advantage
  • Reliability and the ability to manage your own work order flow with minimal supervision

Context Worth Knowing

John M. Corcoran and Company has operated in New England since 1951, and the culture reflects that longevity: long tenure on staff, institutional knowledge that gets passed down, and a genuine emphasis on quality over speed. That context matters for a maintenance role because it shapes expectations. Properties managed by firms with that kind of history tend to hold high standards for presentation and resident experience, which means cosmetic attention and follow-through on punch list items carry real weight, not just the mechanical repairs.

For someone building a maintenance career, part-time work at a well-run property is genuinely useful experience. The breadth of work here, from appliance repairs to contractor coordination to emergency response, covers skills that transfer directly to a full-time maintenance technician or lead tech role. If you're looking to develop a well-rounded maintenance background while working a flexible schedule, this position builds exactly the kind of varied, documented experience that makes future employers pay attention.

Compensation runs between $26.75 and $32.00 per hour, and the position includes a $1,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off, and a 401(k) with company match.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work at a residential apartment community covers a wide range of trades, and the technician who thrives here is someone who can shift from a plumbing call in the morning to an electrical issue in the afternoon without losing focus. Cottonwood Residential is adding a Maintenance Technician at Stratford at Hillcrest Apartments in Winston-Salem, and this is a role that draws on what you already know while steadily expanding what you can do.

On the technical side, you'll handle repairs across plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry, both inside units and across the property grounds. The role operates within standard community hours, and it includes on-call responsibility for after-hours emergencies. That after-hours piece is worth being clear-eyed about: it's part of the job, and it's where your ability to diagnose and resolve problems under pressure gets sharpened most. You won't be doing it alone. The Service Manager provides support, and you'll work within established company standards on every call.

Physically, the role demands real stamina. You'll be on your feet most of the day, climbing stairs and ladders, working in tight spaces, and lifting up to 50 pounds regularly. A valid driver's license is required. EPA Type II or Universal certification, HVAC troubleshooting experience, and CPO certification each strengthen your candidacy, though they aren't listed as hard requirements.

What the role requires vs. what it builds

Coming in, you need working knowledge of residential repairs across at least a couple of trades, solid physical capability, and the communication skills to work through work orders and interact with residents clearly. What the role builds is something different: diagnostic instincts. Apartment maintenance is repetitive enough that patterns emerge quickly. Over time, you develop a mental model of how systems fail in a garden-style residential setting, which makes you faster and more accurate on every turn and make-ready you touch.

Technicians who grow fastest in roles like this are the ones who treat the on-call rotation as a learning accelerator rather than just an obligation. Emergency calls, by definition, involve conditions you haven't seen before, and the problem-solving you do at 10 PM on a Saturday builds judgment that routine daytime work can't replicate.

  • Valid driver's license (required)
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and work on your feet for extended periods
  • Availability for on-call after-hours emergency coverage
  • Ability to work evenings and weekends as part of standard scheduling
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (a plus)
  • HVAC troubleshooting experience (a plus)
  • CPO certification (a plus)

Cottonwood Residential offers health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage with a quick eligibility window, a 401k with company match, HSA matching, three weeks of paid time off in the first year, and over ten paid holidays annually.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
This role covers five apartment communities across two Pittsburgh-area submarkets: four properties totaling 198 units in Greensburg and one 97-unit community in New Kensington. Multi-site portfolios at this scale demand someone who can move fluidly between hands-on skilled trades work and the logistical side of managing people, vendors, and budgets. Birgo is looking for a maintenance supervisor who does both well.

The day-to-day splits roughly into two modes. Some of it is field work: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, drywall, turns, punch lists, and groundskeeping across properties that aren't all in the same zip code. The rest is coordination: leading a two-person tech team, sourcing and managing contractors when the scope exceeds what the crew can handle, tracking expenditures against budget, and serving as the operational link between maintenance and property management. AppFolio handles work orders in a paperless workflow, so comfort with mobile tools matters here.

The Greensburg and New Kensington markets sit in the older housing stock belt east and northeast of Pittsburgh. Properties in these corridors tend to be garden-style or low-rise buildings with aging mechanical systems, which means HVAC and plumbing calls come with some frequency. A supervisor who can personally handle high-skill repairs keeps vendor costs down and reduces unit downtime on turns. That's a real budget lever at this portfolio size.

Birgo emphasizes servant leadership internally, and that framing is worth taking seriously in the context of this role. Managing two techs means coaching and developing them, not just directing work. Strong candidates will have experience building a team's technical capability over time, not just assigning jobs and checking completions. Emotional intelligence in conflict resolution, which comes up in any maintenance team eventually, matters as much as trade credentials here.

What Birgo is Looking For

  • 5 or more years of multifamily maintenance experience
  • 3 or more years in a supervisory capacity
  • Hands-on expertise across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and drywall
  • Experience managing a multi-site portfolio
  • Comfort with mobile work order platforms (AppFolio experience is a plus)
  • Budget awareness and cost control discipline
  • Active driver's license, reliable insured vehicle, and ability to lift 50 pounds unassisted

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, with participation in an on-call rotation. Compensation is $31 per hour. Birgo offers medical, dental, vision, life, and short-term disability insurance with a company contribution, a 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, paid holidays, sick time, mileage and boot reimbursements, uniforms, a professional development reimbursement program, profit-sharing, and a discount at Birgo properties.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (The Reserve)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Maintenance technicians at The Reserve handle the full range of day-to-day upkeep: HVAC service and repairs, plumbing, electrical work, and structural fixes across the property's interior and exterior. You're also responsible for preventative maintenance, which means staying ahead of issues before they turn into emergency calls. Speaking of which, after-hours emergencies are part of this role. When a resident loses heat in January or has a water leak at midnight, someone has to respond. That's you sometimes.

On a typical day, you'll work through a queue of resident service requests, document what you find, complete the work, and move on to the next one. Keeping accurate records matters here, both for accountability and for spotting recurring problems on the property. The job keeps you moving physically, so expect time on your feet, climbing, bending, and lifting throughout your shift.

What You Bring

  • 2 to 3 years of maintenance experience in a residential or comparable setting
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license
  • EPA Type 2 or Universal certification (preferred but not required)
  • Ability to communicate clearly with residents and teammates, even when the situation is frustrating

The EPA certification is worth mentioning separately. If you have it, you're more useful on HVAC work from day one. If you don't, it's a credential worth pursuing early and one that adds real value to your skill set across any property you work on in the future.

The Role in Context

BAM Companies has been operating since 2010 and manages properties across multiple markets. The Reserve in Evansville is part of that portfolio. Pay for this position ranges from $17 to $19 per hour depending on experience and qualifications. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage with BAM covering a significant share of the cost, paid life insurance, rent discounts at BAM properties, and a PTO structure that gives you 88 hours after 90 days and 120 hours after your first year, plus 14.5 paid holidays.

One honest note for anyone weighing this against other maintenance roles: the difference between a solid technician and an exceptional one at a property like this usually comes down to how they handle resident interactions, not just the technical work. You can fix a unit perfectly, but if you leave a resident feeling dismissed or uninformed, the job isn't really done. The technical skills get you hired. The communication habits are what build a reputation on site.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Richardson, TX
job.description:
It's 7 a.m. and you're already walking the grounds at The Pradera in Richardson, TX, punch list in hand, checking curb appeal before residents head to work. By 9 a.m., you're knee-deep in a plumbing call. That's a typical Tuesday.

What the Role Actually Covers

Berkshire Residential Investments owns and manages its own portfolio, which means decisions move faster and accountability runs deeper than at a typical third-party shop. As a Maintenance Technician at The Pradera, you're a core part of keeping the physical asset performing. That means more than just closing work orders. You'll help preserve the property's condition over time, support management in holding community standards, and keep safety protocols consistently enforced.

Day to day, you're working across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems. You'll help manage the shop, track inventory, and maintain key security. Curb appeal is taken seriously here. A well-kept exterior drives traffic, supports occupancy, and reflects directly on resident retention. You'll be expected to treat that as your responsibility, not just a manager's concern.

Customer service is part of the job description for real, not as an afterthought. Residents notice whether maintenance staff are approachable and communicative. How you carry yourself during a service call affects renewal decisions more than most people realize.

What Berkshire Is Looking For

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across the core trades: appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and building maintenance
  • Comfort with basic computer use and related applications for work order management
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
  • A self-directed approach to quality and follow-through on punch list items

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and solid insurance coverage. The company emphasizes internal growth, which means a technician who performs consistently has a real path toward a lead or service manager role over time.

One thing worth knowing: Richardson sits in a dense DFW submarket with a lot of multifamily competition. Properties that stay tight on make-ready times and curb appeal hold occupancy better than those that don't. A technician who owns their work order queue and keeps turns moving on schedule contributes directly to that NOI story, even if the numbers don't show up on your daily to-do list.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Leasing skills sit at the center of this role, and they show up in concrete, measurable ways. At Redstone Residential's Rexburg community, a Leasing Manager's effectiveness gets measured in occupancy trends, renewal rates, and the quality of every prospect interaction from the first phone call to the signed lease. This is a hands-on leasing position with real operational responsibility layered in.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

Sales and customer service aren't background skills here. They drive the core function of the job. You'll conduct prospect tours, manage phone and email pipelines, and run renewal campaigns designed to hold occupancy. Redstone uses Entrata as its leasing platform, so comfort with structured software workflows matters. You'll also work within their online and social marketing systems, which means basic SEO awareness and digital communication skills translate directly into leasing performance.

On the administrative side, you'll maintain resident ledgers and keep balances accurate. That requires attention to detail and a working comfort with cloud-based tools like Google Drive and Dropbox. Mistakes in ledger management create downstream problems for collections and delinquency tracking, so accuracy carries real weight.

The Operational Layer

Beyond leasing, this role supports the Community Manager across broader operations. That includes budget performance awareness, rent collections, and some staff administration. You're not just filling units. You're helping keep the property running day to day, which gives you visibility into how leasing activity connects to NOI and overall community health.

Rexburg is a student-market town built largely around BYU-Idaho's enrollment calendar. That means leasing cycles here follow a rhythm that differs from conventional multifamily. Traffic peaks and lease-up pressure align with academic timelines, and renewal campaigns need to account for the transient nature of a student population. Experience in or awareness of student housing dynamics is a genuine advantage in this market.

What Separates Strong Candidates

  • Demonstrated ability to hit leasing goals without waiting to be directed, especially during peak traffic periods
  • Comfort using Entrata or a comparable leasing CRM, not just basic office software
  • A communication style that works equally well with prospects, current residents, and teammates
  • Enough composure to handle a high-volume leasing season without letting service quality slip

Redstone operates at scale, managing over 38,000 beds across 20 states as a third-party manager. That structure means their systems, reporting standards, and leasing processes are well-developed. For someone early in a property management career, working inside that kind of operational framework builds transferable skills quickly. The Leasing Manager role is a natural stepping stone toward a Community Manager position, particularly for candidates who develop both the leasing and administrative sides of the job.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the center of daily operations at a Fairstead affordable housing property in Dallas. You'll work alongside the Property Manager to keep the property compliant, occupied, and financially sound. A good portion of your time goes toward HUD compliance: executing the 4350.3 Handbook requirements, coordinating annual and interim recertification reviews, and helping prepare the property for REAC inspections, Management and Occupancy Reviews, LIHTC reviews, and investor site visits. When EHS violations surface, you help get them cleared.

On the financial side, you'll track arrears daily, ensure rents are collected, posted, and deposited, and create purchase orders in Yardi. You'll work with the in-house legal team to monitor rent payment status and coordinate evictions when lease violations escalate past intervention. On the resident-facing side, you're responding to calls, emails, and complaints within a few hours, alerting staff to move-ins and move-outs, and making sure the maintenance team closes out service requests. You also manage the lease renewal program to protect retention.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of experience in affordable housing leasing or property management (required)
  • Working knowledge of EIV, Yardi, and RealPage
  • Familiarity with HUD 4350.3 compliance requirements and LIHTC recertification processes
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, specifically for resident relations and documentation
  • Knowledge of the Dallas residential market

What This Role Builds

Affordable housing compliance is a distinct discipline within property management, and this position develops real depth in it. Candidates who come from conventional multifamily often underestimate how different the regulatory cadence is. You'll sharpen your ability to read and apply HUD guidance, manage recertification timelines, and prepare a property for formal review cycles. Those skills transfer directly into Community Manager roles at affordable properties, compliance specialist positions, or regional roles within affordable housing portfolios. Fairstead operates across 28 states with more than 30,000 units, so internal advancement for people who prove themselves operationally is a realistic path.

The candidates who thrive here combine genuine attention to detail on the compliance and financial side with the interpersonal steadiness that resident-facing work requires. Affordable housing residents often face real housing instability, so the ability to handle difficult conversations with patience and professionalism matters as much as knowing your way around Yardi. If you've worked affordable housing and already understand the distinction between market-rate delinquency follow-up and the specific protocols required under HUD guidelines, you'll hit the ground running.

job.title: Community Manager - Multi site - The Hixon and Terava Apartments
job.description:
You're wrapping up a site visit at The Hixon, then driving across Bend to check in with the team at Terava before the afternoon leasing rush. That's the rhythm of this role: two communities, one manager, constant context-switching.

The Role

CloudTen Residential is hiring a Multi-Site Community Manager to oversee day-to-day operations at two Bend, Oregon apartment communities: The Hixon and Terava. You'll report to a Regional Manager and carry full operational accountability across both sites. That means staffing, leasing, financials, maintenance oversight, compliance, and resident relations. A valid driver's license is required.

On the financial side, you'll manage rent collection, work delinquent accounts within Oregon landlord-tenant law, handle daily deposits, monitor expenses, and contribute to budget preparation. You're expected to flag inefficiencies and recommend cost-effective improvements, not just report numbers up the chain.

Leasing and marketing are part of the job too. You'll oversee unit advertising, conduct showings, keep lease records clean, and analyze local market data to guide pricing decisions. Renewal outreach and retention efforts fall under your scope as well.

People management is a core part of this position. You'll hire, train, and evaluate on-site staff across both properties. That includes building a team culture that reflects CloudTen's standards and giving people what they need to do their jobs well.

What You Need

  • At least two years of property management experience; multi-site experience is a plus
  • Solid working knowledge of Oregon landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing regulations
  • Comfort with property management software and Microsoft Office (Word and Excel in particular)
  • Strong organizational skills, since you'll be managing schedules, records, and priorities across two locations simultaneously
  • High school diploma required; college coursework or a degree in a related field is preferred
  • Valid driver's license

Compensation is set at $85,000 annually. CloudTen offers medical, dental, and vision insurance, company-paid life insurance, FSA options, paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays.

One thing worth knowing about this specific setup: managing two separate communities means your authority is real, but your time is divided. Strong candidates for multi-site roles tend to be people who build systems rather than rely on memory. If you've managed a single property well by staying on top of every detail personally, that approach gets harder to sustain when you're splitting time between two sites. Managers who document processes, delegate effectively, and trust their on-site teams tend to do better in this structure than those who prefer to control everything directly.

job.title: Service Manager
job.description:
What This Role Covers

Multifamily maintenance operations run on the Service Manager. Leasing fills units; the Service Manager keeps residents in them. At Huntington at Stonefield, a Dream Live Prosper Communities property in Houston, this position owns the full maintenance function: work order turnaround, make-ready scheduling, preventative maintenance, vendor oversight, and budget control through AppFolio.

The property requires lease-up experience. That's a specific ask. During a lease-up, vacant units hit the schedule in waves, turn timelines compress, and the make-ready process has to run without much margin for error. If you've managed a maintenance team through a lease-up before, you understand the pace this role operates at from the start.

Day to day, you're directing your team's work order assignments, targeting 24-hour completion on service requests and 5-day turns on vacancies. You're also in the field alongside your crew, handling HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, and pool maintenance yourself when needed. This is a working manager role, not a desk job.

What You Bring

  • HVAC certification required; EPA 608 or equivalent
  • Proven background as a maintenance supervisor or HVAC service manager in multifamily
  • Lease-up experience is required, not preferred
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and pool equipment
  • Experience managing vendor relationships and controlling OpEx budgets
  • Comfortable with AppFolio or similar property management software for purchasing and work order tracking
  • Valid driver's license with a clean record and a reliable vehicle for daily use and on-call rotation
  • Own basic tools; ability to lift 50+ lbs and handle multi-floor physical demands daily
  • Flexible schedule availability including weekends

The strongest candidates here will have run preventative maintenance programs before, not just reacted to breakdowns. PM schedules directly protect NOI by reducing emergency repair costs and extending equipment life. If you've built or improved a PM calendar at a previous property, that experience translates immediately.

This is a full-time, on-site position at 13100 Stonefield Drive, Houston, TX 77014. Dream Live Prosper Communities operates as part of DLP Capital, which has placed on the Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private companies for thirteen consecutive years.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Student housing maintenance runs at a different tempo than conventional multifamily. Turns happen in concentrated windows, pool logs need to be airtight, and a broken HVAC unit in a Tempe summer is a genuine emergency. PeakMade Real Estate manages off-campus student communities across the country, and this Maintenance Technician role in Tempe sits at the center of keeping one of those assets performing at its physical best.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're moving through service requests, preventative maintenance tasks, and curb appeal walkthroughs. In Tempe, that means pool chemistry logs are not optional paperwork. With summer temperatures routinely pushing past 110 degrees, the pool is a heavily used amenity and the chemical records need to be accurate and current. HVAC is similarly non-negotiable. The ability to troubleshoot and repair HVAC systems independently matters here more than it would in a moderate climate.

Turn season is where student housing separates from conventional apartments. Units flip in a compressed cycle, and you'll be working with the maintenance team to schedule and execute make-ready work at volume. A clean punch list process and solid communication with the Maintenance Supervisor keeps that from becoming chaos. The rest of the year involves preventative maintenance schedules, equipment upkeep per manufacturer specs, and keeping grounds, breezeways, and common areas in good shape.

You'll also participate in on-call rotation. That's the honest part of the job that doesn't always get front-billed. For the right candidate, it's manageable. For someone who hasn't done rotating emergency coverage before, it's worth knowing upfront.

What PeakMade Is Looking For

  • At least one year of maintenance experience, apartment industry preferred
  • Ability to troubleshoot and repair HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances
  • EPA Type I and II certification preferred
  • Must live within 30 miles of the property and have reliable transportation
  • Availability for a varied schedule including weekends, holidays, and on-call rotation
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at heights on ladders, and perform physical tasks outdoors in extreme temperatures
  • Candidates should bring their own hand tools
  • Additional certifications as required by local, state, or federal law

PeakMade offers technical training and the opportunity to earn HVAC and CPO certifications through the company, which is a real differentiator for technicians looking to build credentials. A tech who comes in with strong hands-on skills and adds those certifications has a clear path toward a Maintenance Supervisor role. The company also offers paid parental leave, PTO plus two additional wellbeing days, 401(k) match, and monthly renewal bonuses.

Strong candidates for this specific role will already be comfortable working with pool systems and have some HVAC diagnostic experience. Given the Tempe climate and the student housing turn cycle, those two skill areas will get tested quickly and often.

job.title: Occupancy Specialist Apartment Community
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Channel Island Apartments is a 152-unit affordable housing community in Oxnard, and this role sits at the intersection of compliance and leasing. The Occupancy Specialist owns the full application cycle: screening income-eligible households against HUD and LIHTC regulatory requirements, processing move-ins, and completing annual and interim recertifications on time and in full. A missed recertification or a documentation gap on a tax credit file isn't a minor inconvenience here. It's a compliance event. So the person in this seat needs to be organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable working within the specific rules that govern affordable housing occupancy.

Beyond the file work, you're also the frontline leasing presence. That means conducting property tours, following up on leads, monitoring local market conditions, and contributing to marketing strategies that keep occupancy where it needs to be. You'll coordinate with the property manager and maintenance team on move-in readiness and unit inspections, and you'll handle resident concerns with the kind of professionalism that keeps a community stable. Delinquency management is part of the picture too, including rent collection and follow-up consistent with company procedures.

IPG is a national operator with a portfolio of over 40 multifamily communities and 111 mobile home locations across 13 states, so there's real infrastructure behind this role. Proficiency in Yardi or comparable property management software is expected from day one.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of leasing or occupancy experience in property management
  • Bilingual fluency in English and Spanish (this is a hard requirement, not a preference)
  • Familiarity with LIHTC and Section 8 program requirements, or a demonstrated ability to get up to speed quickly
  • Experience with delinquency tracking and rent collection processes
  • Comfort with property management platforms such as Yardi, Rent Cafe, or Blue Moon
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to interact clearly with regulatory agencies and housing authorities
  • Solid time management and the discipline to keep recertification timelines on track across a 152-unit community

Context Worth Knowing

Affordable housing occupancy roles carry a compliance burden that market-rate leasing positions don't. LIHTC files require income verification, asset documentation, and student status review at every certification. HUD programs add their own audit trail requirements. Candidates who've only worked conventional leasing will need to invest real time learning the regulatory side. Those who already understand tax credit compliance will be productive much faster and will likely find this role a strong foundation for a compliance coordinator or property manager position within an affordable housing portfolio. The $24 to $28 hourly range reflects the specialized nature of the work, and the Monday through Friday, 8 to 5 schedule is a genuine quality-of-life advantage compared to many leasing roles.

job.title: Apartment Leasing Consultant - Capri North and South
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Capri North and South is an AIR Communities property in Las Vegas, and this leasing consultant role is fundamentally a sales position with a customer service backbone. Your job is to drive occupancy by converting traffic into signed leases. That means working AIR's sales process start to finish: responding promptly to inquiries, scheduling and conducting tours, and closing. Follow-up discipline matters here. Prospects who don't hear back quickly move on, and every missed connection is a missed lease.

Commission structure has multiple tiers, so your earnings aren't flat. Higher-rent units, longer lease terms (18 months or more beats the standard 12), and exceeding monthly goals each unlock additional commission percentages on top of the $20/hour base. If you're consistently closing, those layers add up fast. If you're just hitting quota, you're leaving money on the table.

Beyond your home property, you'll provide leasing support across AIR's portfolio as needed. That means your performance metrics don't live in a vacuum. You're part of a broader operation where occupancy, traffic-to-lease conversion, and delinquency prevention all connect. You'll also contribute to community marketing efforts and operate within Fair Housing guidelines at every step.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of sales or customer service experience with measurable goal achievement. Property management background is a plus, but hospitality, retail, and restaurant experience translate well.
  • A track record of following a defined sales process, not just winging it.
  • Schedule flexibility, including weekends. Leasing offices don't close on Saturdays.
  • Reliable transportation and strong English communication skills, written and verbal.
  • Genuine ability to read a prospect and adapt your pitch to what they actually need in a home.

The Bigger Picture

Las Vegas is a high-velocity rental market. Renter mobility is above average, which means traffic can be strong but conversion windows are short. The candidates who perform best in this type of environment treat every tour as a one-shot opportunity. They know their floor plans cold, they understand what makes each unit worth its rent premium, and they close without being pushy. Average leasing consultants wait for prospects to decide. Strong ones guide the decision.

AIR offers a 25% rent discount at any AIR community, which means you could live onsite and eliminate your commute entirely. The company also offers a potential winter break after peak season with benefits intact, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, and up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave. Career-wise, strong leasing consultants at companies like AIR typically move into assistant manager and property manager roles. The skills you build here, closing under pressure, managing resident relationships, and tracking your own performance metrics, carry directly into those next steps.

job.title: Assistant Manager - Avenue 25
job.description:
It's 8:55 AM and there's a bank deposit to finalize, two make-ready inspections before noon, and a resident in the leasing office waiting to talk about a charge on their account. That's a typical Tuesday at Avenue 25, and it's exactly the kind of controlled chaos this role is built for.

What the Role Actually Involves

Olympus Property is hiring an Assistant Manager for Avenue 25 in Phoenix, a full-time onsite position that sits at the intersection of financial accountability and resident relations. You'll handle daily rent collection and ensure all deposits hit before bank close, maintain accurate resident and financial records, and step into the Business Manager seat when they're out. Delinquency doesn't wait, and neither does this role.

You'll also carry leasing responsibilities when the team needs coverage. That means showing units, supporting retention efforts, and participating in community events, some of which fall after standard hours or on the first weekend of the month. Inspecting make-ready apartments before move-in is part of your regular cadence, and you'll process final account statements when residents move out, including assessing unit conditions and coordinating disposition paperwork.

Staying current on the Phoenix submarket matters here. New construction, nearby retail shifts, and hiring trends in the area all feed into occupancy decisions, and Olympus expects their onsite teams to bring that awareness into daily operations.

What Olympus is Looking For

  • Prior onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or a cross-trained Leasing Consultant at an apartment community
  • Familiarity with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite (strongly preferred)
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with flexibility for after-hours events and first-weekend coverage
  • Comfort handling both financial recordkeeping and face-to-face resident interactions on the same shift
  • Detail orientation around deposits, compliance, and file integrity

Pay runs $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience, with monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses on top of base. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, educational assistance, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program. Olympus has earned a spot on the National Apartment Association's Top Employer list three consecutive years, 2023 through 2025.

One thing that separates strong Assistant Manager candidates from average ones in a Phoenix lease-up or stabilized asset: the ability to protect NOI from two directions at once. That means keeping collections tight while also keeping renewal traffic warm. Operators who treat those as separate jobs tend to let one slip. The best Assistant Managers run them in parallel, and Olympus structures its bonus incentives to reinforce exactly that habit.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Weinstein Properties has operated apartment communities for over 70 years under continuous family ownership, and that longevity shows in how they run properties: closely, consistently, and with direct involvement from corporate. This Assistant Property Manager role at Bexley Chamblee sits inside that structure, which means you'll have real operational support rather than being left to figure things out on your own.

Chamblee's multifamily market has tightened considerably as the city has absorbed spillover demand from Buckhead and Midtown, and Class A communities there compete on service quality as much as amenities. The expectation at this property reflects that reality: residents notice when operations slip, and Weinstein's hands-on model is built to prevent that.

What the Role Actually Involves

Day-to-day, you're functioning as the operational anchor of the community. That means handling escalated resident concerns before they become bigger problems, keeping leasing activity moving, monitoring key performance metrics, and partnering with the Maintenance Supervisor to manage projects and keep the property in top condition. You'll also serve as a communication bridge between on-site staff and corporate, which at Weinstein means regular contact rather than occasional check-ins.

The corporate team is described as genuinely hands-on, providing process guidance and direct support rather than leaving property teams to self-direct. If you've worked at a company where "corporate support" meant receiving a policy manual and not much else, this will feel different.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Prior property management experience, with Class A multifamily exposure preferred
  • Comfort working within defined processes and a structured operating environment
  • Strong communication habits and a genuine sense of urgency when issues arise
  • Experience leading or mentoring on-site team members
  • Ability to manage high volumes of resident and corporate requests without losing attention to detail

Candidates who do well here tend to be people who find structure clarifying rather than constraining. Weinstein's model rewards accountability and consistency. If you prefer to set your own systems from scratch at every property, the fit may not be there. But if you want to operate inside a proven framework with leadership that's genuinely accessible, that's exactly what this role offers.

Compensation is competitive and experience-based, with both quarterly and annual bonus opportunities included.

job.title: Maintenance Techician- Sonoran Apartments
job.description:
Maintenance technician roles at mid-size regional operators tend to reward generalists. The person who can clear a service request queue in the morning, run a make-ready punch list in the afternoon, and field an after-hours emergency call that evening is the one who grows fastest in this environment. That's the kind of technician MG Properties is looking for at Sonoran Apartments in Phoenix.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

MG Properties has spent over 30 years acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S., and their maintenance teams reflect that depth. At Sonoran, you'll be handling the full scope of day-to-day upkeep: completing resident service requests, performing appliance repairs, painting, grounds and common area cleaning, and turning units between residents. Turns, in particular, require you to move fast without cutting corners. A tight make-ready timeline keeps occupancy healthy, and a sloppy punch list creates callbacks that cost everyone time.

You'll also carry on-call rotation responsibility. That means some evenings and weekends, you're the person a resident reaches when something goes wrong. Reliable transportation isn't listed as a preference here. It's a firm requirement.

What This Role Requires

  • At least two years of apartment maintenance experience, ideally on a property of 200 units or more
  • Working knowledge across trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and general repairs
  • A genuine customer service orientation. Residents interact with maintenance more directly than almost any other staff, and how you handle those moments shapes the community's reputation
  • Flexibility and the ability to work within a team, including on-call rotation
  • Reliable personal transportation

What This Role Builds

Technicians who come in with solid trade skills but limited exposure to apartment-specific operations will develop real fluency here. Managing a service request load across a 200-plus unit property teaches prioritization in a way that single-family or commercial work rarely does. You'll also build familiarity with turn workflow and the pace expectations that come with it, which is foundational if you're working toward a lead tech or maintenance supervisor role down the line.

MG Properties offers monthly bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, and a full benefits package including medical, dental, and vision. Employees also receive rental discounts and paid time off including holidays and personal days.

Phoenix's apartment market has seen sustained construction and population growth, which means properties here deal with high traffic, competitive lease-up pressure, and resident expectations that reflect newer product in the market. Maintenance teams that run tight, responsive operations are a direct competitive advantage. That's the context you'd be stepping into at Sonoran.

job.title: Housekeeper, Full-Time
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This full-time housekeeper role at Redpoint College Station puts you at the center of the resident experience every single day. The property's common areas, including the pool and spa, clubroom, public restrooms, and laundry rooms, stay clean and presentable because of the work you do. That means sweeping, mopping, dusting, and polishing on a regular schedule, clearing debris from parking areas, walkways, and stairways, and keeping the curbs clean. You'll also step in to support general maintenance needs and assist with cleaning and moving tasks as the property requires. When something looks damaged, broken, or off, you flag it to your supervisor rather than wait for it to become a bigger problem.

The on-call component is real. Outside of approved PTO, you're expected to be available for after-hours and weekend situations. Student housing runs on a tight schedule around move-ins, move-outs, and events, and the property needs to look sharp when it matters most. A valid driver's license is required, and the physical demands are genuine: standing for a full shift and lifting up to 100 lbs. are part of the job.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED, plus at least one year of full-time housekeeping or cleaning experience (or an equivalent combination)
  • Ability to read instructions and document labor and materials accurately
  • Reliable attendance and schedule flexibility, including availability for after-hours emergencies
  • Valid driver's license
  • Physical ability to stand for extended periods and lift up to 100 lbs.
  • Comfort working within OSHA and safety guidelines, and following property-specific procedures

Where This Role Fits in a Property Career

Housekeeping and porter work in student housing is often where people build their first real foundation in property operations. You learn how a community functions from the ground up: what common areas drive resident satisfaction, how make-ready turns flow, and how maintenance teams coordinate. People who take this work seriously and develop a reputation for dependability often move into maintenance technician roles or lead porter positions. The skills you build here, specifically attention to asset condition, communication with supervisors, and safety awareness, carry directly into any property operations role you pursue later.

Scion offers health, dental, and vision insurance, 401k matching, paid parental and maternal leave, paid time off, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. For a non-exempt, full-time position in student housing operations, that's a solid package worth noting.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Most apartment communities run on the visible work of leasing staff, but the physical product residents actually pay for depends entirely on what happens in the maintenance shop. At a stabilized residential community like Westwood Village in Westland, a skilled technician isn't just fixing things. They're protecting NOI, preserving curb appeal, and directly shaping whether residents renew. That's the context this role sits inside.

Paragon Properties is hiring a Maintenance Technician at Westwood Village Apartments, a full-time position paying up to $26/hr based on experience and certifications. The schedule is a guaranteed 40-hour week, with after-hours on-call rotation that includes weekends and holidays. Paragon provides an on-call bonus and a quarterly team bonus, which reflects a comp structure that actually rewards the extra burden of emergency availability rather than just expecting it.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

Your workload will split between resident service requests and make-ready work. On the make-ready side, you'll prep vacant units for occupancy, handling basic drywall patching, painting, and rough carpentry as part of the turn process. On the service side, you'll troubleshoot and repair plumbing, electrical systems, major appliances, pool and spa equipment, and HVAC. HVAC certification (Type II or Universal) is strongly preferred, and given how much of a technician's time goes toward heating and cooling calls, that credential carries real weight here.

Curb appeal and physical integrity of the property are also part of the job. You'll flag potential liabilities and propose improvements when you spot them, which means this role requires some situational awareness beyond just closing out work orders.

What the Role Builds Toward

Technicians who develop a strong combination of HVAC competency, appliance repair, and turn experience tend to move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles within two to four years. At a company like Paragon that offers internal certification programs and advancement pathways, the skills you build here compound quickly. Universal EPA certification alone opens doors to higher-comp positions across Class A, B, and C communities throughout any market. If you eventually want to move into a maintenance director or regional facilities role, the foundation starts with being the person who can diagnose a condensate line issue and also spot a trip hazard in the parking lot on the same afternoon.

What Paragon Offers

  • Up to $26/hr depending on experience and certifications
  • Paid time off plus 9 company-paid holidays
  • Rent discount at Paragon communities
  • 401(k) with employer contribution
  • After-hours on-call bonus and quarterly team bonus
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance with a short enrollment waiting period
  • Company-paid life and disability insurance
  • Tool kit provided after 30-day new hire training period
  • Uniform program and employee recognition program

What the Role Requires

  • At least one year of maintenance experience, whether technical, vocational, or hands-on
  • HVAC Type II or Universal certification, strongly preferred
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • High school diploma required; trade school or college-level coursework strongly preferred
  • Ability to work outdoors year-round in Michigan weather
  • Pre-employment background check, drug screening, and physical required

The candidate who stands out in this role combines technical range with genuine follow-through on customer service. Residents remember how a technician communicated during a repair almost as much as whether the repair held. That combination of craft and communication is what tends to get noticed at the company level and lead to the next step.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Puts to Work Every Day

Community Manager work at Ackermann Group sits at the intersection of financial oversight, team leadership, and resident experience. You'll draw on your ability to read occupancy trends, manage delinquency, and evaluate NOI performance through property management software. Yardi Voyager experience is particularly useful here, as is comfort with reporting tools that surface T-12 and T-3 data quickly. On the leasing side, you'll need a sharp eye for traffic patterns and the judgment to adjust concessions or marketing strategies when numbers shift. This is a role where financial fluency and people skills work together constantly.

The maintenance side of the job demands a different but equally important skill set. You'll coordinate with your Maintenance Supervisor on unit turns, make-ready timelines, preventative maintenance schedules, and service request completion rates. Capex project management also falls under your scope, which means tracking budgets, communicating with leadership, and keeping projects on schedule without losing sight of day-to-day operations. The ability to hold both the strategic and the tactical at the same time is what separates a strong Community Manager from an average one.

Skills This Role Builds

If your background is primarily in leasing or assistant management, this role accelerates your development in two areas that matter most for senior property management positions: full P&L accountability and cross-functional team leadership. You'll build experience recruiting and interviewing your own staff in collaboration with HR and your Regional Manager. You'll set performance goals, run site-level meetings, and coach a leasing and maintenance team through the full operating cycle. Those experiences translate directly to Regional Manager and Director of Operations roles down the line.

Working with tools like EliseAI and AIRM also gives you exposure to AI-assisted leasing and revenue management platforms that are reshaping how multifamily operators handle prospect communication and pricing. Getting hands-on experience with these systems now puts you ahead of peers who haven't worked in environments where that technology is already embedded in daily operations.

What Ackermann Group Brings to the Role

Ackermann Group has been developing and managing properties in the Midwest since 1938. That kind of tenure in one market means the operational infrastructure is mature and the institutional knowledge runs deep. Columbus is a strong multifamily market with consistent demand driven by a large university presence, a growing tech sector, and steady in-migration. Working for a company with deep local roots means your Regional Manager understands the market dynamics you're operating in, which makes the collaboration on marketing strategy and budget planning more grounded than it often is at national operators.

The compensation structure includes quarterly bonuses and commission potential on new and renewed leases, which aligns your financial incentives directly with occupancy and retention performance. A CAM certification is preferred, and the company offers career coaching and development support if you're working toward it.

  • At least 2 years of residential property management or relevant leadership experience required
  • Proficiency in property management software required; Yardi Voyager, Rent Cafe CRM, EliseAI, and AIRM experience preferred
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing laws required
  • CAM certification preferred
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred
  • Schedule includes Monday through Friday, 9am to 6pm, plus at least one Saturday per month

job.title: Maintenance Technician - San Diego, CA
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

At The Rey in San Diego, the Maintenance Technician role touches nearly every corner of daily community life. You're the person residents call when something goes wrong, and you're also the one quietly keeping things from going wrong in the first place. That balance between reactive repairs and proactive upkeep is really what defines this position.

Day to day, you'll handle the full range of general maintenance needs: plumbing fixes, electrical troubleshooting, appliance repairs, carpentry work, and general building upkeep. You'll help manage the shop, keep inventory organized, and make sure equipment and keys are properly secured. Curb appeal matters here. If something looks off walking through the property, you notice it and you address it. Management leans on you to uphold community standards, and that means being thorough on make-readies and punch list items so units are genuinely ready for new residents, not just technically turned.

You'll interact with residents regularly, which means your communication style matters as much as your technical skills. A friendly, calm presence when someone's frustrated about a maintenance issue goes a long way toward resident retention. That's not a soft skill, it's a real part of the job.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Comfortable with computers and basic software for work order management or communication
  • Strong written and spoken English communication skills
  • A detail-oriented approach to property inspections and safety compliance

The Fit and the Context

Berkshire Residential owns and manages its own properties, which means decisions get made closer to the ground than at a typical third-party management shop. Maintenance staff here tend to have a real voice in how things run at the property level. That's worth something if you're someone who takes ownership of your work and wants to be heard when you flag a recurring issue.

The pay range for this role in California runs from $24 to $28 per hour, depending on experience, with benefits that include health coverage, retirement, paid time off, and a meaningful rent discount for employees who live on-site or at a Berkshire community.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this type of role: the ability to prioritize well under pressure. On a busy day you might have a handful of open work orders, a unit turn in progress, and a resident standing at the office with an urgent request. The technicians who thrive here are the ones who can triage calmly, communicate honestly about timelines, and follow through without needing to be chased. That combination of technical competence and personal accountability is what makes the difference between a good hire and a great one.

job.title: Apartment Leasing Sales Consultant - Winthrop West
job.description:
AIR Communities runs a large portfolio of apartment communities across major U.S. markets, and this onsite leasing role at their Tampa property is built for someone who treats leasing as a sales function, not a hospitality one. You're following prospects through a defined process: prompt follow-up, scheduled tours, closing. The expectation is hitting monthly leasing goals consistently, not occasionally.

The commission structure rewards more than just volume. Leasing a higher-rent unit, securing an 18-month or longer lease term, or exceeding your monthly goal each trigger separate commission tiers. That layered structure gives strong performers real upside on individual transactions, not just a flat per-lease bonus.

One benefit worth understanding: AIR offers a 25% rent discount at any of their communities. If you lease onsite, you can eliminate your commute entirely. That's a meaningful compensation component depending on Tampa rental rates at the time you're hired.

The role also includes a potential extended winter break after peak leasing season. This is unpaid time, but benefits and the rent discount stay active. It's an unusual arrangement. If you prefer year-round full-time hours, clarify that expectation before accepting. If you'd use the time well, it's a genuine perk.

What the role requires

  • At least one year of sales or customer service experience with measurable goals, in property management, hospitality, retail, or a similar environment
  • Comfort following a structured sales process and tracking your own performance against it
  • Weekend availability and schedule flexibility based on community hours and season
  • Reliable transportation
  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing laws and regulations

What separates the better candidates here is prior experience in a role where hitting a number was the actual measure of success. Leasing consultants who come from retail or restaurant backgrounds often adapt well because they're used to a traffic-driven environment where every interaction counts. People who haven't worked against a quota before tend to struggle with the pace AIR expects.

Tampa's rental market has seen consistent demand pressure over the past few years, which keeps occupancy goals achievable but also raises resident expectations. You'll be selling into a competitive submarket where prospects have options, so knowing how to communicate the specific value of your community matters more than generic enthusiasm.

job.title: Assistant General Manager
job.description:
It's a Saturday afternoon and the leasing office is humming. The GM is off, you're fielding a tour, a maintenance escalation just hit your phone, and someone at the front desk needs a signature. You handle all three without letting any of them slip. That's the job.

What the Role Actually Involves

Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant General Manager for their Hoboken, NJ community. This is a second-in-command role at a Bozzuto-managed property, which means you carry real operational weight. When the GM is present, you're contributing. When the GM is out, you're running the show.

On the financial side, you'll own rent collection, post receipts, and manage delinquency. You'll track accounts receivable and stay close to the numbers that move occupancy and NOI. On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours personally, work to convert traffic into signed leases, and push toward retention goals through consistent, genuine resident interaction. Bozzuto puts real stock in the resident experience, so every touchpoint matters, from the first tour to a service call follow-up.

You'll also keep an eye on the physical presentation of the community, inside and out. Curb appeal and common area condition reflect directly on the brand, and Bozzuto holds that standard seriously. When team members need guidance and the GM isn't around, you step in to coach and redirect without letting things slide.

Expect to work one to two weekends per month, with two weekdays off in exchange. Weekend coverage is part of the role because that's when prospective residents are actively looking.

What Bozzuto Is Looking for

  • A four-year degree or equivalent experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • At least two years in one of those industries, with real exposure to rent collection, budgets, and accounts receivable
  • Comfort with Yardi or similar property management software
  • Sales ability and written and verbal communication skills that hold up under pressure
  • Active presence on social media platforms like Instagram and Facebook, with the ability to create content that actually engages people
  • A real estate license, or the willingness to obtain one within 90 days of hire where required

The salary range runs from roughly $60,000 to $80,000, with bonus eligibility on top of base. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

One honest note about this role: the AGM position in a busy Hoboken community means you're managing high expectations from residents who are paying premium rents in a competitive market. They notice when things are off. Strong candidates in this role tend to have sharp follow-through on the small stuff, not just the big operational moments. If you treat a maintenance request the same way you treat a lease signing, that consistency is what builds the trust Bozzuto's culture is built around.

job.title: Bilingual Leasing & Sales Consultant-Greater Orlando Area
job.description:
A prospect calls at 4:45 PM on a Friday. They toured two communities earlier that week, they're comparing prices, and they want to talk in Spanish. How you handle the next ten minutes will determine whether that lease gets signed or goes to a competitor down the street.

Cortland, one of the top ten multifamily owners and operators in the country, is hiring a Bilingual Leasing and Sales Consultant for its Greater Orlando portfolio. This is a conversion-focused role. You own your pipeline from first contact to signed lease, and your results show up directly in occupancy and revenue numbers. Cortland operates a vertically integrated platform covering design, construction, and property management in-house, which means the product you're selling is one the company has a direct stake in delivering well.

What the Role Actually Involves

You'll manage a full sales cycle: generating and qualifying leads, conducting tours, following up through a CRM, handling objections, and closing. The expectation is that you hit leasing goals and conversion targets consistently, not occasionally. You'll track your own pipeline health, monitor lead-to-lease ratios, and report on activity metrics. CRM discipline matters here. Cortland tracks performance closely, so records need to stay current and accurate.

Beyond closing leases, you'll represent the community through marketing programs, social media presence, and resident events designed to drive referrals and retention. Cortland positions its properties as premium living experiences, so the service standard is high and the presentation expectations match that.

Bilingual fluency in English and Spanish is central to this role, not a secondary skill. Orlando's renter pool includes a large Spanish-speaking population, and the ability to guide a prospect through the full leasing process in their preferred language directly affects traffic-to-lease conversion.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • At least six months of experience in sales, leasing, or a performance-measured customer-facing role
  • Fluency in English and Spanish
  • Comfort being held to leasing goals and conversion KPIs
  • Experience with or ability to learn CRM systems for lead tracking
  • Organized follow-up habits and strong time management
  • Coachable, with the ability to adjust sales approach based on feedback and market conditions
  • Professional presentation consistent with a Class A brand standard

The candidates who outperform in roles like this tend to treat follow-up as a system, not a task. A tour without a follow-up call within 24 hours is a lead that cools. The consultants who consistently hit conversion targets are usually the ones who work their CRM daily and treat every touchpoint in the pipeline with the same energy as the initial tour.

Cortland was founded in 2005 and is headquartered in Atlanta. The company participates in E-Verify and maintains a drug-free workplace. Cortland is an equal opportunity employer.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Lincoln Property Company is one of the larger private real estate firms operating in the country, and this Assistant Property Manager role in Lawrenceville, GA sits on the commercial side of that platform. We're talking office, retail, and industrial assets, not multifamily. That distinction matters. The day-to-day rhythm here is shaped by lease administration, CAM reconciliations, and tenant relationship management rather than traffic reports and lease-ups.

The role supports a Property Manager across the full operational and financial picture of a property or small portfolio. That means helping produce monthly reporting packages, keeping vendor invoice approvals moving in compliance with the management agreement, and coordinating tenant move-ins and move-outs from documentation through walk-through. You'll also be involved in operating expense reconciliation work alongside the accounting team, which requires a working understanding of how CAM and OpEx are structured and calculated. If those terms are new to you, this probably isn't the right fit yet.

Lease administration is a real part of this job. Setting up leases in the system, tracking changes, generating reports across platforms. It's detailed, repetitive in the best way, and unforgiving when done carelessly. Strong candidates treat lease data like it matters, because downstream it absolutely does.

Lincoln also expects this person to support sourcing and procurement, assist with bid processes, and contribute to emergency response planning. The position is 100% in-office in Lawrenceville with regular property inspections built into the schedule.

What separates candidates who grow quickly in this kind of role from those who stall is usually financial fluency. You don't need to be an accountant, but you do need to be comfortable with percentages, basic variance analysis, and reading a budget package critically. The APM who asks smart questions about a number that looks off earns trust from the PM faster than one who just passes paperwork along.

What Lincoln is Looking for

  • Bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience
  • One to two years in commercial property management or a closely related field
  • Solid Microsoft Office skills, intermediate to advanced
  • Familiarity with AP processing and CMMS platforms is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication, particularly with tenants and vendors
  • Organizational discipline and the ability to meet reporting deadlines consistently
  • Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship

This is a full in-office position with no remote option. Lincoln offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k), and paid time off. Background check required upon offer.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Luma
job.description:
Maintenance Technician roles at apartment communities are straightforward in concept: keep the property running, keep residents happy, and keep the on-call rotation from eating you alive. At a company like MG Properties, which has been acquiring and operating multifamily assets across the Western U.S. for more than three decades, there's real infrastructure behind that work. This isn't a mom-and-pop shop figuring it out as they go.

The Work at Luma

Luma Apartments in San Diego is the property, and the role covers the full scope of day-to-day maintenance operations. You'll work through service requests across all trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repairs, painting. Grounds, offices, and common areas stay clean and presentable on your watch. When a unit turns, you're part of the make-ready process, moving through the punch list to get the apartment rent-ready on schedule. You'll also rotate through on-call coverage for after-hours emergencies. That part's not glamorous, but it's the job.

MG Properties is looking for someone who's already done this at scale. Ideally, you've worked a 200-plus unit property for at least a year and have genuine hands-on experience across the trades, not just one specialty. Reliable transportation is required. The on-call rotation is real, so flexibility matters.

What Separates a Strong Candidate Here

The technicians who do well in roles like this aren't just mechanically capable. They treat service requests like resident interactions, because that's what they are. A fast, clean repair with a decent attitude does more for retention than a concession. At a property that's putting its name on the building, presentation and professionalism show up in every unit entry. If your approach to maintenance is purely transactional, the fit probably isn't there.

Multi-trade competency also matters more than it used to. As San Diego properties push toward smart home integrations and more sophisticated HVAC systems, a technician who can troubleshoot across categories is genuinely more valuable than one with a single deep specialty. That breadth also tends to accelerate the path toward lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles if that's the direction you want to grow.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Pay: $28 to $30 per hour, depending on experience
  • Bonuses: Monthly bonus eligibility plus company profit sharing
  • Time off: 10 days PTO accrued annually, 10 paid holidays, 2 personal days, 40 hours paid sick time
  • Retirement: 401(k) with employer match
  • Health: Medical, dental, vision, life insurance, EAP, FSA, and dependent care spending account
  • Rental discounts available

MG Properties participates in E-Verify, maintains a drug-free workplace, and requires a background check and drug screen prior to hire.

job.title: Leasing and Experience Manager (550 Moreland)
job.description:
The Role and What It Actually Covers

Apartment communities in high-demand markets like Santa Clara live and die by the quality of the team that residents interact with every day. This position sits at the intersection of leasing, resident relations, and team leadership. It's a real operational role with real supervisory weight, and Prometheus structures it differently than most companies would.
