Where other operators call this an assistant manager or assistant business manager, the Leasing and Experience Manager title reflects the actual scope: you're running leasing activities, managing the front-line team, and owning the resident experience at 550 Moreland simultaneously.

Prometheus is the largest privately held apartment owner in the Bay Area, with over 13,000 homes across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle. They've operated since 1965 and are vertically integrated, handling acquisitions, development, value-add renovations, and property management in-house. They're also a Certified B Corporation, which matters to how they operate internally, not just how they market themselves externally.

What You'll Be Doing Day to Day

Resident relations takes up a meaningful chunk of this role. You're the person who fields concerns, follows through on resolutions, and builds the kind of trust that turns a lease renewal from a transaction into a given. You'll also plan community events, which at a well-run community aren't just nice-to-haves. They're part of how residents feel connected to where they live.

On the leasing side, you're already experienced enough that you're helping close deals and coaching others, not learning the basics yourself. You'll contribute to sales and marketing strategy, track market conditions, and work with pricing and concessions. Occupancy reporting, collections, and resident profile management are also in your lane. The supervisory piece means you're setting goals for the leasing team, running training, and tracking performance.

Weekend availability is required. The community sees its highest traffic on Saturdays and Sundays, so your regular days off fall on weekdays.

Qualifications Prometheus is looking for:

  • At least two years of leasing experience
  • High school diploma or GED required; bachelor's degree preferred
  • Background in customer service, sales, or marketing environments
  • Comfort with supervisory responsibilities and team development

Compensation runs $33.25 to $36.25 per hour, with a $200 per-lease incentive, a discretionary semi-annual bonus, and weekend shift premium pay. Medical, dental, and vision are 100% company-paid for eligible employees and dependents. There's also a 401(k) with employer matching, tenure-based housing discounts, tuition reimbursement, and paid volunteer time.

One thing worth noting for candidates thinking about career trajectory: this role is a natural bridge to a full community manager position. The supervisory and operational experience you build here, combined with exposure to pricing strategy and leasing performance in a competitive Silicon Valley market, tends to carry real weight when moving into a general manager seat. Prometheus promotes from within, and the structure of this role is designed with that in mind.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Assistant Community Manager role at Hawthorne at Indy West sits at the intersection of leasing, collections, and team operations. On any given day, you might open the office, work a lead pipeline, conduct tours, and post payments before noon. By afternoon, you're doing ledger reviews, following up on delinquencies, and helping a resident work through a billing question without escalating it into a formal dispute. When the Community Manager is out, the property runs through you.

The leasing side is real work. You're conducting tours, processing applications, handling renewals, and keeping an eye on occupancy. You'll also manage social media content for the community, which means knowing what residents respond to and keeping the feed current without it becoming an afterthought. The financial side carries equal weight: rent collection, check scanning, payment posting, weekly delinquency calls, and coordinating with the CM on any eviction procedures that need to move forward. Ledger accuracy matters here. Billing errors that go unnoticed become problems fast.

Hawthorne operates as one of the top 50 multifamily management companies in the country with a strong Southeast footprint. This is a managed community, and regional leadership will see your numbers. Financial reporting flows up, so accuracy and consistency in your administrative work isn't optional.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of property management experience, with some time in an assistant manager seat preferred
  • Comfort with the full delinquency cycle: calls, notices, ledger documentation, and knowing when to escalate
  • Leasing competency you can actually demonstrate on a tour, not just on paper
  • A valid driver's license
  • CALP accreditation is a plus, not a requirement
  • High school diploma or GED

The schedule runs Monday through Friday with one weekday off each week, plus Saturdays from 10 to 4. Evening and weekend availability may come up for resident events. That's standard for this type of role, and worth knowing upfront.

Compensation and Growth

Hawthorne pays hourly plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. The benefits package includes medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, paid parental leave, and company-paid life insurance. They also run a formal Career Path Program, and the progression from assistant manager to community manager is a real one here, not just language in a job posting. If your goal is to run your own property, this company has the structure to get you there.

The candidates who do well in this seat tend to have one thing in common: they treat the financial side of the role with the same seriousness as the leasing side. Delinquency management and ledger accuracy aren't back-office tasks. They're how a community hits NOI. If that framing clicks for you, this is a good fit.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Hillpointe builds workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and they build it fast. As one of the top-ranked developers on the NMHC Builders and Developers list, they control the full stack in-house: land acquisition, construction, procurement, and asset management. That integration matters for this role because a Maintenance Supervisor here isn't just keeping a stabilized asset running. You may be called in to help bring a brand-new community online, which means your baseline competence needs to be real from day one.

Macon sits in a part of Georgia where workforce housing demand has stayed steady even as larger metros have seen lease-up pressure. The community you'd oversee serves residents who depend on reliable, responsive maintenance. Slow turns and deferred work orders aren't abstract line items here. They affect occupancy and resident retention in a market where word travels.

The core of the job is what you'd expect from a Maintenance Supervisor role: managing the make-ready process on vacant units, handling service requests, running preventative maintenance, and keeping grounds and amenities in shape. You'll also supervise vendors and contractors, inspect their work, and hold them to standard. Inventory management falls to you as well, and you'll be expected to stay within budget on supplies and tools. Safety compliance is non-negotiable. OSHA standards and company protocols apply, and you'll lead regular safety meetings with your team.

The on-call rotation is real and worth knowing going in. Evenings, weekends, and early mornings are part of the schedule. This is standard for any supervisory maintenance role at a residential property, but it's not something to overlook if you're coming from a facilities or commercial background where hours are more structured.

What tends to separate strong candidates in this kind of role is diagnostic instincts. Anyone can complete a work order. The better Maintenance Supervisors catch the issue behind the issue, spot a recurring HVAC problem before it becomes a pattern of complaints, or flag a plumbing concern during a make-ready that would have caused a callback two weeks after move-in. That kind of attention compounds over time into better NOI and fewer emergency costs.

What You'll Need

  • EPA Type I and II or Universal certification for refrigerant handling (required)
  • CPO certification or willingness to obtain it
  • Valid driver's license and all state or local certifications applicable to the role
  • Hands-on proficiency with hand tools, mechanical equipment, and basic office software
  • High school diploma, GED, or equivalent experience
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly, climb ladders, and work in varied outdoor conditions
  • Comfort reading technical manuals, blueprints, and schematics

For someone looking to grow, the Maintenance Supervisor role at a developer-owner like Hillpointe can open a direct path toward regional maintenance or facilities management. Because the company controls construction and asset management internally, there's real exposure to how a property is built and how that affects long-term maintenance planning. That context is harder to get at a third-party management shop.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Patchen Oaks Apartments
job.description:
Patchen Oaks is a 192-unit apartment community in Lexington, and Ackermann Group, a Midwest real estate and property management company with roots going back to 1938, is hiring a full-time Leasing Consultant to work the front lines of occupancy there. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, plus rotating Saturdays from 9 to 4. That rhythm matters: leasing is a people-facing discipline, and the schedule reflects when prospects actually show up.

The core skill this role requires is conversion. You're greeting prospects, building rapport quickly, conducting tours, and turning interest into signed leases at a reasonable close rate. That takes product knowledge, not just enthusiasm. You'll need to understand Patchen Oaks at a granular level: unit mix, building materials, utility setup, year built, and how the property stacks up against competing communities in the Lexington submarket. Local market awareness shapes how you position the community in conversation, and it's something the role expects from day one.

Fair housing compliance runs through every part of the job. Accurate guest cards, complete leasing documentation, and consistent resident interaction records aren't paperwork for its own sake. They're the legal and operational foundation the community manager depends on. Proficiency in property management software, particularly Yardi Voyager and Rent Café, is preferred because those tools are where your work actually lives.

The role also builds skills that carry forward. Handling the full leasing cycle, from first inquiry through move-in, trains the kind of operational attention that makes someone ready for an assistant manager position. You'll also develop resident relations instincts: anticipating issues before they escalate, flagging service requests, and contributing to the community's online reputation through the quality of daily interactions. Those habits compound over time.

What separates strong candidates here is the combination of sales discipline and genuine follow-through. Plenty of people can give a good tour. Fewer stay organized with follow-up, keep guest cards current, and still show up sharp for a Saturday morning shift after a busy week. Ackermann mentions commission potential on new and renewed leases, which means the role rewards consistency, not just peak performance.

What You'll Bring

  • Prior customer service experience (required); leasing or sales background preferred
  • Familiarity with Yardi Voyager, Rent Café, and CRM tools preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to build rapport fast
  • Comfort working independently and within a team across leasing, maintenance, and management
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Availability for the full-time schedule including rotating Saturdays

Ackermann offers health benefits including medical, dental, and vision, a 401k with company match, paid time off (including your birthday), an employee rent discount at any Ackermann community, and career coaching. The commission structure tied to both new leases and renewals gives the compensation real upside for someone who treats the role as a craft.

job.title: Customer Experience Specialist (Leasing/Customer Service)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Customer Experience Specialist role at The Westerly Apartments in Millcreek, UT sits at the intersection of leasing and resident relations. Day to day, you're the first voice prospective residents hear when they call, the first face they see when they walk through the door, and the person making sure vacant units are show-ready before traffic picks up. That means walking the tour path, checking amenity spaces, and running through a mental punch list before you ever greet a prospect.

Beyond leasing, you'll field resident inquiries across phone, email, and text, keep the package room organized, support community events, and help maintain vendor relationships. Cottonwood has been an early adopter of self-guided tours, so you'll work alongside that technology rather than against it, which means your time with prospects is more intentional and less reactive. The schedule is full-time and includes evenings and weekends, which is standard for any leasing role where occupancy actually matters.

What You Bring

  • Genuine comfort talking to people in all contexts: prospects mid-tour, residents with complaints, vendors with questions
  • Strong written communication for email and text follow-up (a slow response kills a lead)
  • Attention to detail when walking units and common areas, you'll catch what others walk past
  • Ability to hold pricing, availability, and floor plan details in your head and communicate them clearly
  • Flexibility with scheduling, including weekend availability
  • A problem-solving instinct when residents raise concerns, because how you handle friction matters more than how you handle easy interactions

Where This Role Takes You

Cottonwood is direct about the growth path: this position is designed to feed into management. That's worth taking seriously. The skills you build here, reading traffic patterns, understanding what drives conversion, managing resident expectations, communicating concessions and pricing clearly, are exactly what a leasing manager or assistant property manager needs on day one. Companies that track quarterly bonus performance also tend to identify their next managers from that same data, so your results here create a visible record.

Leasing roles at well-operated communities also expose you to the full resident lifecycle, from initial inquiry through move-in and renewal, which gives you a complete picture of what drives NOI at the property level. That context is something you can carry into any future role in multifamily, whether you move toward operations, marketing, or management.

Cottonwood offers competitive base pay with a quarterly bonus structure, plus full health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits available within your first month. The 401k and HSA company match, three weeks of PTO in year one, and 10.5 paid holidays round out a benefits package that's above average for an entry-level leasing position.

job.title: Maintenance & Construction Apprentice ($1,000 hiring bonus)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a structured apprenticeship inside a property management company that owns and operates luxury apartment communities across the Carmel, IN area. You'll work alongside experienced tradespeople on renovation and maintenance projects, moving between properties as the work demands. Travel is a constant here, up to 40% of the time, so your "office" changes depending on what's on the schedule.

Day to day, the work spans the full cycle of a unit turn. That means demo and material removal, drywall patching, interior painting, installing LVP flooring and light fixtures, setting cabinets, and closing out the punch list details that separate a finished luxury unit from one that just looks finished. You'll also rotate through exterior work: power washing, seasonal repairs, landscaping, and building upkeep. Physical demands are real. You'll lift 75-plus pounds, work from ladders, and stay outdoors through whatever the Indiana weather brings.

BAM provides the tools and the training. The $1,000 hiring bonus and the $19 to $21 hourly starting pay reflect that this is a compensated apprenticeship, not an unpaid credential program. You build trade skills while earning, without the debt load that formal trade school typically carries.

What You Bring

  • A valid driver's license and reliable transportation for local property travel
  • Comfort working at heights and on ladders (safety training is provided, but comfort with heights is required on day one)
  • Basic hand tool familiarity: tape measure, hammer, screwdriver
  • Zero to two years of experience in construction, landscaping, or general labor (preferred, not required)
  • High school diploma or GED (preferred)
  • Your own tools are a plus, but the company will supply what you need

The right attitude carries more weight here than a resume. Reliability, attention to detail on finish work, and the ability to take direction from experienced tradespeople will determine how quickly you advance.

Skills This Role Builds and Where They Lead

Most people who start as maintenance apprentices in multifamily either move into a lead maintenance technician role or specialize in a specific trade area like HVAC, plumbing, or electrical. The punch list and make-ready experience you accumulate here is directly transferable to any Class A or B property, and companies pay well for technicians who can manage a full unit turn with minimal supervision. The renovation side of this role adds capex project exposure that most standard maintenance positions don't offer early on, which makes your skill set broader and more marketable faster.

The compensation package includes a significant rent discount at one of BAM's luxury communities plus free utilities, 15.5 paid holidays from the start, 88 hours of PTO at 90 days, and 120 additional PTO hours at the one-year mark. Low-cost medical, dental, vision, disability, and pet insurance round out the benefits.

job.title: Cleaner - Full-Time
job.description:
Student housing communities run on turn cycles, occupancy pressure, and the kind of daily visible cleanliness that directly affects leasing traffic and resident retention. The person keeping hallways, common areas, and grounds in shape isn't background staff. They're the first thing a prospective resident notices on a tour.

Redstone Residential operates over 38,000 beds across 20 states, making them one of the larger third-party student housing operators in the country. This full-time Cleaner role is based at their Eugene, Oregon community and pays $23.00 per hour.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of this job is keeping a student housing community clean and presentable, indoors and out. That means regular cleaning of hallways, common areas, the clubhouse, office, model unit, and parking garages. It means grounds work: picking up trash and debris, clearing animal waste, watering landscaping, and maintaining curb appeal day to day. In winter, keeping walkways clear of snow and ice is part of the job.

One piece that's specific to student housing: you'll conduct scheduled cleaning checks inside residents' apartments to confirm units are being maintained to the property's standards. That's a regular duty here, and it requires someone who can handle that interaction with residents professionally and without making it adversarial. Student housing populations cycle quickly and aren't always tidy. That's just the reality of the asset class.

You'll also assist with basic repairs and general maintenance tasks as needed. This isn't a deep technical role, but being willing to help where the team needs it matters.

Who Fits This Role

  • Prior janitorial or cleaning experience, ideally in a residential or commercial property setting
  • Comfortable working independently and managing a daily task list without close supervision
  • Physically able to lift 50+ pounds and stand for four to six hour shifts
  • A genuinely friendly, approachable demeanor, especially when conducting apartment checks

The candidate who does well here tends to take ownership of their section of the property rather than waiting to be directed. In student housing, conditions can change fast between Monday morning and Friday afternoon. Staying ahead of that requires a certain kind of self-motivation.

Benefits include health, vision, and dental insurance, 15 days of PTO, 10 paid holidays, paid parental leave, three paid service days, a 401(k) with up to 6% match, short-term disability, and a continued education program.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
It's 9 PM on a Tuesday and a resident's heat is out. That call comes to you. That's the job, honestly, and knowing that upfront is more useful than a list of perks.

Fairstead is a vertically integrated affordable housing owner and operator with more than 30,000 units across 28 states. They develop, build, and manage their own properties, which means maintenance staff work within a single unified system rather than bouncing between ownership and a third-party management company. This Euclid, Ohio position carries a $2,000 signing bonus and sits at the core of keeping a residential property functional and safe for the people who live there.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're handling make-ready turns on vacated units, running preventative maintenance rounds, checking safety systems monthly, and working through resident work orders as they come in. Electrical diagnostics, HVAC checks, appliance repairs, and general building upkeep are all part of the rotation. You'll maintain a working inventory of supplies and tools, and you'll help enforce maintenance standards that protect the property's physical assets from misuse or premature wear. On-call rotation is part of the position, which means after-hours emergency calls are real and expected. The paperwork and communication side matters too. You'll need to document work clearly and coordinate effectively with property staff.

Fairstead operates with a tech-forward approach for an affordable housing company, including data-driven systems and digital tools. That doesn't eliminate the physical demands of the role, but it does mean you'll likely use software to log and track work orders rather than relying on paper-based processes.

What You Bring

  • Prior experience as a maintenance or service technician in a residential or commercial setting
  • Working knowledge of electrical systems sufficient to diagnose issues and complete minor repairs
  • General mechanical aptitude across plumbing, HVAC, appliances, and building systems
  • HVAC certification, CMRP, or equivalent credential (preferred, not required)
  • Ability to lift up to 70 pounds unassisted and stand for extended periods
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • Attention to detail, especially on punch list items and unit inspections

The candidates who do well in roles like this one tend to be self-starters who can triage a work order list without constant direction. In affordable housing specifically, the resident population often depends on quick, reliable service in ways that are more immediate than in market-rate communities. That's not pressure meant to discourage anyone. It's just context for why responsiveness and follow-through matter here more than in some other settings.

Fairstead offers medical coverage through Meritain Health with a generous employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match, 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, 12 or more paid holidays, and a flexible spending account among other benefits.

job.title: Activities Director - Orchard Mesa
job.description:
Multifamily operators increasingly recognize that amenities alone don't retain residents. Programming does. The Activities Director role exists because a well-run events calendar directly supports occupancy: residents who feel connected to their community renew leases, refer friends, and generate the kind of organic reputation that no ad spend can replicate. CloudTen Residential, a Nevada-based company with a portfolio spanning hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning across the West, is hiring for this position at Orchard Mesa in Mesa, AZ.

What This Role Actually Involves

Working under the Community Manager, you'll own the full activities program: building a monthly calendar, writing and distributing a resident newsletter, coordinating vendors and entertainers, managing the activities budget, and supervising an Activities Assistant through event setup, execution, and breakdown. You'll design promotional materials and push programming through social media and digital communication channels. Beyond the creative side, there's real operational accountability here. You'll track income, control expenses, and handle petty cash in line with company accounting policies. Safety compliance and Fair Housing adherence are non-negotiable parts of the job, not afterthoughts.

You'll also work alongside the leasing and maintenance teams on community-wide initiatives, which means your events calendar has to fit into the broader operational rhythm of the property. When a lease-up push is underway or a capital project is disrupting amenity spaces, you adapt. That cross-functional coordination is where a lot of activities directors either grow or stall.

Pay runs $26.00 to $29.00 per hour depending on experience. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, an FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • A high school diploma at minimum; an associate or bachelor's degree in recreation, hospitality, or communications is preferred
  • At least two years of event or activities planning, ideally in residential or healthcare settings
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office, property management software, and basic reporting tools
  • The ability to engage genuinely with a diverse resident population and build inclusive programming
  • Strong organizational instincts and the discipline to manage multiple projects without losing detail on any single one

The candidates who tend to stand out in this role are the ones who treat resident feedback as data. Gathering post-event input, tracking participation trends, and adjusting the calendar based on what actually draws people out (versus what looks good on paper) separates a strong activities director from someone who just executes a template. If you've worked in senior living or student housing, those instincts transfer directly here.

From a career trajectory standpoint, this role builds a skill set that compounds well. Resident retention strategy, budget management, vendor relationships, cross-team collaboration, and digital communication are all transferable to community management, regional support roles, or even marketing-focused positions within a multifamily platform. CloudTen's expanding portfolio means internal movement is a realistic path for people who perform.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Multi-site - Elan Luxo II, Elan Beach Lofts, Elan Bay Lofts, Elan Pacific Lofts, Elan Coronado Bella Mer
job.city: Elan - Baylofts ; Elan - Beachlofts ; Elan - Bella Mer Coronado ; Elan - Luxo Ii ; Elan - Pacific Lofts
job.description:
Sunrise Management runs five Elan-branded communities across San Diego, and this role sits at the center of all of them. Elan Luxo II, Beach Lofts, Bay Lofts, Pacific Lofts, and Coronado Bella Mer each have their own rhythm, their own residents, and their own maintenance needs. Your job is to hold it all together.

This is a multi-site supervisor position, which means your mornings aren't predictable. One day you're coordinating turns at Bay Lofts, the next you're troubleshooting an HVAC issue at Bella Mer while your tech handles service requests across town. A valid driver's license is required, and you'll genuinely use it. The role pays $27 to $33 per hour depending on experience.

The core of the work is what you'd expect from any maintenance supervisor: make-ready units within three to five days of move-out, preventive maintenance logs, pool and spa upkeep, appliance and HVAC repairs, curb appeal, common area cleanliness, and 24-hour service request completion. You'll also handle on-call emergency coverage when it comes up, which it will. That's the honest reality of this kind of role.

What's different here is the supervisory load across multiple sites. You're not just a skilled tech who happens to carry a radio. You're the person who sets work schedules, runs monthly safety meetings, keeps MSDS records current, trains your team on PPE protocols, and stays in close communication with multiple property managers. You'll also weigh in on hiring and performance reviews for the maintenance staff under you, and you'll surface capital improvement recommendations when you see them.

Sunrise describes their culture around resident hospitality, and that filters into maintenance too. Service requests handled within 24 hours, residents kept in the loop when parts need to be ordered, consistent community inspections. The expectation is that residents feel the attention, not just the repair.

Multi-site supervisors who do this well tend to develop a strong operational picture that translates directly into Maintenance Director roles or regional facilities positions. The exposure to multiple property types, management relationships, and vendor negotiations at this scale is hard to replicate in a single-site role.

What you'll bring

  • At least one year of hands-on property maintenance experience
  • Prior supervisory experience (required)
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and pool systems
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing laws and safety compliance requirements
  • Strong communication habits with both residents and management
  • Valid driver's license in good standing
  • Organized enough to track inventory, time sheets, and maintenance logs across sites

If you're the kind of person who notices the burned-out light before anyone reports it and already has a replacement in the truck, you'll fit the pace here.

job.title: Service Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a field-based maintenance role covering scattered-site properties across the Lehigh Valley. You'll drive between single-family homes, commercial assets, and vacation properties owned or managed by Dream Live Prosper Communities, handling work orders across the full range of trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, painting, and general upkeep.

The standard is clear: resolve assigned service requests within 48 hours with no callbacks. You'll manage your own work order queue in property management software, keep the queue moving, and execute make-readies on vacated homes so they're rent-ready on schedule. Grounds and common area upkeep are part of the job too, not an afterthought.

On-call rotation is real here. You'll respond to after-hours emergencies as part of the team's shared rotation. If that kind of flexibility doesn't fit your life right now, this role isn't the right fit.

You'll need a reliable vehicle with room for tools and supplies. The company provides the properties; you bring the transportation and your own basic hand tools.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on experience across basic plumbing, electrical, HVAC, painting, and general repairs
  • Ability to troubleshoot and close out repairs independently, without waiting to be directed
  • Comfort with mobile work order systems and property management software
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 lbs and work outdoors in all weather
  • Valid driver's license, clean driving record, and a vehicle capable of hauling tools and equipment
  • CPO certification is a plus, not a requirement
  • Availability for on-call rotation, including weekends

Context Worth Knowing

Scattered-site maintenance work runs differently than a traditional apartment community. There's no leasing office to anchor your day. You're planning your own route, managing your own time, and keeping several property types in good shape simultaneously. Strong candidates in this kind of role tend to be the ones who treat their work order queue like a personal commitment, not a list someone else is tracking. The 48-hour, no-callback standard exists because resident satisfaction on scattered sites depends almost entirely on the technician, since there's no front desk or community team to absorb the friction when something goes wrong.

Pay starts at $20 to $25 per hour depending on experience and certifications. Benefits include health, dental, vision, and life insurance, 401(k) matching, and PTO.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Student housing leasing management operates on a different calendar than conventional multifamily. You're selling beds a year out, managing a lease-up cycle tied to academic schedules, and working with a resident demographic that expects a social experience alongside a place to sleep. PeakMade Real Estate specializes in exactly this space, managing off-campus student communities across the country from their Atlanta headquarters. This Leasing Manager role sits onsite in Ithaca, New York, which puts you in a college market with real seasonal intensity.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a dual-track position: half leasing leadership, half marketing execution. You'll hire, train, and manage a leasing staff while also owning the property's social media presence, digital content, and community programming. That combination is specific to student housing. Conventional multifamily rarely asks a leasing manager to shoot and edit content in Canva, manage online reputation across platforms like Reputation.com and JTurner, and still hit closing ratios. Here, that's the full job description.

On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, sign leases (beds and apartments), support move-in and move-out events, and keep prospect traffic data current. Renewal programming falls under your scope as well, including lease renewal events and resident retention campaigns. On the marketing side, you'll develop and execute the annual marketing plan within budget, using social platforms, creative tools, and campus-specific outreach to drive traffic and conversions.

What PeakMade Is Looking For

  • 2 or more years of leasing experience specifically in off-campus student housing
  • Prior leadership experience, formal or informal
  • Hands-on comfort with Instagram, Facebook, Canva, Lightroom, VSCO, and property management software
  • Strong communication skills across in-person, phone, and online leasing channels
  • Flexibility for some evenings and weekends, especially during peak leasing season
  • High school diploma or equivalent required

The pay range runs $52,000 to $57,000 annually, with monthly, quarterly, and annual commission layered on top. PeakMade also offers a housing discount, 401(k) match, 15 days of PTO plus two additional wellbeing days, up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave, and a mentorship program.

A Note on What Separates Strong Candidates

In student housing, the leasing cycle is unforgiving. Pre-leasing for the following academic year typically starts in the fall, which means you're selling apartments to people who won't move in for another nine to twelve months. Candidates who've managed that timeline, kept traffic moving in the off-peak months, and still hit occupancy targets before the summer rush tend to do well in roles like this. If your background is conventional multifamily without student housing exposure, the calendar alone will be an adjustment. Two-plus years in the student space is a real requirement here, not a preference dressed up as one.

job.title: Regional Property Manager Manufactured Housing Communities
job.description:
Manufactured housing communities operate differently from conventional apartments, and not every regional manager makes that transition cleanly. The resident base tends to be longer-term, the maintenance issues are more varied (you're dealing with homes, not just units), and the communities often span multiple small markets rather than clustering in one metro. Investment Property Group owns and operates a portfolio that spans manufactured home, multifamily, and RV communities across the country. This Oregon regional role sits squarely in the manufactured housing side of that portfolio.

The Portfolio and the Work

This position covers communities spread across the Willamette Valley and surrounding areas: Springfield, Eugene, Albany, Aumsville, Monmouth, Salem. The geography matters. You're not commuting between properties that are twenty minutes apart. Expect to be on the road three or more days per week, and plan your week accordingly. A company car is provided, which helps, but this is genuinely a travel-heavy role. If you prefer to manage from a desk, this isn't the right fit.

The portfolio sits at 1,000-plus units across multiple sites. Your direct reports are property managers and on-site teams at each location. Your job is to keep them focused, equipped, and accountable. That means regular site visits, budget reviews, hiring decisions, and stepping in when a community has a performance problem that the on-site team can't resolve independently. You'll report out to senior leadership with analysis and action plans, not just status updates.

On the financial side, you'll own the monthly review process: pulling apart the numbers, flagging anomalies, and building corrective plans when a property is drifting off target. You'll also manage budgets and work with the compliance and maintenance teams to keep operations consistent across the region.

What This Role Actually Requires

  • At least three years of senior-level multi-site management experience, area manager or regional level
  • Multi-site portfolio experience at 1,000 or more units
  • Comfort with Yardi, Rent Cafe, Blue Moon, and related platforms
  • Strong grasp of local housing market conditions across the Oregon markets listed
  • Valid driver's license and willingness to travel 30 to 70 percent of the time within the state
  • Must be Oregon-based or willing to relocate

The compensation is $120,000 to $130,000 base, with a 20 percent annual discretionary bonus and a company vehicle. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, life insurance, HSA, employee assistance program, and a 401k with company match.

One honest note: manufactured housing communities carry a specific resident relations dynamic. Residents are often long-term, sometimes multi-generational, and disputes over community rules or maintenance responsibilities can run deep. The candidates who do well in this kind of regional role aren't just financially sharp. They know how to de-escalate, they take community standards seriously, and they treat residents with consistency regardless of the situation. That combination, financial fluency plus people judgment, is what separates a strong regional manager from one who burns out or loses the trust of their on-site teams.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager - Mountain Gate & Trails
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Mountain Gate and Trails is an AIR Communities property in Las Vegas, and this role puts you in charge of keeping it running. You'll lead a maintenance team, own the full scope of service operations, and report capital and maintenance needs up the chain. That means vendor management, preventive maintenance scheduling, apartment turns, and resident service requests all land on your desk. AIR runs a tech-forward maintenance operation, so you'll work with digital tools that are meant to increase the volume of work your team can handle each day without sacrificing quality.

Budget accountability is real here. You're expected to manage spend efficiently while holding quality steady, which is the perpetual tension of this job. You'll also carry compliance responsibility across AIR's operating procedures and Environmental Health and Safety requirements. Las Vegas is a market that doesn't slow down seasonally the way other regions do, so on-call rotations and flexible scheduling are part of the deal year-round.

Compensation runs $75,000 to $77,000 base, with a 15% target bonus opportunity plus quarterly customer satisfaction bonuses of up to $250 per month for managers who consistently deliver strong resident experiences. An on-site apartment discount is also available.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of hands-on technical maintenance and facilities experience in property management
  • One to three years leading a team in a customer service and asset maintenance environment
  • Mechanical aptitude and comfort with physical work, including moving heavy equipment
  • Ability to work evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts as needed
  • Organized, solution-focused, and detail-oriented without needing to be told twice
  • Reliable transportation

A Word on What Separates Strong Candidates

We've seen maintenance managers who are excellent technicians but struggle to develop their team, and others who are great with people but let the preventive maintenance schedule slip until small problems become capex surprises. The candidates who do well in roles like this one hold both. They run tight punch lists, stay ahead of turns, and still make time to train the person behind them. AIR invests in certifications and tuition reimbursement up to 100% for job-related credentials, which tells you something about how they view developing talent from within. If you've been a strong lead tech looking for your first or second shot at a supervisor title, this structure supports that move.

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, HSA/FSA options, short and long-term disability paid by the company, 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, up to 16 weeks paid parental leave, and 14 paid holidays plus vacation and sick time.

job.title: Bilingual Resident Services Specialist - Sandy Springs, GA
job.description:
Cortland runs one of the larger centralized contact center operations in multifamily, and this role sits at the core of it. Rather than working on-site at a single property, you'd be handling resident interactions across Cortland's portfolio from a shared services environment, which means high volume, varied issues, and a real premium on consistency and speed.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Incoming calls, emails, and chat messages from residents form the bulk of the day. You're fielding questions, resolving concerns, de-escalating tense situations, and keeping multiple conversations moving at once. The bilingual requirement (English and Spanish) reflects the demographics of Cortland's resident base across markets, and fluency in both languages is a genuine operational need here, not a nice-to-have. Fair Housing compliance runs through every interaction, and you'll be expected to apply it without prompting.

The tech stack leans on RealPage, OneSite, and Funnel alongside CRM tools, so prior exposure to any of these platforms will shorten your ramp time considerably. Candidates who've worked in multifamily contact centers or leasing offices know how quickly system navigation becomes second nature; those coming purely from other service industries should expect a learning curve on the property management side.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • At least two years of customer service experience, preferably in a high-volume contact center or multifamily setting
  • Full bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish
  • Familiarity with RealPage, OneSite, Funnel, or comparable property management platforms
  • Comfort reviewing applications, verifying documentation, and maintaining compliance accuracy under pressure
  • High school diploma or equivalent; demonstrated discretion with confidential resident information
  • Flexibility for weekend and extended-hour availability as needed

Where This Role Fits

Cortland is headquartered in Atlanta and has a significant presence across the Sun Belt, including several communities in the Sandy Springs and Perimeter Center corridor. Sandy Springs has seen steady multifamily demand driven by proximity to major employers along GA-400 and the I-285 interchange, which keeps occupancy competitive and resident expectations high. A centralized contact center serving those communities handles a real cross-section of resident needs.

For someone looking to grow in multifamily operations, contact center experience at a vertically integrated operator like Cortland carries weight. You're exposed to portfolio-wide processes, technology systems, and resident lifecycle management in a way that a single-property leasing role rarely offers. That breadth translates well into future roles in resident experience, operations coordination, or regional support.

job.title: Assistant Manager - Monte Viejo
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits between leasing and operations. You'll spend a meaningful chunk of your day on the financial side: collecting rent, making sure deposits hit before bank close, tracking delinquency, and keeping resident ledgers accurate inside RealPage/Onesite. When a resident disputes a charge or a move-out balance needs to be settled, that falls to you.

You'll also step into the leasing rotation when traffic picks up or the team needs coverage. That means showing units, following up on prospects, and inspecting make-readies before a new resident gets the keys. If something's off on the punch list, you catch it before move-in, not after.

When the Property Manager is out, you run the property. That's not an occasional thing to prepare for. It's part of the job, and Olympus expects you to handle it without hand-holding.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with some flexibility required for resident events and the first weekend of each month.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years of assistant manager experience, preferably at a larger apartment community
  • Hands-on experience with RealPage, Onesite, or Knock (strongly preferred)
  • Comfort handling collections, deposits, and financial recordkeeping accurately and on deadline
  • Ability to manage resident concerns directly, including complaints, without escalating everything upstream
  • Awareness of the local submarket: new construction, hiring trends, competing properties, anything that could affect occupancy or income
  • A detail-oriented work style that holds up under a full daily workload

The Role in Context

Monte Viejo is an Olympus Property community in Phoenix. Olympus has earned National Apartment Association Top Employer recognition three years running, and their culture emphasis is genuine rather than decorative. The pay range starts at $25 to $27 per hour depending on experience, and the position includes monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses on top of base pay. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer match, tuition reimbursement, and an apartment rental allowance.

For candidates who want a clear growth path: assistant managers who consistently handle financial operations and step into the property manager role during absences are typically first in line when a Business Manager position opens. If running your own property is the goal, this is the direct route there within Olympus's structure.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning at Bexley Westshore and you're already juggling three things at once: a prospect waiting for a tour, a resident at the counter asking about her renewal, and a maintenance follow-up that needs a callback before noon. That's a normal day in this role, and the right person finds that kind of pace energizing rather than draining.

The Role at Bexley Westshore

Weinstein Properties has been family-owned and operated for more than 70 years, with a portfolio of over 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. Bexley Westshore in Cumming, GA is one of those communities, and this Assistant Property Manager position sits at the center of its daily operations.

The work covers the full resident lifecycle. On the leasing side, you'll respond to internet leads, take calls, schedule and conduct tours, process applications, prepare lease paperwork, and collect deposits. Once a resident moves in, your involvement continues through renewals, transfers, pet addendums, early terminations, and move-outs, including security deposit dispositions. You'll post rent payments and follow up on outstanding balances. You'll also coordinate with the maintenance team, walking units to confirm make-ready quality and following up with residents on open work orders. Resident events are part of the job too, from planning through execution.

Leadership experience is required here. Weinstein isn't looking for someone to shadow the Property Manager indefinitely. You'll help train team members, contribute to hitting property goals, and step into a genuine support role at the management level. Prior property management experience is a plus, but candidates from hospitality, sales, or customer-facing management roles are considered seriously if the leadership foundation is there. Weinstein provides structured training and coaching to fill in the property management specifics.

The schedule runs weekdays 9 to 6, Saturdays 9 to 5 on a team rotation, with Sundays closed. Starting pay is $23 per hour, increasing with experience, plus quarterly bonuses. Benefits include health, dental and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid holidays, birthday time off, vacation and sick time, a rent discount, and an Employee Assistance Program.

What Strong Candidates Bring

Cumming sits in Forsyth County, one of the fastest-growing counties in Georgia, which means leasing traffic tends to stay active and resident turnover creates real operational pressure. The candidates who perform well here aren't just friendly. They manage competing priorities without dropping details, communicate clearly when conversations get difficult, and take ownership of tasks without waiting to be asked twice.

  • Demonstrated leadership or management experience in a customer-facing environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to handle sensitive resident conversations professionally
  • Comfort with leasing activity: tours, applications, and closing
  • Attention to detail when walking units, reviewing lease files, or processing account transactions
  • Willingness to occasionally work outside standard hours for resident events or weather-related situations

For someone earlier in their property management career, this role builds a skill set that transfers directly into a Property Manager position. Weinstein promotes from within, and many of their current leaders started in leasing or assistant roles on-site.

job.title: Part-Time Leasing Consultant - Stone Cliff
job.description:
Part-time leasing roles at well-established apartment operators tend to attract candidates who want real property management experience without a full-time commitment. At MG Properties, a company with three decades of ownership and management across the Western U.S., this position at Stone Cliff Apartments in Aurora carries more substance than a typical part-time leasing gig.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your day centers on converting traffic into signed leases. That means greeting prospects, walking units, qualifying applicants, and preparing leases for signing. You'll also coordinate with maintenance to make sure new residents move in without hiccups, which requires staying on top of the make-ready schedule and communicating clearly across teams. Resident interaction doesn't stop at move-in: you'll field maintenance concerns, handle complaints professionally, and follow up on rent payment as needed. File accuracy matters here too. Rental data entry and lease file organization are part of the role, and the expectation is that paperwork stays current and complete.

What MG Properties Is Looking For

  • At least one year of property management experience (preferred, not required)
  • Demonstrated sales ability and customer service skills
  • Professional etiquette in both resident and team interactions
  • Comfort working in a team environment
  • Attention to detail in data entry and lease documentation

The pay range is $22 to $23 per hour depending on experience, with paid time off and 48 hours of paid sick time included. Note that this position is anticipated to be filled in August 2026, so timing matters if you're planning ahead.

Why This Role Is Worth Considering

Aurora's apartment market sits in an interesting spot. The submarket has seen significant new supply in recent years, which means leasing teams at established communities compete on service quality and relationship-building, not just price. Consultants who can read a prospect's hesitation and respond with genuine knowledge about the community tend to outperform those who rely on a rehearsed pitch. If you're building a career in property management, the leasing consultant seat is where you develop the occupancy instincts and resident communication skills that carry over into assistant manager and eventually property manager roles. MG Properties promotes from within, so the part-time entry point here has a real career path attached to it.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Puts to Work Every Day

The Assistant Community Manager position at The Village at Colbert Park runs on a specific combination of skills: financial discipline, people attunement, and operational follow-through. You'll carry real accountability across resident accounts, delinquency management, and utility billing, while simultaneously staying dialed into how the team is performing and how residents feel about living there. Those two tracks, the numbers and the human side, don't operate separately in this role. They inform each other constantly.

Student housing adds its own layer. Lease cycles compress around academic calendars, which means turn season at a collegiate community is genuinely high-volume and physically demanding. Scion uses Turnable to manage the electronic turn board, and you'll be in that system regularly to track progress and hold vendors and team members to move-in deadlines. When crunch time hits, this role gets hands-on. Moving furniture, helping with punch list items, sorting high volumes of resident trash during turn: that's part of the job description, and it matters that you're willing to do it.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A fair amount of your week involves resident-facing work: managing escalated concerns, processing damage disputes, responding to Google and Yelp reviews, and making sure move-ins run cleanly. You'll also run weekly market surveys and collaborate with the Centralized Sales Team on occupancy strategy, which means you're contributing to both the customer experience and the revenue picture.

On the administrative side, you'll assist with month-end reporting, reconcile accounts receivable, and keep delinquency below 2% by month end. The General Manager leans on you as a true second-in-command, so when they're out, you're running the operation. That expectation is built into the role from day one.

Staff development is part of this too. You'll help recruit, onboard, and coach team members, including managing the on-call schedule. Morale in student housing can fluctuate with the academic calendar, and your involvement in building a stable, motivated team directly affects how smoothly everything else runs.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart Here

Experience with Entrata is genuinely useful, not just a checkbox. The tech stack at Scion is broader than most properties: Greenhouse, Lattice, Turnable, Qualtrics, and ClickUp are all in play. Candidates who adapt quickly to new platforms and don't need hand-holding on systems will have an easier time stepping into full productivity.

The other differentiator is composure during competing demands. Student housing communities field a high volume of resident interactions, and the population skews young, often navigating their first independent living experience. The candidates who thrive here tend to be patient communicators who can hold a firm policy line without being dismissive. That balance shows up in resident satisfaction scores and, eventually, in lease renewal rates.

  • 1+ years of experience in property management or residential living communities
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Customer-focused approach with solid prioritization habits
  • Proficiency in property management systems; Entrata experience preferred
  • Willingness to work non-traditional hours, including on-call shifts during peak periods
  • Must be eligible to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, 401k matching, paid parental leave, paid time off, a floating holiday, discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. This is an exempt, salaried position.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Community managers sit at the center of everything: financial performance, team output, resident experience, and ownership reporting. At a property this size, that means the role touches every department and every problem. Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the top 50 multifamily operators in the country and a Southeast-rooted company, is filling that seat at Hawthorne at Weaverville in Asheville, NC.

What This Role Actually Covers

You run the property. That means owning the budget, tracking delinquency, managing deposit accounting, and producing financial reporting that holds up to ownership scrutiny. You'll work inside Yardi and Knock daily, so comfort with both matters. On the leasing side, you're not just reviewing your team's numbers. You're conducting tours, responding to leads, and keeping occupancy and renewal rates on target through active participation, not just oversight.

Team leadership is a real part of the job. You hire, train, and coach office and maintenance staff. You run weekly team meetings and stay close enough to daily operations to catch performance issues before they compound. Vendor relationships, work order flow, and preventative maintenance coordination fall under your watch too.

Resident escalations land on your desk. You handle them directly, with professionalism. You also manage the community's online reputation and plan resident events. The leasing office runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays, 10 to 4. One weekday off per week keeps the schedule at 40 hours, though evening and weekend availability may come up for events or community needs.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least two years of property management experience, including time as a leasing consultant and assistant community manager
  • Six months of community manager experience in multifamily, strongly preferred
  • Yardi, Knock, and Microsoft Office experience, strongly preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CAM, CAPS, real estate license, or property management license preferred

Compensation includes a base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with match, paid time off, paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, and telehealth access. Hawthorne also runs a formal career path program with a clear track toward regional management for strong performers.

The candidates who stand out in this role combine financial literacy with genuine team development instincts. Reading a T-12 and making a budget call is one skill set. Keeping a leasing team motivated through a slow traffic month is another. The managers who advance at companies like Hawthorne tend to be strong at both, not just one.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Paragon Properties runs two communities in Southfield simultaneously under this role, which means the day-to-day operational picture is wider than a typical single-site assistant position. You're tracking leasing activity, resident satisfaction, and administrative accuracy across two addresses at once.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of this role sits at the intersection of leasing and operations. You're fielding prospect calls and walk-ins, converting traffic into signed leases, and maintaining the sales standards Paragon sets for both phone and in-person performance. At the same time, you're processing applications, move-in paperwork, and renewals for manager review, so accuracy matters as much as personality. Vacant unit inspections, model readiness, and punch list awareness are part of keeping the communities presentable and competitive.

Resident retention gets real attention here too. Move-in follow-ups and work order check-ins are built into the job, not left to chance. You'll also contribute to outreach efforts, local employer marketing, and resident events, which means some of your best leasing work happens away from the leasing office.

What Paragon Is Looking For

  • At least one year in a customer service or sales role, with six or more months of on-site leasing experience preferred
  • High school diploma or equivalent; some college preferred
  • Proficiency in MS Office, with Yardi experience a plus
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations
  • Strong attention to detail, especially on lease paperwork and compliance
  • Industry designations (CAM, NALP, etc.) are a plus

The compensation runs up to $28.00 per hour depending on experience and property size, with quarterly bonus potential on top of the base. The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision with a short waiting period, company-paid life and disability insurance, a 401(k) with employer contribution, paid time off, paid holidays, and a rent discount.

Where This Role Can Take You

Assistant Community Manager is the most direct path to a Community Manager seat. Candidates who build strong T-3 and T-12 familiarity here, who understand how delinquency trends and occupancy fluctuations affect NOI, and who can eventually own a budget conversation will move up faster than those who treat the role as purely leasing. Paragon has a stated training and advancement program, so the infrastructure for that progression exists. The dual-community exposure accelerates it.

Pre-employment background check, drug screening, and physical are required. Paragon Properties is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
It's 7 a.m. on a Monday and the punch list from the weekend on-call shift is already waiting: a reported HVAC issue in Building C, two work orders from Saturday, and a vacant unit that needs to be turned before the new resident moves in Friday. That's a typical morning for a Maintenance Technician at Hillpointe's Bethlehem, GA community.

The Work

Hillpointe builds and operates market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and this role sits at the center of keeping a property performing. You'll handle the full range of day-to-day maintenance: completing resident work orders, running preventive maintenance tasks, conducting inspections, and doing whatever it takes to keep buildings, amenities, and common areas clean, safe, and functional. Make-readies are a core part of the job. When a unit turns, you're prepping it to meet move-in standards on schedule, because vacancy days cost money and a slow turn shows up in NOI.

You'll also manage inventory, coordinate with vendors and contractors, and keep documentation current. Grounds upkeep is part of the rotation, and you'll participate in safety meetings and follow OSHA protocols. A rotating on-call schedule means some evenings, early mornings, and weekends are part of the deal.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on mechanical and troubleshooting ability across building systems, including HVAC, plumbing, and electrical
  • Experience completing work orders and pre-move-out inspections with accuracy and follow-through
  • EPA Type I and II or Universal certification for refrigerant recycling, or willingness to obtain it
  • Valid driver's license (required for golf cart operation on property)
  • Comfort reading technical manuals, blueprints, or schematics
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly, climb ladders, and work in outdoor or confined conditions across varying temperatures
  • High school diploma or GED, with relevant hands-on experience or training

Strong candidates in this type of role tend to be self-starters who close out work orders the same day they open them and flag a small issue before it becomes a capital repair. That instinct, catching a failing HVAC component during a routine PM rather than after a resident complaint, is what separates a technician who just keeps up from one who actually protects the asset. At a vertically integrated developer like Hillpointe, that attention to the physical condition of the property directly ties back to asset performance.

For technicians looking to grow, this role builds a track record that leads naturally toward Lead Technician or Maintenance Supervisor positions, particularly at a company that develops and manages its own portfolio at scale.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor, 300-500 Units - Houston, TX
job.description:
Maintenance supervisors at mid-size communities often get pulled between two competing demands: keeping daily service requests moving and building a team that can handle the work without constant oversight. At a 300 to 500 unit property, that tension is real. The portfolio is large enough that deferred work compounds fast, but small enough that the supervisor is still hands-on, not just managing from a clipboard.

Berkshire Residential Investments owns and manages its own assets, which means the maintenance team here reports into an ownership structure rather than a third-party fee management chain. That distinction matters. Decisions about capex, long-range planning, and community standards don't get filtered through a separate owner relationship. The people setting the budget are the same people setting expectations for how the property looks and performs.

What the Role Covers

This position leads the service team at a Houston community in The Core submarket, with unit count in the 300 to 500 range. Day-to-day, the supervisor is responsible for scheduling the team efficiently, monitoring work quality and completion rates, and making sure make-ready turns stay on track. Tour routes and models need to be in showcase condition, which means the supervisor has to stay close to how the property presents, not just how it functions mechanically.

Beyond the physical plant, the role carries real coaching responsibility. That means setting individual goals with staff, modeling the right behaviors on the floor, and supporting the property manager in holding community and corporate standards. The supervisor also manages shop inventory, equipment, supply levels, and key security, and stays familiar with property budgets and longer-range capital planning conversations.

  • Minimum 2 years of experience managing maintenance operations at a residential community
  • At least 1 year of direct team leadership
  • Comfortable with technology and property management software
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Houston's housing stock runs hot and humid, and properties in The Core deal with HVAC systems that work hard year-round. A supervisor who can diagnose mechanical issues quickly, prioritize service orders accurately during peak summer demand, and keep turn times tight when occupancy pressure builds will outperform someone who's technically skilled but weak on scheduling and delegation. The coaching piece also carries real weight at Berkshire. A candidate who sees team development as part of the job, not a distraction from it, fits the culture better than one who prefers to handle everything personally.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development planning, and a benefits package. The company operates with an in-house ownership model, which creates more direct lines between property performance and the decisions that affect it day to day.

job.title: Maintenance Porter - Full-Time
job.description:
Porter roles at student housing communities carry more daily variability than most people expect. You're covering a lot of ground, often literally, and the standard of presentation matters because curb appeal and common area cleanliness directly affect leasing traffic and resident retention.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Redstone Residential operates over 38,000 beds across 20 states, making them one of the larger third-party student housing operators in the country. This Eugene property is part of their broader conventional multi-family portfolio. The Porter role here is full-time at $18.00 per hour, and the core of the job is keeping the community clean, safe, and presentable every day.

That means common areas, hallways, parking structures, and outdoor grounds. Snow and ice clearing when the season calls for it. Trash and debris removal, including pet waste. Lawn and landscaping upkeep, watering, and general grounds care. You'll also assist the maintenance team with basic repairs and general tasks as needed, so some mechanical comfort helps even if this isn't a tech-heavy position. The expectation is that you manage your daily rounds with minimal supervision and bring a genuinely decent attitude when you cross paths with residents.

Qualifications

  • Prior janitorial or cleaning experience preferred
  • Ability to work independently and stay on task without constant direction
  • Physical capability to lift 50+ lbs. and remain on your feet for 4 to 6 hour shifts
  • Friendly, professional demeanor with residents and coworkers

Benefits and Growth

Redstone offers a solid benefits package for a full-time hourly role: health, vision, and dental coverage, 15 days of PTO plus 10 paid holidays, paid parental leave, three paid service days, short-term disability, and a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match. They also include a continued education program and professional development support, which matters more than it sounds for someone who wants to move into a maintenance technician role down the road.

Porter positions are a legitimate entry point into property maintenance careers. The people who advance from here tend to be the ones who treat the grounds like they own them, notice things before they become work orders, and build trust with the maintenance team. That track record opens doors to make-ready work, tech roles, and eventually lead maintenance. Redstone's scale means those opportunities exist internally if you want them.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager - WOODLEA ELDERLY
job.description:
It's Monday morning. A tenant's recertification deadline is two weeks out, her income documentation is incomplete, and the HUD 4350.3 clock is running. That's the kind of moment that defines this role at Woodlea Elderly in Wilmington.

Fairstead is a vertically integrated affordable housing owner and operator with more than 30,000 units across 28 states. The company brings development, construction, and property management under one roof, and it runs a tech-forward operation that includes Yardi, digital compliance workflows, and data-driven decision-making at the property level. Woodlea Elderly is part of that portfolio, serving residents in the HUD-subsidized, elderly housing space where compliance precision and genuine resident care carry equal weight.

What This Role Covers Day to Day

The Assistant Community Manager supports the Property Manager across the full spectrum of site operations. On the compliance side, you'll work within the HUD 4350.3 Handbook framework, assist with preparation for REAC reviews, Management and Occupancy Reviews (MORs), LIHTC reviews, and investor site visits. Annual and interim recertifications are part of your regular rhythm, and you'll use EIV to verify income data and flag discrepancies before they become findings.

On the financial side, you'll track arrears consistently, follow up with tenants per company policy, post and deposit rents daily, and create purchase orders in Yardi. Delinquency management at an elderly affordable property requires a particular combination of firmness and empathy. Many residents are on fixed incomes, and your follow-up approach will reflect that reality while still protecting the property's financial performance.

Resident relations are central to this position. You'll respond to questions, complaints, and service requests promptly (same day where possible, never beyond 24 hours), coordinate with maintenance on open work orders, and manage communication around move-ins, move-outs, and any on-site emergencies. You'll also support lease renewal efforts to maintain healthy occupancy and reduce costly turn activity.

When a compliance review is approaching, you'll be in the weeds: pulling files, confirming EHS violations are cleared, and making sure documentation is airtight. The property's audit readiness is a direct reflection of how well this role is executed.

Qualifications

  • Minimum two years of experience in affordable housing leasing or property management
  • Working knowledge of HUD programs and the 4350.3 Handbook
  • Hands-on experience with EIV, Yardi, and RealPage
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, especially for sensitive resident interactions
  • Familiarity with the Wilmington residential market is a plus

Candidates who stand out in this type of role tend to be detail-oriented enough to catch a certification error before it becomes a finding, and people-skilled enough to handle a frustrated elderly resident with patience. Both matter equally here. The compliance side can be learned and refined, but genuine care for residents in this demographic is harder to teach.

Fairstead offers medical insurance through Meritain Health, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match (100% of the first 3%, 50% of the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 12 paid holidays, 7 sick days, and a flexible spending account, among other benefits.

job.title: Daytime Concierge (Mon-Fri, 11a-7p) - Shaw, D.C.
job.description:
Concierge roles at high-end multifamily properties are often misunderstood. The title sounds soft. The work isn't. This position at Bozzuto's Shaw community sits at the center of the resident experience, and the person filling it will handle everything from package logistics to event execution to first impressions for prospective residents walking through the door.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

The shift runs Monday through Friday, 11 a.m. to 7 p.m., which means you're catching residents on both ends of the workday. Mornings bring package deliveries and the occasional maintenance question. Afternoons bring traffic from prospects touring the community, residents returning home, and the social media content that keeps the building visible online. You're managing front desk logs, coordinating club room reservations, keeping the package room from turning into a storage unit, and scheduling freight elevators so move-ins don't become a hallway standoff. Bozzuto places real emphasis on community programming, so event planning is part of the job, not an afterthought.

The resident relationship piece is genuine here. Knowing residents by name, knowing their preferences, knowing their dogs, that's not a line in the job description for decoration. At a Class A building in Shaw, residents have options and expectations. The concierge is the consistent face that makes the property feel like home rather than just an address.

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

  • At least two years in hospitality, hotel, retail, or travel environments
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with software, apps, and property management platforms
  • Polished, professional presentation
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds (the holiday package volume is real)
  • A genuine instinct for anticipating what someone needs before they ask

Compensation and Growth

The base salary for this position is $50,000, with additional bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement. Bozzuto also maintains a range of employee resource groups and has a track record of developing people internally.

For candidates thinking about trajectory: concierge experience at a well-run, high-end community builds a resume that translates directly into leasing, assistant community manager, and resident services coordinator roles. You learn resident retention from the front lines, which is a skill that carries weight anywhere in multifamily. Shaw is a competitive submarket, and working a Bozzuto property here means daily exposure to a standard of operations that not every company maintains.

job.title: Make Ready Technician - South Lamar
job.description:
Make-ready work is one of the most skill-dense roles in residential property management. You're not just cleaning up after a resident moves out. You're running through a full punch list, prioritizing repairs by move-in deadline, estimating materials on the fly, and turning over an apartment that a new resident will walk into with real expectations. At Olympus Property's South Lamar community in Austin, that work happens Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, which is a schedule that's genuinely rare in maintenance.

What You'll Actually Do

The core of this role is unit turns. You'll inspect vacant apartments, identify what needs repair or replacement, and work through the list before the next resident moves in. That means plumbing work (fixtures, toilets, shower components), electrical repairs (switches, fixtures), and a lot of surface work: painting, priming, sealing, caulking, plastering, sanding. You'll also handle door hardware and lock systems, which matters more than most postings make it sound. A resident's first impression is often the front door.

Beyond turns, you'll pick up general work orders as needed. You'll also be calculating material needs and estimating costs, so you're expected to think ahead, not just execute tasks handed to you.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on experience in apartment turns, residential rehab, commercial maintenance, or retail facilities
  • Comfort working across multiple trades: basic plumbing, electrical, painting, and finish work
  • The ability to assess a unit, build a punch list, and sequence work efficiently
  • Attention to detail on final finishes, because make-ready quality directly affects resident satisfaction scores and lease-up momentum

Where This Role Can Take You
