  • Genuine organizational discipline and the ability to meet firm deadlines without being managed toward them
  • Comfort navigating online platforms and managing digital content
  • Bilingual Spanish is a plus given the LA market

Compensation runs $25 to $28 per hour. Full-time employees receive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with an employer contribution, a 401(k) with company match, short and long-term disability coverage, and a solid PTO package that includes vacation, sick time, personal days, holidays, and parental leave. Fridays end an hour early, which is a small but genuine quality-of-life detail. The Culver City location keeps you close to the westside without the Santa Monica price tag.

job.title: Cleaner - Full-Time-Temporary
job.description:
It's 7 a.m. in Pullman and move-in weekend is two days out. The hallways need a pass, the parking garage has tracked-in mud from last night's rain, and a resident cleaning check is already on the schedule before noon. That's the rhythm of this role.

Redstone Residential operates one of the largest third-party student housing portfolios in the country, with more than 38,000 beds across 20 states. This position supports one of their Pullman communities, which means working within a student housing environment where turnover is seasonal, occupancy expectations are high, and curb appeal directly affects leasing traffic. The role is full-time and temporary, paying $18.00 per hour, with a 401(k) plan that includes up to 6% matching.

What the Work Looks Like

This is a hands-on, on-your-feet position. Most of the shift involves keeping common areas clean and presentable: hallways, the clubhouse, the leasing office, model units, and outdoor grounds. You'll conduct scheduled cleaning checks inside resident apartments to confirm units meet the property's cleanliness standards, a task that requires both consistency and a professional manner with residents. Snow and ice clearing, trash and debris removal, landscaping upkeep, and basic maintenance assists round out the day-to-day. You'll be expected to manage your task list with minimal supervision.

Pullman's student population means this property likely sees concentrated turnover periods around the academic calendar. Keeping common areas sharp during peak traffic times matters more here than it would at a conventional mid-rise with staggered lease expirations. A strong cleaner in this context understands that the condition of a hallway or entrance is often the first impression a prospective resident gets on a tour.

What Redstone Is Looking For

  • Prior janitorial or cleaning experience in a residential, commercial, or institutional setting
  • Ability to complete daily tasks independently and stay on schedule without close direction
  • Physical capability to lift 50 or more pounds and remain on your feet for four to six hours at a stretch
  • A genuinely friendly, professional manner when interacting with residents and team members
  • Willingness to participate in Redstone's required training program

Candidates who do well in roles like this tend to take visible pride in the finished product, not just the completion of a checklist. In student housing specifically, the ability to stay consistent during busy periods (move-in, move-out, inspection weeks) without cutting corners is what separates reliable team members from ones who don't last through the season.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Roving -Terava, The Hixon and Lakeside Place
job.description:
Roving maintenance roles exist because no single property can always justify a full bench of technicians, but every property still needs consistent, skilled coverage. CloudTen Residential has structured this position to float across three Bend, Oregon communities: Lakeside Place, Terava, and The Hixon. If you know Bend's rental market, you know it's grown fast over the past decade, and the properties that hold occupancy are the ones that keep units tight and curb appeal sharp. This role sits at the center of that.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your day shifts between sites depending on where the need is greatest. One morning you might be knocking out a punch list of service requests at one property; by afternoon you're helping another team get a unit rent-ready before a new lease starts. The 3-to-5-day turn window is the standard here, so you'll move through make-readies with purpose: appliance repair, basic electrical, plumbing, painting, and anything else a unit needs to get back on the market clean and safe.

Beyond turns, you're handling day-to-day service requests with a 24-hour resolution target, supporting pool and spa upkeep, keeping common areas presentable, and running monthly preventive maintenance rounds that cover life safety systems, lighting, fire safety checks, and pool equipment. You'll need to know where shutoffs live at each site and be comfortable communicating delays to both residents and site managers when parts or scheduling push timelines out.

On-call emergency response is part of the job. After-hours calls come with the territory in any maintenance role, and this one is no exception. The flexibility to respond on evenings and weekends is a real requirement, not a footnote.

What CloudTen Is Looking For

  • One to two years of hands-on maintenance experience across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and painting
  • A valid driver's license (required, since you're moving between properties)
  • Comfort working independently and managing your own schedule across multiple sites
  • Basic computer and mobile device skills for work order systems and documentation
  • Strong communication habits, both with residents and with site management teams you're supporting
  • Availability for weekends, evenings, and holiday coverage

Pay runs $25.00 to $27.00 per hour depending on experience. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, company-paid life insurance, an FSA option, and paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays.

One thing that separates strong candidates in a roving role: the ability to walk into a property you don't manage daily and still get things done efficiently. You won't always have the home-field advantage of knowing where every tool is stored or which residents tend to submit repeat requests. Adaptability and organization matter here more than they do in a single-site position, and technicians who build that skill set often move into lead or supervisor roles as a natural next step.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
A prospect walks in off the street after seeing the listing online. They have questions, a budget, and maybe a move-in date three weeks out. Your job starts the moment they walk through the door.

Griffis Residential is hiring a Leasing Consultant for their Seattle community. This is a front-line sales and service role. You'll handle inbound traffic from prospects, conduct apartment tours, qualify applicants, and carry deals from first contact through signed lease. You'll also support renewals, move-in and move-out procedures, and coordinate with the maintenance team when resident concerns need follow-up.

What the Work Looks Like

Day to day, you're fielding calls and emails, scheduling tours, and walking prospects through available units. You match what you know about the apartment to what the prospect actually needs. You prep leases, track applications, and make sure nothing falls through the cracks between inquiry and move-in. On the marketing side, you support efforts to keep the community visible and the pipeline moving. Weekend availability is required; some evenings come with the territory.

Griffis operates luxury apartment communities, so the expectation is polished, professional communication across every channel. Residents and prospects notice when that standard slips.

What Griffis Is Looking For

  • High school diploma required; a bachelor's degree or NALP certification is preferred
  • At least one year of onsite leasing experience, or a background in hospitality, sales, or a similar customer-facing field
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort multitasking across phone, email, and in-person interactions simultaneously
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing regulations (a plus, but not a hard requirement)
  • Availability to work weekends and occasional evenings

The pay range is $23 to $25 per hour. Benefits include a 50% rental discount, a quarterly bonus program (up to $2,000 annually), per-lease occupancy bonuses starting at $175, medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with up to 4% company match, a minimum of three weeks PTO accruing from day one, 11 paid holidays, tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 per year, and paid parental leave.

One thing worth knowing: leasing consultant experience translates directly into assistant manager and property manager roles. Companies like Griffis promote from within, and time spent in leasing builds the resident relations, sales, and administrative skills that those next-level roles require. If you're treating this as a stepping stone into property management, this is a reasonable place to build that foundation.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Student housing operates on a different clock than conventional multifamily. Lease-up happens in the fall for the following academic year, the turn is compressed into a few brutal weeks in August, and your residents' parents are often just as involved as the residents themselves. The Assistant Community Manager role at The Domain at Waco exists inside that specific rhythm, and the person who thrives here understands that the financial office and the leasing floor aren't separate jobs , they're the same job.

The financial responsibilities here are real and central. You own the delinquency process from first notice through payment plan negotiations to guarantor outreach to coordinating with legal on evictions when it comes to that. You're posting payments, reconciling ledgers, preparing weekly and monthly reporting on occupancy and variance, handling security deposit dispositions, and coding invoices against budget. Clean books aren't a bonus , they're the baseline expectation. If spreadsheets make you anxious, this isn't the right fit.

At the same time, you carry an individual leasing and renewal goal during pre-lease season. By-the-bed leasing has its own mechanics: roommate matching, unit assignments, guarantor verification, and the particular patience required when you're explaining a joint-and-several lease structure to a parent in Houston who's never rented an apartment. You'll work the full pipeline from lead to signed lease, support renewal campaigns, and participate in on-campus outreach. Baylor's student population is the market , knowing that calendar matters.

When the Community Manager is off-site, you run the property. That means you need to already understand how the pieces connect: what a delinquency spike does to NOI, why curb appeal on move-in day matters to retention, how a botched punch list during turn creates maintenance headaches for twelve months. You'll also help hire and train leasing staff and Community Assistants, participate in the on-call rotation, and assist with annual turn inspections, punch walks, and move-in readiness.

What separates strong candidates in this role isn't leasing charisma. It's follow-through. Student housing offices get loud in August and quiet in October, and the people who struggle are usually the ones who can close a lease but let the ledger slide, or who handle the front desk well but disappear when a parent calls upset about a damage charge. The job rewards people who close every loop, document every outcome, and treat the delinquency number as their own.

What Karya is looking for

  • At least one year in property management, leasing, hospitality, or a comparable customer-facing role
  • Comfort with ledgers, reconciliation, and spreadsheet-level math
  • Ability to work weekends and extended hours during pre-lease season, turn, and move-in
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Prior student housing or by-the-bed leasing experience is preferred, as is familiarity with Entrata or RealPage
  • Bilingual English/Spanish is a plus

Compensation includes an hourly rate, leasing commissions, renewal bonuses, and quarterly or annual performance bonuses tied to occupancy and delinquency targets. Medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, and paid time off are included. A housing discount or on-site apartment may be available depending on circumstances.

job.title: Leasing Agent
job.description:
Urban lease-up shops live and die by first impressions, and at FLATS, the leasing agent is that impression. This Chicago-based lifestyle brand operates with a design-forward identity and a tech-integrated approach to apartment living, which means the leasing role here carries more brand weight than a typical Class B shop where you're just filling units.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

You'll own the full leasing cycle: fielding inquiries, conducting tailored tours, following up on leads through calls, texts, and email, and closing leases while hitting monthly targets. The follow-up cadence is where most leasing agents either earn their keep or fall behind. Traffic without conversion is just noise. Beyond closing, you'll handle applications, prepare lease documents, and keep records clean and compliant, which matters in Illinois where leasing activity is regulated and your license status is a real requirement. Either an Illinois Leasing Agent or Broker's License, or the ability to get a 120-day Student Permit before your start date, is non-negotiable here.

Move-in coordination is part of the role too. You'll make sure units are market-ready and that the move-in experience matches the brand promise. Resident concerns that surface early in a tenancy often land on the leasing agent's desk before anyone else's. How you handle those moments affects retention as much as it affects your own reputation on the team.

Weekend and evening availability is part of the job. That's true at most lease-up focused properties, and FLATS is direct about it.

What FLATS Is Looking For

  • Illinois Leasing Agent or Broker's License, or eligibility for a 120-day Student Permit
  • Prior leasing or sales experience, with a track record of closing
  • Strong written and verbal communication, the kind that works across email threads, phone calls, and face-to-face tours
  • Organized enough to manage multiple leads, applications, and move-in timelines simultaneously
  • Flexible schedule that covers evenings and weekends when prospect traffic peaks

Where This Role Can Take You

Leasing agents who develop genuine sales instincts and operational fluency tend to move into assistant manager or property manager roles within a few years. At a company like FLATS that runs multiple urban properties, internal mobility is realistic for people who demonstrate both closing ability and the kind of ownership mentality the company explicitly values. The skills that transfer are real ones: lead management, lease compliance, market comp knowledge, and resident relations. Those carry weight at virtually any multifamily operator.

What separates strong candidates here from average ones is the ability to sell the lifestyle authentically without it feeling like a script. FLATS leans hard into brand identity. Prospects who tour these properties are often choosing between a FLATS unit and several other well-appointed options in the same neighborhood. The agent who can articulate what makes the community distinct, and back it up with genuine product knowledge and a polished follow-up process, is the one who closes.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Supervisor - Venue at Lakewood
job.description:
Maintenance supervisors at AIR Communities carry two distinct skill sets at once: hands-on technical competence and people management. This role at Venue at Lakewood in Bradenton demands both, every day. If you're stronger in one area than the other, this probably isn't the right fit.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

The technical side covers what you'd expect from a full-service apartment maintenance operation: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and general building systems. You'll oversee preventative maintenance schedules, manage apartment turns to get units ready for move-in, and field resident service requests alongside your team. AIR uses modern maintenance technology to track and prioritize work orders, so comfort with digital tools matters here.

The management side is just as active. You'll lead at least one direct report, coordinate vendor relationships, and communicate capital and maintenance needs up to property management. Budget oversight is part of the job. You're expected to track spend, flag issues early, and keep quality high without letting costs drift.

Environmental health and safety compliance is a real part of this role. AIR has operating procedures and regulatory requirements that the maintenance team is responsible for following. You'll need to know those standards and make sure your team does too.

What the Role Requires

  • At least 3 years of technical maintenance and facilities experience in residential property management
  • 1 to 3 years of supervisory or team lead experience in a maintenance or customer service setting
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule including evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts (at minimum one week per month)
  • Physical ability to move heavy equipment and machinery
  • Reliable personal transportation
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and genuine attention to detail
  • English fluency (read, write, speak)

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The supervisors who do well in roles like this are the ones who troubleshoot fast and communicate clearly. Bradenton's climate means HVAC demand stays high through much of the year. Candidates who know refrigerant systems well and can diagnose problems without waiting on a vendor call will have a real advantage. On the management side, the difference usually comes down to how well someone can develop a team member who's still learning. That's a different skill than doing the repair yourself, and AIR puts weight on it.

AIR offers an on-site apartment benefit, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, paid parental leave, tuition assistance, and full reimbursement for job-related certifications and licenses. That last point is worth noting for anyone looking to add credentials like EPA 608 or CAMT to their resume while working.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Bozzuto operates some of the most well-regarded residential communities on the East Coast, and their maintenance teams carry a real operational weight. The Assistant Maintenance Manager role at their Alexandria property sits at the intersection of hands-on trade work and team leadership. You're not just fixing things. You're running a program.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your day is built around two priorities: keeping current residents comfortable and getting vacant units back online fast. That means staying sharp on service ticket volume, making sure HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance calls get closed out properly, and following up with residents so nothing slips. On the make-ready side, you're managing the turn process from punch list to move-in ready, which directly affects how quickly new leases can start. A slow turn is a real NOI drag, and you'll feel that pressure in a community like this one.

Beyond the reactive work, you're also executing preventative maintenance programs that protect the asset long-term. That includes mechanical systems like boilers, chillers, and central plant components, not just unit-level repairs. Snow removal and grounds upkeep fall in your scope too, and so does maintaining the safety and code compliance standards that keep the property operating without incident.

Weekend availability and participation in the emergency on-call rotation are part of this role. That's standard at this level in multifamily, but worth knowing going in.

What Bozzuto Expects You to Bring

  • 5 or more years in the trades, facilities maintenance, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems including split systems, boilers, and chillers
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Understanding of OSHA, MSDS, and risk management practices
  • Supervisory experience or a demonstrated ability to lead a small team
  • Comfort with technology platforms, work order systems, and Microsoft Office basics
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently, climb ladders, and work in varying weather

Where This Role Can Take You

Strong Assistant Maintenance Managers at companies like Bozzuto typically move into Maintenance Manager roles within a few years, taking full ownership of a community's physical plant and maintenance budget. The skills you build here, specifically preventative maintenance discipline, turn efficiency, and team supervision, translate directly to portfolio-level facilities roles as well. The salary range for this position runs from $68,000 to $70,000, with bonus eligibility, plus a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off, 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

If you think in terms of asset preservation and take personal ownership of the physical product your residents experience every day, this is a role worth a serious look.

job.title: Affordable Housing Compliance Specialist
job.description:
A file lands in the queue at 8 a.m. By 8 a.m. the next day, it needs a compliance decision. That 24-hour review window is the operational heartbeat of this role.

The Work

Asset Living, one of the NMHC top 50 third-party management firms, is hiring an Affordable Housing Compliance Specialist for a position based in Staten Island, NY. This role sits inside Asset Living's affordable housing division and focuses on keeping resident files audit-ready and fully aligned with LIHTC regulatory requirements.

Day to day, you'll review incoming applicant files for eligibility and compliance, working against that 24-hour turnaround standard. You'll track regulatory changes in the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program and translate those changes into updated internal processes. When outside entities conduct tax credit reviews, you're in the room. When TDHCA schedules its annual training, you're on the calendar. This position also carries a significant travel component: roughly 50% of your time annually, covering property visits, conferences, and training sessions.

The HCCP designation is a clear milestone in this role. If you don't already hold it, you'll be expected to complete the Housing Credit Certified Professional training and pass the exam within your first two years. That credential signals genuine fluency in tax credit compliance, and Asset Living is investing in getting you there.

What You Bring

  • Detail orientation that holds up under volume. Compliance errors in affordable housing files can trigger findings during audits, so accuracy isn't negotiable.
  • Working knowledge of LIHTC eligibility rules and regulatory frameworks. HUD program familiarity is a plus.
  • Hands-on experience with RealPage Onesite Tax Credit software, or the computer literacy to get there quickly.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills. You'll document findings clearly and interact with property staff, applicants, and external reviewers.
  • HCCP designation, or the willingness to pursue it on the timeline described above.

The salary for this role in New York is set at $60,000.

One thing worth understanding about affordable housing compliance as a career path: specialists who build deep LIHTC and HUD audit experience tend to move into regional compliance manager roles or portfolio-level compliance director positions. The combination of file-level technical skill and regulatory monitoring you'll develop here translates directly into higher-level oversight work as Asset Living's affordable housing portfolio grows.

job.title: Business Manager - The Overlook at Quarry Hill
job.description:
Austin's Class A multifamily market keeps pushing rents and expectations upward, which means the Business Manager role at a luxury community carries real weight. You're running the full asset: financial performance, team development, resident experience, and physical condition of the property. That's not a coordinator title with a manager label slapped on it.

The Overlook at Quarry Hill is an Olympus Property community, and Olympus has earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer recognition three consecutive years. The Business Manager here reports to Regional Leadership and owns the daily operation from every angle, including budgeting, vendor contracts, leasing programs, and maintenance oversight.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On the financial side, you're building and managing annual business plans, reviewing T-12 performance, tracking NOI, and having real conversations with your Regional Manager and Regional VP about where the asset is and where it's headed. You're not just reporting numbers; you're expected to have a point of view on them. Monthly budget projections, occupancy strategy, and capex decisions all run through you.

On the people side, you're leading an onsite team of both office and maintenance staff. That means hiring, training, counseling, and motivating people who handle everything from make-readies and punch lists to lease renewals and traffic conversion. Keeping a luxury Class A community in market-ready condition requires a maintenance team that's on its game and a leasing team that knows how to close.

Vendor relationships matter here too. You'll bid, negotiate, and manage service contracts and one-time projects, which requires some comfort with the numbers behind those decisions, not just the relationship side.

RealPage, Knock, and OneSite experience is strongly preferred. If you've been running reports and managing delinquency out of OneSite for a few years, that's a real advantage.

Who Fits This Role

  • Minimum two years of experience as a property manager in multifamily, with luxury or Class A background preferred
  • Comfort reading and presenting financial reports to regional leadership
  • Experience managing both leasing and maintenance staff at the same time
  • RealPage/OneSite/Knock platform familiarity
  • Availability Monday through Friday with flexibility for after-hours resident events and emergencies

The base salary range is $65,000 to $68,000, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program, among others.

One thing worth noting for candidates coming from smaller operators: Olympus runs a structured career pathing program and sends managers to Budget Camp and Leadership Conferences. If you've been running a community without much institutional support, this environment offers more infrastructure than you might be used to, and that's either appealing or an adjustment depending on your style.

job.title: Field Support Supervisor - Multifamily Regional Maintenance
job.description:
Regional maintenance roles at multifamily companies tend to fall into two buckets: the ones that are mostly administrative oversight, and the ones that actually put you on the ground with tools, blueprints, and conversations that matter. This one is clearly the second kind. Weinstein Properties, a family-owned operator with more than 70 years in the business, is adding a Field Support Supervisor to cover several of their Dallas-Fort Worth communities.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You'll move between properties regularly, so a desk isn't your home base. On any given week, you might be reviewing a contractor's proposal for exterior repairs at one community, walking a punch list on a project transitioning from the construction team at another, and helping a site maintenance supervisor think through a water intrusion problem at a third. The role touches capital projects, vendor management, and day-to-day operational support in equal measure.

Weinstein self-manages their portfolio, which means the Asset Management and Support team you'd join works closely with the people actually running the properties. You're not a third-party consultant parachuting in. You're a resource that property teams can rely on, which means your relationships with maintenance supervisors and community managers matter as much as your technical knowledge.

  • Frequent property visits to assess needs and provide hands-on technical guidance
  • Managing projects from scoping through completion, including vendor selection and proposal review
  • Supporting the handoff of construction projects to property teams, including documentation and knowledge transfer
  • Evaluating products, equipment, and contractors, and encouraging qualified vendors to bid competitively
  • Identifying capital needs, erosion issues, water intrusion, and exterior building concerns, then writing clear work requirements to address them

Who Fits This Role Well

The minimum bar here is real: EPA certification (Type I and II or Universal), at least five years in multifamily maintenance, and three or more years in a regional support capacity. The ability to read blueprints and a valid driver's license are both required, not optional. If you've spent time on capex projects and know how to evaluate a contractor's scope before signing off on it, that experience will be put to use immediately.

What separates stronger candidates from technically qualified ones in this kind of role is usually communication. You're working across property managers, maintenance supervisors, vendors, and a construction group. The ability to give clear guidance without being dismissive of what site teams are already dealing with makes a significant difference in whether people actually call you for help or try to work around you.

A Note on the Company

Weinstein Properties has operated for over 70 years as a family-owned company with communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. That longevity in a competitive industry reflects something real about how they operate. The company's stated focus on customer experience isn't just marketing language here. It shows up in how they think about property operations, which means the support function you'd be filling is tied directly to resident outcomes, not just asset performance numbers.

Compensation is competitive, and the company offers benefits and a 401k. If you're based in or near DFW and want a regional role with genuine variety and direct impact on how properties run day to day, this is worth a serious look.

job.title: Dual-Site Leasing & Marketing Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

Student housing leasing moves fast and follows a rhythm most conventional multifamily managers never experience. Annual turnover isn't a figure on a T-12; it's a full operational event where hundreds of residents move out and a new cohort moves in within a compressed window. The Leasing and Marketing Manager role at Scion's Ion Austin and Lark Austin communities requires someone who can hold a sales conversation in the morning, pull traffic and conversion KPIs in the afternoon, and still coach a team member through a difficult prospect interaction before the day ends. Interpersonal skill, data literacy, and genuine comfort with a six-day workweek during peak periods all matter here.

This is a dual-site position, so the ability to context-switch between two communities without losing track of either property's occupancy goals, concession budgets, or resident feedback loops is a real daily demand. If you've only ever managed one asset at a time, that's worth thinking through before applying.

What the Work Actually Involves

On the sales side, you'll drive leasing activity directly and through your team, conduct weekly market surveys, and identify local marketing opportunities that generate qualified traffic. Scion uses Entrata as its property management system, so familiarity there saves ramp time. Social media is an active part of the job, particularly Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook, and on-campus marketing events fall under your scope as well.

Beyond leasing, the role carries real operational weight. You'll work alongside the General Manager on the annual turnover process, coordinate facilities work orders, track resident satisfaction tied to maintenance response, and keep curb appeal and common areas to standard. Staff development is part of the job too: coaching Experience Team Members, supporting Fair Housing compliance, and building a team culture that holds up during the busy season.

  • Two or more years in customer service, sales, or community management
  • Comfort working up to six days per week during peak leasing and turnover periods
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and property management systems (Entrata preferred)
  • Strong written and verbal communication across multiple platforms
  • Experience managing or directing a team, even informally

What Makes This Specific Role Worth Considering

Student housing sits in its own category within multifamily. Lease-up pressure is seasonal and concentrated, concessions are a real competitive tool in the Austin market, and your residents are vocal and digitally active in ways that make your social media presence functionally part of your leasing funnel. Candidates who thrive here tend to understand that the turnover window is where reputations are made or lost, and they plan for it months in advance rather than reacting to it.

Scion operates at scale across student housing nationally, which means internal mobility and career development are realistic outcomes for people who perform. A strong showing in a dual-site role like this one positions you well for a General Manager track or a regional operations role down the line. The learning reimbursement benefit signals that the company invests in people who want to grow, not just fill a seat.

job.title: Leasing and Experience Manager (Alderwood & Timberleaf)
job.description:
A prospective resident walks in on a Saturday afternoon, a little overwhelmed by their options in Silicon Valley's rental market. By the time they leave, they've got a clear picture of the community, a follow-up scheduled, and a genuine sense that someone actually listened to them. That interaction is the heartbeat of this role.

What This Role Actually Involves

Prometheus Real Estate Group is hiring a Leasing and Experience Manager to work across two of their Santa Clara communities: Alderwood and Timberleaf. Prometheus is the largest privately held apartment owner in the Bay Area, with a portfolio of over 13,000 units across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle. They've held that position since 1965 by investing long-term and reinvesting in their properties consistently, so this isn't a company chasing short-term NOI at the expense of resident experience.

The title is their version of what most companies call an Assistant Property Manager or Assistant Business Manager, but the scope here is genuinely broader. You'll handle leasing activity directly, help coach the leasing team toward closes, and build out sales and marketing strategies that keep occupancy where it needs to be. You'll also take ownership of resident relations: resolving concerns, following up until they're actually resolved, and organizing events that build a real sense of community. On the operational side, you'll work with pricing, concessions, collections, and occupancy reporting. It's a full-cycle position where you're touching leasing, people management, and daily operations in the same week, sometimes the same day.

Weekend availability is part of the job. Traffic is highest on Saturdays and Sundays, and Prometheus structures schedules accordingly, with regular weekdays off in exchange.

Who Fits Well Here

Prometheus looks for at least two years of leasing experience, and a bachelor's degree is preferred (a high school diploma or GED is required). They also hire across industries, so if your background is in hospitality, retail, or another customer-facing field with some leasing experience layered in, that combination is worth highlighting.

What separates strong candidates in a role like this is the ability to hold two modes at once: the warmth and attentiveness that makes a resident feel genuinely cared for, and the operational discipline to keep delinquency low, concessions tracked, and the leasing team accountable to goals. People who lean too far into one mode or the other tend to struggle. The best Leasing and Experience Managers know when to slow down for a conversation and when to stay focused on the numbers.

Compensation runs between $33.25 and $36.25 per hour, with a $200 per-lease incentive, a semi-annual discretionary bonus, and weekend shift premium pay. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, vision, and dental (dependents included), 401(k) with employer matching, tenure-based housing discounts, tuition reimbursement, and 12 paid holidays, including your birthday.

  • At least two years of leasing experience required
  • High school diploma or GED required; bachelor's degree preferred
  • Weekend availability required as part of the regular schedule
  • Comfort with leasing team supervision, coaching, and goal-setting
  • Experience with pricing, concessions, collections, and occupancy reporting

This role sits one step below Community Manager, and Prometheus promotes from within. If you're looking to move into full property management, this is a well-structured path to get there.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning and you're already reviewing last night's online reviews, pulling a delinquency report, and fielding a call from a vendor running behind on a turn. By 10 AM, you've coached a leasing consultant through a tough objection and approved a make-ready punch list. That's the rhythm of this role at Evolve Huntersville, and it's a good one if you're wired for it.

What This Role Actually Covers

Hawthorne Residential Partners is one of the top 50 multifamily management companies in the country, with deep roots in the Southeast. As Community Manager at Evolve Huntersville in Huntersville, NC, you carry full operational accountability: financial performance, leasing and renewals, vendor oversight, team development, and resident experience. You're reading financial reports and making budget-aware decisions, not just passing numbers up the chain. Delinquency tracking, deposit accounting, move-out reconciliation, and occupancy strategy all sit on your desk. You'll work in Yardi and Knock, so comfort with both gives you a real head start.

On the leasing side, this isn't a role where you hand off entirely to your team. You support leasing activity directly, conduct tours, respond to leads, and make sure applications and renewals get processed accurately and on time. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, which means showcasing resident events and keeping the community's online reputation sharp.

Team leadership here is hands-on. You hire, train, and run weekly meetings across office and maintenance staff. You're the culture carrier for what Hawthorne calls their Live It philosophy, which centers on service and genuine connection. That means handling escalated resident concerns with real care and holding your team accountable at the same time.

Experience and Qualifications

  • At least two years of property management experience, including time as a Leasing Consultant and Assistant Community Manager
  • Six months of direct Community Manager experience in multifamily is strongly preferred
  • Yardi, Knock, and Microsoft Office experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license required; CAM, CAPS, or a real estate or property management license is a plus
  • High school diploma or GED required

The office runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays 10 to 4, with one weekday off to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Some evenings and weekends come up for resident events or community needs.

Compensation includes a base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, and company-paid life insurance.

One thing worth noting for anyone thinking about trajectory: Hawthorne has a formal Career Path Program designed to move Community Managers toward Regional Manager roles. The skills you build here, specifically reading a T-12, managing NOI at the property level, and developing a team that performs without constant oversight, are exactly what regional operations demand. If you're thinking two or three years out, this role builds the foundation directly.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Part-Time)
job.description:
Part-time leasing roles at established New England operators tend to be genuinely instructive. The hours are focused, the traffic is real, and the feedback loop between prospect interaction and signed lease is short enough that you learn quickly what works and what doesn't. This position at The Ledges in Weymouth puts you in that environment under the banner of John M. Corcoran & Company, a firm with roots going back to 1951 and a reputation for developing people as deliberately as it develops properties.

What the Role Involves

The core of this position is converting traffic into leases. You'll tour apartments with prospective residents, walk them through pricing and lease terms, and process their applications through to approval. From there, you'll build out lease packages and coordinate move-ins, which means the job doesn't end at the signed application. You own the experience through the point when a new resident gets their keys.

Beyond the tour itself, you'll contribute to the marketing side of leasing. That includes setting occupancy goals and working toward them through digital channels, social media, and local networking. You'll also stay connected with current residents throughout their tenancy and complete regular property inspections to keep curb appeal where it needs to be. At 20 hours per week, the schedule runs afternoons Monday through Friday, with a slightly later shift on Wednesdays.

Skills This Role Requires vs. Skills It Builds

A few things need to come in the door with you: clear communication, comfort with computers and customer-facing interactions, solid time management, and the kind of organized follow-through that keeps a prospect pipeline from going cold. A high school diploma or equivalent is the educational baseline.

What the role builds is different. You'll develop a working fluency in lease administration, a feel for how advertising channels actually drive traffic, and an understanding of how move-in quality shapes early resident retention. Those are transferable skills. Leasing consultants who learn to read their own traffic data and close consistently tend to move into assistant manager roles, where occupancy accountability and delinquency management become part of the job. This position is a reasonable first step toward that track.

The Company Behind the Role

JMC's longevity in New England real estate is worth noting because it reflects something about how the company operates internally. Long tenure among staff is a signal that the culture isn't just a talking point. For someone starting in property management, working inside a company where institutional knowledge is accessible and mentorship happens organically is a real advantage. The $2,500 sign-on bonus, along with medical, dental, vision, life insurance, PTO, and a 401(k) with company match, rounds out a compensation package that's competitive for a part-time leasing role at this pay range.

  • Pay range: $23.00 to $27.50 per hour
  • Sign-on bonus: $2,500
  • Schedule: Monday through Friday afternoons, 20 hours per week
  • Benefits: Medical, dental, vision, life insurance, paid time off, 401(k) with match

If you want to learn leasing from a company that's been doing it for over 70 years, this is a practical place to start.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is often described as a sales job, and that's technically true. But at the property level, it's also the first real impression a future resident gets of where they're going to live. That gap between "sales transaction" and "someone choosing a home" is where this role actually lives.

Paragon Properties is hiring a Leasing Consultant for their Southfield, Michigan community. Starting pay is $18.50 per hour and is negotiable based on prior leasing experience. This is a full-time, 40-hour-per-week position with a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage with a short waiting period, paid time off, nine paid holidays, a 401(k) with employer contribution, company-paid life and disability insurance, and a rent discount. There's also a move-in bonus tied to leasing activity, which rewards the work directly.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

You'll handle the full leasing cycle: phone and walk-in traffic, tours, application processing, move-in paperwork, and renewal coordination. A good chunk of the job is communication, both the kind that closes a lease and the kind that keeps a current resident from leaving. You'll inspect vacant units and models to make sure they're show-ready, follow up on work orders to confirm resident satisfaction, and help with outreach to local businesses and employers. Resident events are part of the mix too.

The administrative side is real. Processing applications, preparing paperwork for manager review, and keeping documentation accurate all require genuine attention to detail. Yardi experience is a plus here. Fair Housing knowledge matters too, because mistakes in that area carry consequences.

What Paragon Is Looking For

  • At least one year in a customer service or sales role; six or more months of on-site leasing experience preferred
  • High school diploma or equivalent required; some college preferred
  • Comfort with MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook); Yardi experience a plus
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations preferred
  • Strong sales instincts and genuine follow-through

Pre-employment background check, drug screening, and physical are required before starting.

One thing worth noting for candidates coming from retail or hospitality: leasing has a learning curve that's less about personality and more about process. The people skills translate immediately. What takes time is understanding lease terms, application workflows, and how to handle objections specific to housing decisions. Paragon offers a training program, which helps, but candidates who already know how to read a lease or have touched property management software will get up to speed faster and feel less overwhelmed in the first 90 days. This role can also move into an Assistant Manager position for someone who develops the administrative and financial side of the work.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance
job.description:
Birgo operates a portfolio of residential properties across Cleveland, with this opening focused on Shaker Heights and Edgewater. The technician hired here will carry a broad scope: make-readies, preventative maintenance, and the full range of trade repairs that keep occupied units functional and turned units rent-ready on schedule.

What You'll Actually Do

Turns are the rhythm of this role. Drywall patches, paint, plumbing fixes, electrical troubleshooting, carpentry, HVAC checks , you'll move through make-ready punch lists and get units back online. Beyond turns, you'll handle day-to-day repair requests across multiple properties and run a preventative maintenance program that keeps deferred costs from compounding. Shaker Heights in particular has older housing stock, which means boiler systems show up frequently. Comfort with boiler operation and maintenance is a genuine advantage here, not a nice-to-have on paper.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., with participation in an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That rotation is worth understanding before you apply: after-hours calls are real, and being prepared for them mentally is part of doing this job well.

You'll need your own reliable, insured transportation to move between properties, a valid driver's license, and the physical capacity to lift 50 pounds unassisted, work in confined spaces, and safely use power tools and ladders.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on experience across multiple trades: plumbing, electrical, drywall, painting, carpentry, and HVAC
  • Ability to work through a make-ready punch list efficiently and independently
  • Boiler experience (helpful, given the property locations)
  • Valid driver's license and personal, insured transportation
  • Eligibility to work in the United States
  • Physical ability to lift 50 pounds, use power tools safely, and work in confined spaces

The Bigger Picture

Birgo pays $23 to $26 per hour, weekly. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life coverage with employer contribution, paid time off, paid holidays, sick time, a 401(k) match, professional development reimbursement, and discounted rent at Birgo properties. The company describes itself as mission-driven, and its stated values include integrity, teamwork, and a genuine investment in staff development. For a technician who wants to sharpen skills across trade disciplines while working a predictable weekday schedule with a company that tracks professional growth, this is a solid setup.

What separates strong candidates here is range. Single-trade specialists will struggle with the variety this role demands. The technician who can close out a plumbing ticket, pivot to a drywall repair, and still troubleshoot a boiler issue before the end of the day is the one who'll thrive across Birgo's Cleveland portfolio.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Berkshire Residential Investments owns and manages its own properties, which means the leasing team at a community like 20 Midtown operates with a different kind of accountability than you'd find at a third-party fee management shop. There's no owner-operator disconnect. The people setting leasing strategy are the same people watching NOI.

This role sits at the intersection of team leadership and sales execution. You'll hire, train, and develop leasing staff, set the pace on the sales floor, and own the resident experience from first inquiry through renewal conversations. That means coaching your team through traffic fluctuations, keeping delinquency communication professional and consistent, and making sure the property's voice across social media and digital channels reflects the community accurately. Berkshire uses content marketing and social presence as real leasing tools, so comfort with those platforms matters here.

Three years of multifamily experience is the baseline. What separates stronger candidates is the combination of analytical thinking and people instincts. Goal-setting in leasing requires reading T-3 trends, understanding where concessions are moving in the submarket, and adjusting team focus accordingly. The best leasing managers don't just motivate their teams with energy. They give their team the right targets and the context to understand why those targets matter.

Atlanta's Midtown submarket has seen consistent Class A lease-up activity over the past several years, with newer deliveries keeping competitive pressure on occupancy and pushing properties to differentiate on experience rather than price alone. A leasing manager here needs to know how to hold rate while still closing traffic, and how to coach a leasing team through a market that rewards relationship-building over transactional pitches.

What Berkshire is looking for

  • At least three years in multifamily real estate, with direct team leadership experience
  • Demonstrated ability to recruit, train, and assess leasing staff performance
  • Comfort setting goals analytically and reporting results clearly
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills for both resident-facing and internal use
  • Active engagement with social media and digital content as leasing channels
  • Ability to work effectively with residents and prospects from diverse backgrounds

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, health insurance, retirement benefits, paid parental and sick leave, and bonus eligibility. The company operates with an in-house ownership model, which tends to create more direct career paths into regional and portfolio-level roles for leasing managers who produce results.

job.title: Leasing Specialist - Full - Time
job.description:
Redstone Residential operates more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, making it one of the largest third-party student housing management companies in the country. Its conventional multifamily portfolio is growing fast, and this full-time Leasing Specialist role at its Chicago community puts you at the center of that growth. If you're early in a property management career and want a role that sharpens real, transferable skills, this is a strong place to build them.

Leasing is a craft, and this role teaches it. You'll work alongside Community and Leasing Managers to hit daily and weekly traffic and occupancy goals, which means you're learning how KPIs connect to property performance in real time. Handling ledger questions, processing rent payments, and responding to prospect inquiries are the daily rhythm. None of it is glamorous on its own, but together these tasks build the kind of resident-facing fluency that separates strong property managers from average ones later in their careers.

What the role requires on day one: one to two years in customer service or sales, solid written and verbal communication, and the composure to stay steady when a frustrated resident walks in mid-month. Familiarity with property management software helps, and Redstone uses Entrata, so any prior exposure to that platform is a genuine advantage. Beyond the technical side, the team is looking for someone with a warm presence. In leasing, personality closes tours that specs alone never would.

What the role builds over time is harder to list on a resume but easy to see in practice. You'll develop an instinct for reading prospect intent, an understanding of how delinquency affects NOI at the property level, and the habit of treating every interaction as a data point in the community's reputation. Those skills carry directly into Leasing Manager and Assistant Manager roles, which is typically where strong Leasing Specialists move next in a third-party management environment like Redstone's.

Qualifications

  • 1 to 2 years of customer service or sales experience
  • Strong written and verbal communication
  • Comfort with basic computer tasks including correspondence and memos
  • Experience with Entrata or similar PM software is a plus
  • Ability to stay composed under pressure
  • High school diploma or equivalent

Compensation starts at $19.00 per hour with performance bonuses available. Benefits include health, vision, and dental insurance, 15 days of PTO, 10 paid holidays, paid parental leave, a 401(k) with up to 6% matching, and continued education and professional development programs. Redstone is an equal opportunity employer.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Fairstead runs a portfolio of more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states, and they operate as a fully integrated owner, operator, and developer. That means maintenance leadership at their sites isn't just about fixing things. It's about holding a standard across a professionally managed affordable housing portfolio where operational consistency matters at scale.

This Service Manager role is based in Cleveland and puts you in charge of the day-to-day maintenance operation at the property. You'll supervise maintenance staff, manage special projects, and perform skilled hands-on work yourself when needed. The expectation is that you bring real trade depth, whether that's electrical, plumbing, HVAC, or another core discipline, plus the general maintenance range to handle what comes up between those specialties.

You'll own the condition of the building systems and the cleanliness and safety of the property's common areas and facilities. That means regular inspection of mechanical and electrical equipment, timely repairs, and keeping everything running in line with Fairstead's safety standards. When a complex project comes up, you won't be left alone to figure it out, but routine work is yours to manage independently. Overtime comes with the territory when emergencies or special projects demand it.

On the administrative side, Fairstead uses Yardi, and familiarity with that platform is a plus. You'll also work within Microsoft Office for documentation and reporting. The ability to implement and refine procedures matters here. Fairstead takes a tech-forward approach to operations, so a manager who can adapt to systems and data-driven workflows will fit better than someone who prefers to keep everything informal.

Qualifications

  • At least three years of property maintenance experience
  • Proficiency in a specific trade plus broad general maintenance skills
  • Solid knowledge of building and mechanical trade tools, techniques, and terminology
  • Strong grasp of safety protocols and accident prevention
  • Ability to supervise staff and lead projects
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office; Yardi experience is a bonus

Strong candidates for this role tend to have more than just technical skill. The ones who stand out can also communicate clearly with residents, hold their team accountable without micromanaging, and keep a punch list moving even when priorities shift mid-week. Affordable housing properties often have longer-tenured residents with higher service expectations than people assume. The manager who earns trust on the ground floor of the building earns it across the whole community.

job.title: Manager, Centralized Resident Account Services
job.description:
It's 9 a.m. on the first of the month. Rent has posted across the portfolio, and the delinquency report is already on your screen. You're triaging: who gets a demand letter today, which residents need a payment arrangement conversation, and which accounts are headed to agency placement. That's the rhythm this role runs on.

What This Role Actually Covers

RedPeak is a Denver-based apartment owner, operator, and developer with 24 years focused exclusively on the Colorado market. This position sits at the corporate level and owns centralized resident account operations across the entire portfolio. That means delinquency management, move-out accounting, security deposit reconciliations, collections strategy, and month-end close processes all run through this function. The person in this seat is the primary point of contact for onsite teams and third-party collection vendors, and they work closely with regional managers, property accounting, and legal counsel when eviction proceedings require coordination.

The role also carries a process improvement mandate. RedPeak wants this manager to analyze delinquency trends, identify where bad debt is accumulating, and build proactive strategies to reduce outstanding receivables before they age out. That includes leading system implementations, writing rollout plans, developing training materials, and serving as the internal subject matter expert when new software or workflows come online. This is a centralized function in an active growth company, so the scope will expand as the portfolio does.

One detail worth noting: the position starts at RedPeak's corporate office on South Broadway and will relocate to another Denver location as the function matures. It's structured as a transition-track role, which reflects how RedPeak is building this centralized model out over time.

What RedPeak Is Looking For

  • At least 3 years in multifamily operations, property management, or property accounting
  • Hands-on experience with delinquency management, move-out accounting, and collections workflows
  • Proven ability to lead teams and coach onsite staff through process changes
  • Experience managing software rollouts or process improvement initiatives in a multifamily context
  • Strong analytical skills and comfort working with KPIs and operational data
  • The communication range to handle escalated resident conversations and cross-departmental coordination equally well
  • Proficiency with property management software and a tolerance for high call volume, especially in the early phase of the role
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation for occasional property visits

The salary range is $75,000 to $95,000, with a bonus component. Benefits include full medical, dental, and vision coverage, employer-paid short-term disability, and a 401(k) with company match that vests on day one.

Strong candidates will have more than just collections experience. The differentiator here is the combination of operational discipline and change management ability. RedPeak is building a centralized accounting function, which means the person who thrives in this role can hold the day-to-day delinquency cycle together while simultaneously standardizing workflows, training onsite teams, and pushing system improvements forward. Those two modes, execution and infrastructure building, don't always coexist in one person. When they do, this kind of centralized role becomes a clear path toward a director-level operations or accounting leadership position.

job.title: Part-Time Porter
job.description:
Porter roles at student housing properties move at a different pace than conventional multifamily. Turns happen fast, traffic through common areas is constant, and the standard of cleanliness residents expect tends to be higher than their actual behavior suggests. PeakMade Real Estate, which focuses on off-campus student housing along with multifamily and build-to-rent communities, is hiring a part-time Porter at their Rochester property.

What the Work Looks Like

The core of this role is keeping the property presentable and functional on a daily basis. That means cleaning the leasing office, amenity spaces, laundry facilities, and common areas on a regular schedule. When units turn, you'll help prepare them for the next resident: cleaning, checking condition, and supporting the make-ready process. You'll also manage cleaning supplies and equipment inventory, report anything unusual on the property or involving residents, and follow OSHA safety standards consistently.

Physical demands here are real. Frequent lifting up to 75 pounds, bending, stooping, and working with cleaning chemicals and equipment are all part of the job. If you've done facilities or porter work before, none of this will surprise you.

What PeakMade Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Ability to follow written instructions and communicate clearly in basic exchanges
  • Safe handling and maintenance of cleaning fluids and tools
  • Physical capability to meet the demands described above
  • Reliability and a professional appearance on site

Pay runs $17.00 to $18.00 per hour depending on experience and internal equity. Benefits include a 401(k) match, a housing discount that varies by property, wellness programs through PeakMade's LiveWell initiative, and access to leadership training for those who want to grow within the company.

A Note on Student Housing Specifically

Student housing turns are compressed and unforgiving. Move-out and move-in windows are short, and the volume of unit prep that happens in a few weeks is significant. Porter staff who can keep up during that crunch, and maintain steady quality during the quieter months, tend to get noticed quickly. For someone looking to move into a maintenance tech or lead role down the road, this is a reasonable place to start building that track record.

job.title: Maintenance Technician Apartment Community PLUS Competitive Benefits
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

At Aspen Riverpark Apartments, a 261-unit affordable community in Newark, you'll be the person residents count on when something goes wrong. That means working through a daily queue of service requests covering plumbing, HVAC, appliances, and general repairs, while also keeping up with preventative maintenance so problems don't compound over time. You'll inspect common areas and building systems, catch issues before residents notice them, and keep your supervisor informed about supply needs and reorder points. The work is hands-on and varied, which most technicians with multifamily experience will find familiar, but the pace and expectations at a community this size require solid organization and self-direction.

On-call rotation is part of this role. After-hours emergencies come with the territory in multifamily maintenance, and IPG pays overtime for on-call hours worked. If you've done this before, you know what that means: some quiet weeks, some late-night calls. It's worth going in with eyes open about that dynamic.

You'll bring your own hand tools. The property supplies materials and equipment, but your personal toolkit is expected from day one.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of maintenance experience at a multifamily community of 100 or more units
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, HVAC, and appliance repair (stoves, refrigerators, washers, dryers)
  • Familiarity with basic electrical repairs is a plus
  • Your own hand tools and the safe-use knowledge that goes with them
  • A valid driver's license
  • Strong communication habits, both with residents and with your team
  • The kind of attitude that keeps resident interactions calm and respectful, even on a stressful day

The Bigger Picture

Investment Property Group is headquartered in Park City, Utah, and manages roughly 150 properties across 13 states, spanning multifamily, manufactured home, and RV communities. That scale matters for your career: technicians who perform well in roles like this one often move toward lead maintenance or maintenance supervisor positions as the company continues to grow. IPG has properties in multiple markets, so geographic mobility, if that's something you're open to, can open additional doors.

Pay runs $24 to $28 per hour depending on your background, with a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life insurance, an HSA, and an employee assistance program. There's also a 401(k) with company match and four weeks of accrued PTO. For a maintenance technician role, that's a solid overall package, and it reflects the kind of investment IPG says it makes in the people who keep its communities running day to day.

If you're someone who takes real satisfaction in a clean punch list and residents who feel genuinely taken care of, this role has that built into it. Affordable housing communities tend to have residents who rely on responsive maintenance more than most. The work you do here is noticed.

job.title: Service Technician - Zerzura
job.description:
The Technical Skills This Role Puts to Work Every Day

Maintenance work at a well-run apartment community is less about waiting for things to break and more about moving through a structured day with real technical depth. At Zerzura in Las Vegas, this role draws on hands-on proficiency across at least two trades. Plumbing, HVAC, electrical, appliance repair, carpentry: the expectation is that you arrive already competent in your core areas and build from there. AIR Communities uses technology to route and prioritize work orders, which means less time figuring out what to do next and more time actually resolving issues.

Las Vegas puts specific demands on HVAC systems. The climate is unforgiving, and cooling equipment that runs hard through a long desert summer generates a predictable volume of service requests. Technicians who understand mechanical systems at more than a surface level tend to stand out here, both because the call volume is real and because residents notice quickly when comfort issues go unresolved.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Complete apartment turns according to AIR's make-ready process, getting units to move-in condition for incoming residents
  • Diagnose and repair resident-reported issues across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and appliances with general direction from leadership
  • Participate in on-call rotation, including at least one week per month, with reliable transportation required for after-hours emergency response
  • Assist with move-in and move-out inspections and vendor quality checks as needed
  • Support newer technicians with technical guidance and skill development where your experience allows

Responsibilities shift with the season, community needs, and your individual skill set. Expect the scope to flex.

What AIR Brings to This Role

The base pay starts at $22.00 per hour, and there's a quarterly customer service bonus structure that can add up to $250 per month for technicians who consistently earn positive resident feedback. That's a meaningful supplement, and it reflects how seriously AIR ties compensation to the resident experience.

The 50% rent discount at any AIR community is a genuine differentiator if you're open to living onsite or nearby. On-call shifts are easier to manage when your commute is measured in minutes or eliminated entirely.

AIR's Ascend maintenance development program is worth noting for anyone thinking about where this role leads. Maintenance Technician to Lead Technician to Service Manager is a well-worn path at larger operators, and AIR states a preference for internal promotion. The tuition reimbursement and certification coverage support that trajectory in a concrete way.

Strong candidates for this role will have two or more years of facilities or residential maintenance experience, real proficiency in multiple trades, and the kind of temperament that handles a full work order queue without cutting corners on quality. The ability to close out a punch list completely, not just partially, separates the technicians who advance from those who stay flat.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a full P&L role. As Community Manager at Cortland's Austin property, you carry the NOI target and own everything that affects it: occupancy, delinquency, expense control, vendor contracts, and the leasing pipeline. Your days move between financial review and floor-level decisions. One morning you're analyzing T-3 traffic trends and coaching a leasing consultant on conversion technique; that afternoon you're walking the property for a punch list inspection or sitting with a resident to resolve an escalated concern. The operational and financial threads don't separate cleanly, and that's the point.

On the revenue side, you'll set leasing goals, monitor KPIs, and build the kind of sales culture where follow-up is disciplined and closing rates reflect it. Cortland operates as a vertically integrated company with in-house design, construction, and operations, which means you'll work with centralized support teams rather than coordinating everything through third-party vendors. That structure gives you more resources than a typical fee management shop, but it also means you're accountable to more stakeholders. Communicating up and across the organization is a real part of the job.

What You Bring

  • At least 2 years of sales leadership experience in a high-velocity, short-cycle environment. Multifamily is the obvious fit, but Cortland also values backgrounds in hospitality, luxury retail, or premium automotive where closing speed and customer experience both matter.
  • Demonstrated results hitting occupancy and revenue targets, with the data to back it up.
  • Financial acumen that goes beyond reading a report: budgeting, forecasting, and knowing where to cut without sacrificing resident experience or curb appeal.
  • Proven ability to build and develop a team, not just manage one. Coaching leasing staff toward consistent performance is central to this role.
  • Comfort with property management software, CRM systems, and using social media as a legitimate marketing channel.
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred.

Where This Role Leads

Community Manager is the role where generalist PM skills sharpen into something more specific and transferable. You're building a track record with a named NOI target at a top-10 multifamily owner. That matters when you're ready to move into a regional or multi-site role. The skills that compound fastest here: financial fluency at the asset level, team development, and the ability to read market conditions and adjust pricing or concessions accordingly. Austin's multifamily market has seen real rent pressure and elevated concessions in recent cycles, so managing through softness while protecting NOI is a skill set that travels well beyond any single market. Managers who come out of Cortland's platform with clean financials and strong retention numbers tend to be competitive candidates at the portfolio and regional level.

job.title: Lead Maintenance Technician - Avion
job.description:
Bozeman's rental market has tightened considerably over the past several years, and well-run communities here carry real operational weight. This Lead Maintenance Technician role at Olympus Property's Avion community puts you in charge of the full maintenance operation, from daily service request flow to turn-key scheduling to contractor coordination. For someone who's ready to own a maintenance department rather than just work in one, this is the step that changes your career trajectory.

What You'll Actually Do

The core of this role is keeping a residential community running at a high standard across every system: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, pool equipment, irrigation, and building exteriors. You'll schedule and lead the maintenance team's daily, weekly, and monthly workloads, manage vendor relationships with outside contractors, and keep the shop stocked, organized, and inspection-ready. Make-ready operations fall under your oversight, and you'll work directly with the property's Business Manager to ensure vacant units are show-ready before move-in. Monthly, quarterly, and annual property inspections are part of the rhythm, and you'll track service requests, inventory, and completed work through property management software.

You'll also carry a hiring and development responsibility. Building your service team, training them, and setting the standard for how maintenance work gets done here is part of the job description, and Olympus takes that seriously.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of residential or apartment maintenance experience, with some time in a supervisory or lead capacity
  • EPA/HVAC certification (required)
  • Comfort managing both the hands-on technical work and the scheduling and coordination side of operations
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM, with on-call rotation
  • Experience working with software systems for tracking work orders and inventory

Where This Role Leads

Lead Maintenance Technician is where a lot of strong maintenance careers start compounding quickly. The skills you build here, specifically team development, contractor management, budget-conscious purchasing, and working cross-functionally with leasing and management staff, are exactly what Service Director and Regional Maintenance roles require. Olympus explicitly offers career pathing as part of their structure, which means the path forward isn't just theoretical.

Compensation runs $30 to $35 per hour depending on experience, with monthly and quarterly bonuses on top of base pay. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, and sabbatical eligibility. Olympus has earned recognition from the National Apartment Association as a top employer three consecutive years, which reflects something real about how they run their teams.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - EPA Certified
job.description:
Maintenance technicians at apartment communities wear a lot of hats. On any given day you're pulling work orders, troubleshooting a tricky HVAC unit, helping knock out a turn, and fielding a call from a resident who's convinced their garbage disposal is a plumbing emergency. At Bexley at Anderson Mill, Weinstein Properties is hiring an EPA-certified Maintenance Technician to handle exactly that kind of work, at a well-maintained community with a full-time maintenance team behind you.

What the Work Looks Like

The core of this role is work orders: repairs in occupied units covering HVAC, electrical, plumbing, appliances, and carpentry. You'll also support apartment turns and make-readies, which means punching through lists efficiently so units are rent-ready on schedule. Beyond the apartments themselves, you'll help keep the grounds, amenities, and pool areas in good shape. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, with participation in a rotating emergency on-call rotation. On-call weeks pay an additional $150 regardless of whether calls come in, plus $150 extra for holiday coverage.

The starting rate is $22/hour and can go higher depending on experience. There's also a quarterly bonus tied to property and team performance, up to $980. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, PTO, paid holidays, a birthday day off, a rent discount, and an employee assistance program.

What Weinstein Expects

  • At least 3 years of apartment or residential maintenance experience
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required, not preferred)
  • Hands-on HVAC troubleshooting and repair skills
  • Comfort with work order systems and basic computer use
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs and work indoors and outdoors year-round
  • Reliable transportation and a valid background check

The customer service piece matters here. Residents notice how technicians communicate, not just whether the repair was done right. A strong candidate knows how to leave a unit better than they found it and close out a work order without a callback.

The Weinstein Difference

Weinstein Properties owns and manages its communities in-house. That structure tends to produce more consistent maintenance standards and clearer lines of communication than third-party management, where priorities can shift with ownership changes. It also means advancement paths are real. Technicians who perform well here have moved into lead and supervisor roles, because the company has properties to staff and prefers to promote from within.

The honest part: rotating on-call means some late nights and weekend calls. That's the job. The $150 weekly on-call pay and the team rotation are designed to make it manageable, but if on-call is a dealbreaker for you, this role won't change that.
