MidPen is looking for someone who can support site teams without creating dependency. That means coaching on-site staff toward better documentation habits, better preventive maintenance follow-through, and cleaner common areas, while also jumping in physically when coverage gaps appear. This is a working lead position. You'll be doing make-readies, painting, plumbing repairs, appliance servicing, and grounds work alongside the teams you're supporting.

  • Coordinate and assist with unit inspections, safety inspections, and pre-agency inspections across the region
  • Prepare vacated units for re-occupancy: cleaning, painting, appliance servicing, and finish repairs
  • Direct contractors and service providers, and contribute input toward preventive maintenance program improvements and long-term capital planning
  • Cover maintenance operations at sites during staff absences
  • Maintain inventory control of tools, equipment, and supplies across properties
  • Ensure work orders are accurately completed, closed, and documented; assist with utility routing and shutoff documentation
  • Serve as a resource to site staff on fire and life safety items, training, and special projects

Emergency response comes with the territory. Evening and weekend calls are part of this role, and you'll need a valid California driver's license, reliable transportation, and current auto insurance to travel between properties regularly.

What Makes a Strong Candidate Here

MidPen's portfolio spans more than 130 properties across Northern California, housing working families, seniors, and residents with special needs. Affordable housing maintenance carries compliance layers that market-rate portfolios don't. Candidates who've worked in regulated affordable housing and have direct experience with REAC, TCAC, or MOR inspections will be several steps ahead. Three years of supervisory experience overseeing crews and managing turnovers at multiple sites is required, not preferred.

The stronger candidates we've seen in roles like this bring a coaching mindset. You're not just fixing things. You're also raising the baseline quality of the teams around you, which takes patience and genuine communication skills. MidPen's mission focus is real, and residents here often have fewer options and more vulnerabilities than the typical renter. That context shapes how maintenance work gets done.

Pay ranges from $34.62 to $38.94 per hour depending on experience, with benefits including health, dental, vision, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, and an employee education reimbursement program.

job.title: Leasing and Experience Manager (Carson & Raleigh)
job.description:
Where Leasing Skill Meets Community Leadership

Most leasing roles ask you to close traffic and hand off the relationship. This one asks you to own it. Prometheus Real Estate Group, a vertically integrated owner-operator with over 13,000 apartments across the Bay Area, Portland, and Seattle, runs its communities under a resident-experience model that treats occupancy as a byproduct of genuine connection, not just conversion. The Leasing and Experience Manager role at their Carson and Raleigh communities in Portland sits at the center of that philosophy, combining sales production, team supervision, and hands-on community programming in a single position.

The title matters here. Where other operators use "Assistant Property Manager" or "Assistant Business Manager," Prometheus has built a distinct role that blends leasing performance with resident relations and team development. You'll close leases and coach others to close them. You'll manage delinquency and concessions alongside planning resident events and following up on service concerns. You'll contribute to occupancy reporting and pricing strategy while also being the person residents trust when something goes wrong. That breadth is the point.

What This Role Requires and What It Builds

To step into this position well, you need at least two years of leasing experience and a genuine comfort with sales. You should already know how to read traffic, handle objections, and move a prospect through a showing to a signed lease. Strong written and verbal communication is assumed. So is reliability on weekends, which is when Portland apartment communities see their highest foot traffic and when your presence on-site is most valuable.

What the role builds is different. Managing a leasing team, even a small one, develops supervisory instincts that carry into Community Manager and Regional roles. Setting goals, running training, and celebrating milestones are skills that compound over time. The exposure to pricing, concessions, and occupancy reporting gives you a working vocabulary in operational metrics that most leasing-only positions never offer. Candidates who move from this role into property management leadership typically point to exactly this kind of dual exposure as the reason they were ready.

A few things that separate strong candidates from average ones in a role like this: the ability to shift register quickly, from a sales conversation with a prospect to a difficult follow-up with a current resident to a coaching moment with a junior leasing ambassador, all in the same afternoon. Prometheus operates with a defined resident experience standard, and maintaining that standard under the pressure of a busy weekend requires composure, not just enthusiasm.

  • Minimum two years of leasing experience required
  • High school diploma or GED required; bachelor's degree preferred
  • Weekend availability is a consistent schedule requirement
  • Experience in customer service, sales, or marketing is valued
  • Supervisory or team lead experience is a plus, though not stated as required

Compensation runs $29.75 to $31.75 per hour, with a $200 per-lease incentive, weekend shift premium pay, and a discretionary semi-annual bonus. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, vision, and dental coverage for eligible employees and dependents, 401(k) with employer matching, tenure-based housing discounts, and tuition reimbursement, among others.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
A resident calls at 9 a.m. with a billing question. By 10, you're posting rent payments and flagging a delinquent account for follow-up. By noon, you've toured two prospects and handed off a lease application to process. That's a normal Tuesday in this role.

The Position

Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring an Assistant Community Manager at The Park at North Ridge, a community in North Raleigh off Claxton Circle. Hawthorne ranks among the top 50 multifamily management companies nationally, with a Southeast-focused portfolio and a reputation for promoting from within.

This role sits at the intersection of leasing, resident relations, and financial administration. You'll support the Community Manager on daily operations and step into a lead role when they're out. The work is varied: one hour you're conducting a leasing tour, the next you're reconciling a ledger or making delinquency follow-up calls.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Conducting tours, responding to leads, and guiding prospects through the full leasing process
  • Processing lease applications, renewals, and related documents accurately and on time
  • Posting rent payments, scanning checks, and monitoring delinquency with weekly follow-up
  • Reviewing resident ledgers to verify billing accuracy and payment application
  • Assisting with financial reporting for the Community Manager and regional leadership
  • Managing the community's social media presence, including resident events and engagement content
  • Maintaining the office, amenities, and common areas to a clean, presentable standard
  • Handling resident concerns professionally and following through to resolution

The office is open Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., and Saturdays, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. One weekday off is provided weekly to maintain a 40-hour schedule. Some evening and weekend availability may be needed for resident events.

What You Bring

Hawthorne prefers candidates with at least two years of property management experience. Prior time in an assistant manager role (six months or more) is a plus. A valid driver's license is required. A CALP designation is a nice-to-have but not a dealbreaker.

The candidates who do well here aren't just strong with people. They can read a ledger, spot a billing error, and have a direct conversation with a resident about a past-due balance without it becoming a conflict. Financial literacy and interpersonal confidence carry equal weight in this role.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

Hawthorne also runs a formal Career Path Program. Assistant Community Manager to Community Manager is a common progression here, and the company's Learning and Development team actively supports that track.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
A resident submits a ticket at 7 a.m. about a heating issue. By the time the leasing office opens, you've already diagnosed a failed blower motor, ordered the part, and left a note under the door. That's the pace and the standard this role runs on.

What This Role Covers

Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant Maintenance Manager for a residential property in Oakland. The salary range is $79,000 to $85,000, with additional bonus opportunities. This is a hands-on leadership position, meaning you're both doing the work and setting the tone for how the team does it.

Day to day, you'll resolve service requests across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair. You'll own the make-ready and turn process, keeping units moving through punch list and back to leasable condition on schedule. Preventative maintenance programs fall under your watch, as does general upkeep, grounds maintenance, and compliance with building, county, and OSHA safety codes. Weekend shifts and participation in the emergency on-call rotation are part of the job.

This role also carries real supervisory weight. You'll lead by example, motivate your team, and hold the operation to a high standard of professionalism and safety. Bozzuto places genuine emphasis on resident experience, so timely follow-up on service tickets and clear communication with residents matter as much as technical skill.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Five or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • Supervisory experience, or a demonstrated ability to lead and motivate a crew
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Hands-on proficiency across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems such as boilers, chillers, central plant, or split systems is a plus
  • Knowledge of OSHA, risk management, and MSDS protocols
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office and property technology platforms
  • Physical ability to handle the demands of the role: lifting up to 50 pounds, climbing ladders, working in varied weather

The candidates who tend to thrive in roles like this one combine technical range with accountability. Knowing how to fix something is table stakes. Knowing how to document it, follow up with the resident, and train someone else to do it correctly next time is what separates a good tech from a strong assistant manager.

From a career trajectory standpoint, this position is a well-worn path toward a Maintenance Manager or Chief Engineer role. The supervisory exposure you build here, combined with Bozzuto's scale across multiple markets, gives you both the credentials and the internal network to move up. Bozzuto also offers tuition reimbursement and career development programs, which matter if you're working toward additional certifications or want to broaden into property operations leadership.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Community Relations Manager
job.description:
This role sits at the intersection of sales execution and operational ownership. The skills that matter most here aren't soft ones. They're measurable: conversion rate, pipeline velocity, follow-up discipline, occupancy contribution. If you've built a book of business in a short-cycle sales environment and you understand that a missed follow-up is a missed lease, this role will feel familiar.

What Skills Drive This Role

Consultative selling is the core competency. At a Cortland community, you're not processing applications. You're qualifying traffic, identifying what a prospective resident actually needs, and presenting a value proposition that closes. That means CRM hygiene matters. Pipeline health matters. Conversion metrics get tracked, and you're expected to know yours.

On the operational side, this position supports the Community Manager across daily site functions: inspections of vacant units and make-ready apartments, move-in and move-out walkthroughs, curb appeal monitoring, vendor coordination, and compliance with Fair Housing and OSHA requirements. You're keeping the physical asset aligned with brand standards while simultaneously managing an active leasing pipeline. That's a real dual-track workload, and strong candidates treat both tracks with equal discipline.

Resident experience rounds out the skill set. Planning and executing community events, managing social media presence, handling resident concerns with professionalism and urgency. These aren't soft extras. At Class A communities, resident retention directly affects NOI. A resident who renews is cheaper than a turn.

Qualifications

  • 2 or more years of documented sales success in a high-velocity, short-cycle environment (multifamily, luxury hospitality, premium automotive, timeshare, or similar)
  • Demonstrated ability to meet or exceed leasing goals, conversion targets, and KPIs
  • Experience managing a sales pipeline with disciplined follow-up and accurate CRM records
  • Proficiency in property management software, CRM platforms, and Microsoft Office
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including social media marketing
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred
  • Ability to handle resident concerns with empathy and urgency under pressure

Why This Role at Cortland

Cortland operates as a vertically integrated platform. Design, construction, and management all run in-house. That structure means the people managing communities have more direct access to resources and fewer layers between a problem and a solution. For someone in this role, that translates to real operational support and genuine autonomy to execute.

Nashville's multifamily market has absorbed significant new supply over the past several years, which puts real pressure on traffic-to-lease conversion. Strong candidates in this market know how to differentiate on experience and service quality when concessions alone aren't enough to close. The skill of turning a hesitant prospect into a signed lease through genuine relationship-building, not just price, is what separates average leasing performers from top ones. That's the skill set Cortland is hiring for here.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the operational center of commercial property management. You'll support the Property Manager across a property or small portfolio that may include office, retail, or industrial assets in the Wakefield, MA area. The work spans financial reporting, lease administration, vendor oversight, and tenant relations simultaneously, and you're expected to hold multiple threads without dropping any.

On the financial side, you'll help prepare monthly reports and budget packages, review vendor invoices for accuracy and compliance with the management agreement, and take the lead on collecting data and drafting CAM and operating expense reconciliations in coordination with the accounting team. Lease administration is a core function here: setting up leases in applicable systems, processing changes, and keeping reporting current. You'll also coordinate tenant move-ins and move-outs, participate in walk-throughs, and contribute to emergency preparedness planning. Vendor bidding and procurement support round out the scope. This is a 100% in-office position at the property.

What You Bring

  • A bachelor's degree or a combination of education and hands-on experience that adds up to real commercial property knowledge
  • One to two years in commercial real estate operations, with exposure to office, retail, or industrial preferred
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel for financial calculations and reporting
  • Familiarity with accounts payable and CMMS platforms
  • The ability to read and work with financial terms: percentages, reconciliations, basic variance analysis
  • Clear written and verbal communication, especially when addressing tenant concerns or coordinating with vendors
  • Strong organizational habits and a track record of delivering on deadlines

Where This Role Fits in the Craft

The assistant property manager position in commercial management is genuinely a proving ground. The skills you'll use from day one include tenant communication, invoice review, and lease administration accuracy. The skills you'll build here are harder to teach: reading a T-12 with enough context to ask the right questions, managing vendor relationships under budget pressure, and developing the judgment to escalate a tenant issue versus handle it yourself. Those are the instincts that distinguish a strong APM candidate from someone who can follow a checklist.

Lincoln Property Company operates at significant scale nationally, which means you're working within established systems and processes while still having room to grow. For someone who wants to move toward a full Property Manager role on commercial assets, this kind of structured environment with mentorship and training access is a practical path forward. The CAM reconciliation work alone, done well, builds a skill set that translates directly to any commercial PM role regardless of asset type.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role covers the full resident lifecycle at one of Weinstein Properties' Nashville communities. You'll work leads coming in through phone and internet, schedule and conduct tours, process applications, and put lease files together from start to finish. Once residents move in, you stay involved: renewals, transfers, pet addendums, account questions, and the occasional difficult conversation about a balance owed. When someone moves out, you handle the processing and the security deposit disposition. Rent posting and delinquency follow-up are part of your regular rotation too.

You'll also spend time coordinating with maintenance. That means walking apartments after turns to confirm make-ready punch lists are complete, checking in on work orders, and keeping residents informed when repairs are in progress. Resident events fall to this position as well, from planning through execution.

Weinstein operates with a hands-on philosophy that's been consistent across 70-plus years of family ownership. That shows up in how this role is structured: you're expected to be visible on the property, not parked at a desk. The schedule runs weekdays 9 to 6, with Saturdays on a team rotation (9 to 5), and Sundays off.

What You Bring

  • Prior property management experience is genuinely a plus, but Weinstein will consider candidates from hospitality, retail management, or sales who have handled real customer escalations and some team responsibility
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to hold a firm but professional conversation when a resident situation gets tense
  • Comfort with shifting priorities mid-day. This is a role where a prospect tour, a maintenance call, and a move-out question can all land on you within the same hour
  • Some leadership experience, even informal. You'll help train team members and support the property manager on operations
  • Attention to detail when processing paperwork. Lease files, deposit dispositions, and account ledgers all require accuracy

Nashville Market and Growth Context

Nashville's apartment market has seen significant lease-up activity over the past several years, and competition for residents across the Class A and B segments remains real. Weinstein operates multiple communities in the area, and they're offering placement flexibility based on where you live or which part of the market you know. Starting pay comes in at $24 per hour with room to increase based on experience, plus quarterly bonuses. Benefits include a rent discount, health, dental and vision coverage, 401k with company match, paid holidays, and birthday time off.

A strong candidate for this role will already know how to read a resident's frustration and de-escalate without losing ground on policy. That skill, combined with solid leasing instincts, is what typically accelerates the path from assistant to property manager at operators like Weinstein. Many of their current site leaders started in leasing or assistant roles and moved up from there.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Atwood Apartments
job.description:
Leasing is a skills game. The best consultants in this business know how to read a prospect in the first two minutes, qualify them efficiently, and close without pressure. They also know that occupancy doesn't maintain itself: it's the product of consistent traffic, tight follow-up, and a leasing office that runs clean. That's the kind of role this is at Atwood Apartments in Citrus Heights.

The Skills This Role Runs On

Sales acumen sits at the center of this position. You're greeting prospects, walking units, and guiding people through one of the bigger financial decisions they'll make this year. The conversion side matters: traffic without lease execution doesn't move the needle on occupancy. Alongside that, customer service runs parallel the entire time. Existing residents come to you with maintenance concerns, payment questions, and complaints. How you handle those interactions directly affects retention, and retention is just as important to NOI as new leases.

Administrative precision is the third leg. Rental files need to stay current and accurate. Lease documents have to be prepared correctly and signed before keys change hands. Data entry into the property management system has to be right the first time. Errors in rental records create downstream problems that are expensive to fix.

Day-to-Day at Atwood

A typical day moves between leasing activity and resident interaction. You might spend the morning qualifying applicants and coordinating with maintenance on an upcoming move-in, making sure the unit is ready and the new resident's experience starts well. The afternoon brings walk-ins, follow-up calls, and lease prep. Monthly admin tasks round things out: paperwork organization, reporting, and keeping the office's records in order.

MG Properties has been operating across the Western U.S. for over 30 years, with a track record in acquisition, development, and management. They promote from within, which means a leasing role here has real upward mobility. Consultants who build a strong foundation in leasing, traffic conversion, and resident relations often move into assistant manager and property manager roles. The skills transfer directly: you're already living in the same metrics.

What MG Properties Is Offering

  • $22 to $24 per hour, depending on experience
  • Monthly and quarterly bonuses
  • Company profit sharing
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Employee Assistance Program and life insurance
  • Flexible Spending Account and Dependent Care Spending Account
  • 10 days PTO, 10 paid holidays, 2 personal days, and 40 hours paid sick time annually
  • Rental discounts

A minimum of one year in property management is preferred. Strong sales instincts, professional communication, and the ability to stay organized under a busy leasing office workload are what separate candidates who thrive here from those who struggle. If your follow-up is sharp and your paperwork is clean, this is a role worth pursuing.

job.title: Property Administrator
job.description:
A tenant calls about a billing discrepancy. A vendor needs a contract reviewed. A new tenant is moving in and needs onboarding paperwork. That's a Tuesday morning for the Property Administrator at Prometheus Real Estate Group's Walnut Creek commercial office. This role sits at the center of daily operations, and it moves fast.

What the Job Covers

Prometheus is the largest privately held apartment owner in the Bay Area, with over 13,000 units across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle. Their commercial team manages a separate portfolio, and this role supports that operation out of Walnut Creek. The scope is wider than a typical admin position.

On the financial side, you'll code accounts payable, review accounts receivable, handle rent billing, track operating expenses, and monitor budgets for accuracy and variance. You'll also prepare and review contracts and maintain insurance policy records. Basic accounting knowledge is expected. You don't need a CPA, but you do need to read a ledger and catch errors before they become problems.

On the operations side, you're the first contact for tenants, vendors, and visitors. You manage the office itself, including supplies, team coordination, and policy documentation. You'll also support the broader commercial team with reporting and administrative tasks as they come up.

This is a full-cycle administrative role. Financial accuracy and strong communication carry equal weight here.

What Prometheus Expects

  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred
  • At least two years in an office administration role; property administration experience preferred
  • One to two years in residential or commercial property management
  • At least one year handling accounts payable, accounts receivable, invoicing, and billing
  • Strong Excel skills and comfort with basic accounting principles
  • Clear written and verbal communication under pressure
  • Ability to manage competing priorities without losing accuracy on detail work

Compensation runs $33.50 to $42.00 per hour depending on experience, plus a discretionary annual bonus. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision (dependents included), 401(k) with employer match, 12 paid holidays including your birthday, tuition reimbursement, and tenure-based housing discounts, among others.

Strong candidates in this type of role tend to be people who treat financial accuracy as non-negotiable and who communicate proactively rather than waiting to be asked. The volume of interruptions in a commercial property office is real. If you lose focus every time the phone rings, the billing reconciliation suffers. The people who thrive here manage both without letting either slip.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Most multifamily communities run on two people: the Community Manager and whoever's standing next to them. That second seat is the Assistant Community Manager, and at a property like Avenues of West Ashley, it carries real operational weight. This isn't a purely leasing-focused role. It spans leasing, resident relations, delinquency follow-up, ledger accuracy, and stepping in to run the community when the manager is out.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On a typical day, you might start by reviewing the delinquency report and making follow-up calls before the leasing office opens at 9. From there, you're fielding prospect traffic, conducting tours, and making sure applications and renewal paperwork move through cleanly. Afternoons can shift quickly: a resident dispute at the front desk, a ledger discrepancy to sort out, or social media content to schedule for an upcoming community event. Saturdays are part of the schedule (10 AM to 4 PM), and occasional evenings come with the territory when resident events are on the calendar. None of that is unusual for this level of role, but it's worth knowing upfront.

The financial side is more involved than most ACM postings suggest. You'll handle rent collection, payment posting, check scanning, and weekly delinquency outreach. You'll conduct ledger reviews to catch billing errors and payment misapplications before they become bigger problems. When eviction procedures are necessary, you'll coordinate those too. Hawthorne expects you to understand what you're looking at in a financial report, not just hand it off to the manager.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • At least two years of property management experience, with some time already spent in an assistant manager or senior leasing capacity
  • Comfort handling delinquency conversations directly with residents, without escalating unnecessarily
  • Ability to run the community independently when the manager is unavailable
  • Attention to detail on lease documents, renewals, and account ledgers
  • Valid driver's license; CALP designation is a plus but not required

Hawthorne sits among the 50 largest multifamily operators in the country, with roots in the Southeast. They offer a defined career path program, so the ACM role here has a clear next step toward Community Manager. Monthly leasing and renewal commissions, plus quarterly performance bonuses, supplement the hourly base. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid parental leave, and pet insurance, among others.

Charleston's rental market has stayed competitive, and West Ashley has absorbed significant multifamily inventory over the past several years. Keeping occupancy strong at a community on Ashley River Road means leasing performance and resident retention both matter. The ACM who understands how renewals protect NOI will outperform one who only thinks about new traffic.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (Watermark at Jordan Creek)
job.description:
Watermark at Jordan Creek is a residential property in West Des Moines managed by BAM Companies, a firm that's been operating since 2010 with a hands-on approach to both property operations and team culture. This is a full-time maintenance technician role working directly on the property: handling work orders, running preventative maintenance, and keeping the community in solid shape for residents day to day.

The work covers the usual range for a residential maintenance tech. HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and structural repairs all fall within scope. You'll also be responsible for exterior upkeep and common areas, not just unit interiors. Preventative maintenance gets documented and tracked, which means you're staying ahead of problems rather than just reacting to them. After-hours emergency coverage is part of the job, so expect occasional on-call responsibility.

Pay runs $17 to $19 per hour depending on experience. The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision with BAM covering a significant share of the premium, paid life insurance, rent discounts at BAM properties, and PTO that starts building after 90 days with a jump at the one-year mark.

What they're looking for

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 2 to 3 years of hands-on maintenance experience
  • Valid driver's license
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (preferred, not required)
  • Comfort working independently and managing a work order queue without close supervision
  • Clear communication with both residents and team members

One thing worth knowing: the technicians who stand out in roles like this aren't just the ones who can fix things fast. They're the ones who notice the slow drain before it backs up, the HVAC filter that's overdue, the door hinge that's pulling loose. Preventative instincts matter more than raw speed, especially on a property where deferred maintenance compounds quickly and resident satisfaction is tied directly to how responsive the team feels.

West Des Moines has seen steady residential growth, and well-maintained communities in this market hold occupancy well. For a tech looking to grow, this kind of role builds the hands-on breadth that leads naturally toward a lead tech or maintenance supervisor position over time.

job.title: Floating Property Manager
job.description:
Floating property manager roles exist because portfolios don't break down neatly. Vacancies at one property, a manager out on leave at another, a lease-up that needs steadying hands on deck. Berkshire Residential Investments built this position to keep operations moving across its East Coast portfolio, and the person who fills it ends up with something most site-level managers never get: a wide-angle view of how multiple assets run at once.

What This Role Actually Covers

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means the floating manager here answers to an internal ownership structure rather than a third-party fee management arrangement. That distinction matters. Decisions carry more weight, and the reporting lines connect more directly to asset performance. You'll work alongside the Assistant Vice President on annual budgets, monthly and quarterly forecasts, staffing plans, and capital planning. You'll also take point on hiring, training, and performance management at each property you cover, which means you need to be able to build trust with a team quickly and hand things off cleanly.

Day-to-day, this role shifts between the operational and the financial. One morning you might be running through a T-12 to understand why NOI is trailing projections at a property. Another afternoon might involve working through a delinquency report or coaching a leasing consultant on traffic conversion. Resident communications, marketing plans, and social content are also in scope. The expectation is that you read a property's condition fast and know which levers to pull.

Travel across multiple locations is a core requirement, not an occasional ask. The preference is for someone based on the East Coast, with a particular lean toward the Washington, DC area.

Who Compounds Well in This Role

Five years of multifamily experience is the baseline. More specifically, the people who thrive here have already managed through a full budget cycle, read a financial statement without needing it translated, and led a team through a rough patch without losing the room. The ability to move between properties without losing your footing is a skill in itself, and it tends to separate candidates who've worked across different asset classes or dealt with varied team dynamics from those who've only ever run one site.

From a career trajectory standpoint, floating manager experience is one of the cleaner on-ramps to a regional property manager role. You're already operating at a multi-property level, thinking about staffing and budgets across a portfolio, and building relationships with senior leadership. Candidates who take this role seriously and document what they learn tend to move into regional or district-level positions with a significantly stronger foundation than peers who moved up through a single-site path.

  • Five or more years in multifamily property management
  • Demonstrated experience with budgeting and financial reporting
  • Comfort managing teams across different properties and cultures
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Proficiency with property management software and financial tools
  • Willingness and ability to travel regularly to multiple locations
  • East Coast base preferred, Washington, DC area ideal

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, and personal development plans, among other benefits listed in their full offer package.

job.title: Leasing & Sales Consultant-Cortland at the Village
job.description:
Cortland at the Village in Smyrna, GA is looking for a Leasing and Sales Consultant to own the front-end of the leasing cycle at a community that sits within one of the more active suburban submarkets in metro Atlanta. This is a sales role. If you're more comfortable with paperwork than phone calls, it's probably not the right fit.

What You'll Actually Do

Your day runs on traffic and conversion. You'll work a pipeline of prospects through the CRM, following up consistently and moving leads toward signed leases. Consultative selling is the expectation here, meaning you're asking questions, identifying what a prospect actually needs, and matching them to the right unit rather than just reading off a rent sheet. You'll handle objections, track your own metrics, and stay accountable to occupancy and conversion KPIs.

Beyond closing leases, you'll manage the resident-facing experience through the move-in process, support community events and resident engagement programs, and keep the community's social media presence active. Cortland operates at a brand standard that expects a polished, consistent presentation across every touchpoint.

  • Achieve and exceed leasing goals and conversion targets
  • Maintain accurate CRM records and monitor lead activity and pipeline health
  • Guide prospects through the full leasing process with a concierge-level approach
  • Handle objections and follow up with discipline and consistency
  • Support marketing programs, social media, and resident events
  • Implement coaching and feedback quickly

What You Bring

  • At least six months of sales, customer-facing, or performance-driven experience
  • Comfort being held to measurable goals and tracked against them
  • Strong follow-up habits and genuine time management discipline
  • Confidence building rapport quickly with a range of people
  • Coachability and a willingness to adjust your approach when the market or leadership calls for it
  • Familiarity with CRM platforms, or the aptitude to learn one quickly
  • A professional presentation that aligns with a premium brand standard

Context Worth Knowing

Cortland is a vertically integrated owner-operator, one of the largest in the country, which means decisions about design, capital, and operations largely stay in-house. For a leasing consultant, that translates to a more structured environment with defined processes and real performance expectations. The Smyrna location puts you in a market with solid demand drivers, but occupancy is earned, not assumed.

What separates strong leasing consultants at a company like Cortland from average ones usually comes down to follow-up discipline. The tours are easy. Staying organized across a full pipeline, following up on day two and day five, and actually closing the leads that went quiet, that's where occupancy is built or lost. If you've got that habit already, you'll move up fast. Cortland promotes from within, and leasing consultants who perform consistently tend to have a clear path toward assistant manager and beyond.

job.title: Property Coordinator
job.description:
Commercial property coordinators sit at the intersection of tenant relations, financial recordkeeping, and vendor oversight. At a firm managing hundreds of millions of square feet across institutional portfolios, that coordination role carries real weight. Lincoln Property Company's San Francisco office is hiring a Property Coordinator to keep the day-to-day mechanics of on-site commercial management running cleanly.

San Francisco's commercial office market has been under significant pressure since 2020, with elevated vacancy across Class A and B buildings pushing owners to tighten operational discipline. In that environment, accurate invoice tracking, timely delinquency reporting, and solid vendor compliance aren't back-office niceties. They're core to protecting NOI on assets where every dollar is scrutinized.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A typical week in this role pulls in several directions at once. You'll be the first point of contact when tenants call the management office, which means routing issues quickly and knowing when to escalate. Purchase orders move through Workspace from issuance to payment, and you're responsible for tracking them, coding invoices, and flagging anything that stalls. The Chief Engineer will rely on you to update the electrical analysis worksheet as utility invoices arrive, so comfort with spreadsheet work and attention to detail on utility data matters here.

On the financial side, you'll apply tenant rents and open credits, compile tenant billings and miscellaneous charges, and generate aged delinquency reports for the management team. Sending late letters is part of the job. So is helping prepare and administer service agreements and monitoring vendor certificates of insurance for contract compliance. Beyond the financial and vendor work, you'll also coordinate tenant-facing events like holiday gatherings, welcome lunches, and community drives. It's a genuinely broad scope for a coordinator-level role.

What Lincoln Is Looking For

  • At least two years of commercial property management experience
  • Familiarity with MRI, Workspace, and Yardi
  • Working knowledge of accounts payable, accounts receivable, and the monthly commercial accounting cycle
  • Comfort reading commercial leases and understanding how lease terms connect to tenant billing
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
  • High school diploma required; associate's or bachelor's degree preferred
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation

This position is fully in-office during standard business hours. Remote or hybrid arrangements are not available.

Candidates who stand out in roles like this typically bring one thing that's hard to teach: the ability to hold multiple open loops simultaneously without letting any of them drop. Purchase orders, vendor compliance tracking, delinquency follow-up, and event logistics don't pause for each other. The coordinators who thrive are the ones who've already built systems for staying current across all of it, not just the parts they find interesting.

Pay range for this role is $30 to $32 per hour. Lincoln's benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k), and paid time off.

job.title: Business Manager - Elan
job.description:
Olympus Property runs a tight ship on the operations side, and the Business Manager role at Elan in Austin reflects that. This is a full property management position: financials, team oversight, leasing performance, and asset condition all sit on your desk at once.

What the Job Covers

You'll own the day-to-day and month-to-month performance of the property. That means building and managing budgets, tracking occupancy and delinquency, and reviewing financials with your Regional Manager and Regional VP on a regular cadence. Annual business plans and budget forecasts are part of your scope, not delegated down.

On the team side, you're managing both office staff and maintenance. That includes training, coaching, and holding people accountable. You'll direct leasing and renewal programs to keep occupancy where it needs to be, and you'll work alongside your team on marketing strategy and execution. Vendor contracts and one-time projects also run through you: bidding, negotiating, managing.

Property condition is yours to own. Regular inspections, market-ready units, amenity upkeep. You'll tour the community with clients, vendors, and staff when needed. The schedule is Monday through Friday with hours that flex between 8 AM and 6 PM, plus availability for after-hours resident events and the occasional emergency.

What Olympus Is Looking For

  • Minimum two years of experience as a property manager in multifamily
  • Luxury Class A experience is preferred
  • Familiarity with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite is a strong plus
  • Comfortable with financial reporting and budget management, not just leasing metrics

The candidates who stand out here tend to be operators first. Strong leasing instincts matter, but Olympus is asking this person to run a business unit. If you've managed NOI conversations with regional leadership and built annual budgets from scratch, that experience carries real weight in this process.

Compensation and Growth

Base pay runs $85,000 to $90,000 depending on experience and location. The role is also eligible for monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program. Olympus has also built out formal career pathing, leadership conferences, and budget training specifically for onsite managers who want to move toward regional roles.

Olympus earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer recognition in 2023, 2024, and 2025. That kind of consistency usually signals something real about how the company treats its people, and it's worth factoring in when you're comparing offers.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Student housing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. Turnover isn't a slow trickle across the year. It happens in a compressed window, usually a few weeks in late summer, when every unit on the property needs to be cleaned, punched, and ready before thousands of students arrive. The Assistant Community Manager at The Magnolia at Auburn sits right in the middle of that cycle, and the rest of the year too.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a broad operations role that reports to the General Manager and steps into that seat when needed. Day to day, you're managing resident accounts, utility billing, and accounts receivable while keeping delinquency under 2% by month-end. You're handling escalated resident concerns, posting damage charges from quarterly inspections, and responding to Google and Yelp reviews through Entrata. You're also coordinating with the Customer and Sales Experience Manager on leasing KPIs, concessions, and velocity trends.

When turn season arrives, the job shifts gear entirely. You're tracking progress through Turnable, walking units with vendors, helping assess move-out damage, processing final billing and refund calculations, and getting hands-on with whatever needs doing. Moving furniture, organizing trash, helping the facilities team close out punch lists. The job description says it plainly, and it's worth repeating: this role includes physical work during turn. That's the reality of student housing at scale.

On the people side, you'll help recruit, onboard, and develop on-site staff, coordinate scheduling including after-hours on-call coverage, and support morale through what are genuinely high-pressure stretches.

What Scion Expects You to Bring

  • At least one year of experience in property management or residential communities
  • Proficiency in a property management system, with Entrata preferred
  • Comfort working across platforms: Greenhouse, Lattice, Turnable, Qualtrics, ClickUp, and Microsoft Office
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including resident-facing correspondence
  • Attention to detail on financial reporting, account reconciliation, and compliance with local ordinances
  • Confidentiality, especially when handling account disputes or personnel matters

The Honest Part

Student housing is genuinely demanding. After-hours emergencies are real. Turn is exhausting. Residents and their parents can be a difficult combination to manage. If you've worked conventional multifamily and found the lease renewal cycle too slow, student housing will fix that. If you've worked student housing before, you already know what you're signing up for.

What this role does offer is real breadth. You'll touch financial performance, facilities coordination, leasing strategy, team development, and customer experience within a single position. That range makes the Assistant Community Manager track one of the more useful launching pads toward a General Manager seat, particularly for someone who wants to understand how all the pieces of a property connect before running one independently.

Scion offers health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with matching, paid parental leave, floating holidays, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. The position is exempt and based on-site at The Magnolia at Auburn.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The One at Hope Mills is a Hawthorne Residential Partners community in Cumberland County, where the rental market draws a steady mix of military-connected households from Fort Liberty and long-term local renters. Occupancy and retention both matter here, and the Assistant Community Manager touches both directly every day.

On the leasing side, you'll handle incoming traffic, conduct tours, and walk prospects through the full leasing process from initial inquiry to signed lease. You'll track leads, manage application documentation, and work toward occupancy goals through both new leases and renewals. Social media content for the community falls to this role too, which means staying visible and keeping residents engaged between events.

The financial piece of this job carries real weight. You'll post payments, scan checks, monitor the delinquency report, and make weekly follow-up calls on past-due accounts. Ledger accuracy is part of the routine, and when accounts escalate, you'll coordinate eviction procedures alongside the Community Manager. You'll also assist with financial reporting for regional leadership, so comfort reading account ledgers and understanding where numbers come from matters more than most ACM postings let on.

When the Community Manager is out, you run the site. That means keeping the team on task, maintaining resident communication, and making judgment calls without waiting for direction.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of property management experience, with six months in an assistant manager capacity preferred
  • Solid grasp of rent collection workflows, delinquency follow-up, and ledger review
  • Leasing experience that includes guiding prospects and closing
  • Comfort stepping into a leadership role when the manager is unavailable
  • A valid driver's license
  • CALP accreditation is a plus but not required

Context Worth Knowing

Hawthorne ranks among the top 50 multifamily management companies nationally, with deep roots in the Southeast. Their Career Path Program is a genuine structural commitment, and the Assistant Community Manager role is a recognized step toward Community Manager. Candidates who move up quickly tend to be the ones who treat the financial reporting side of the ACM role as seriously as leasing. Understanding how delinquency affects NOI, and being able to explain a ledger discrepancy clearly to a Community Manager or regional director, separates candidates who stay in this seat from those who move into the next one.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off including your birthday, pet insurance, paid parental leave, and company-paid life insurance. The schedule runs Monday through Friday with Saturday hours, one weekday off each week, and occasional evening or weekend availability for community events.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Maintenance Supervisor at a Luxury Jacksonville Community

Waypoint Management Services is looking for a Maintenance Supervisor to take full ownership of operations at a high-end luxury community in Jacksonville. This is a supervisory role in the truest sense: you're not just turning wrenches, you're running a department. Budget oversight, vendor accountability, make-ready timelines, preventive maintenance schedules, and emergency response all land on your desk.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

Your mornings typically start with a walk of the property and a check on open work orders. The 24-hour response standard is real here, so your team's pace matters. You'll review make-ready conditions with contractors, keep punch lists moving, and make sure units are genuinely move-in ready before keys change hands. HVAC preventive maintenance, pool chemical logs, trash compactor upkeep, and gate and security equipment checks are recurring responsibilities, not occasional ones. You'll also be doing hands-on repairs yourself when the situation calls for it, including plumbing, carpentry, and general building systems.

On the administrative side, you're managing the maintenance budget and keeping tool and equipment inventory accurate. You're coordinating with the Community Manager on anything that touches the resident experience, which at a luxury property is a higher bar than most.

What Waypoint Is Looking For

  • Prior supervisory experience leading both employees and outside vendors or contractors
  • EPA Section 608 certification (Types I and II), required at hire
  • CPO certification, or willingness to obtain it within 90 days
  • CAMT certification, preferred
  • Hands-on skills across plumbing, general repairs, carpentry, and HVAC
  • Comfort with on-call scheduling
  • Bilingual in Spanish and English, strongly preferred
  • High school diploma or GED with at least two years of relevant maintenance experience

The bilingual preference is worth noting. Jacksonville has a growing Spanish-speaking resident population, and a supervisor who can communicate directly with both residents and contractors in Spanish moves faster and avoids miscommunications that cost time and trust.

Waypoint offers medical, dental, and vision benefits starting on day one, a 401k with matching, an employee referral program, recognition and incentive opportunities, and an onsite housing discount. For candidates who are serious about the maintenance leadership track, this kind of package at a luxury asset is a reasonable place to build.

Strong candidates in this kind of role tend to separate themselves not by technical skill alone, but by how they run their team under pressure. When a weekend HVAC emergency hits in the middle of a Florida summer, the supervisor who already has a vendor relationship and a backup plan handles it in two hours. The one who's still building those systems handles it in eight. Waypoint's residents will notice the difference.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Multi-property maintenance work in a dense urban market like West Hollywood demands a different kind of technician than a single-site role. You're moving between properties, triaging competing priorities, and making judgment calls without a supervisor looking over your shoulder. Property Management Associates has operated in the greater Los Angeles area for over 30 years, managing a large residential portfolio across Southern California, and this full-time position supports multiple sites in the West Hollywood area.

What the Role Requires

PMA is looking for at least three years of hands-on experience across the core trades: plumbing, electrical, drywall, and appliance repair. Rent-ready apartment preparation is a meaningful part of this work, so comfort with the full make-ready process matters. You'll handle resident work orders, conduct routine property inspections, manage parts inventory, and coordinate order fulfillment to keep repairs on schedule. Saturday availability is part of the expectation when the workload calls for it.

Because you'll cover multiple properties, a valid driver's license and personal auto insurance are required. PMA provides an auto allowance of $300 per month and a cell phone allowance of $25 per month, along with tools and dedicated tool storage. Compensation runs $23.00 to $26.00 per hour at 40 hours per week.

  • Minimum 3 years of experience in plumbing, electrical, drywall, and appliance repair
  • Proficiency with rent-ready unit preparation and punch list completion
  • Ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds and remain on your feet for up to 8 hours
  • Strong organizational skills for parts inventory and work order tracking
  • Valid driver's license with proof of auto insurance
  • Fluent English communication skills

What This Role Builds

Technicians who work multi-property portfolios develop a sharper diagnostic instinct than those fixed to a single site. When you're seeing dozens of different unit conditions across a large residential inventory, you start to recognize failure patterns faster, prioritize more accurately, and manage your own time with real discipline. Those skills transfer directly into lead maintenance, facilities management, or eventually a regional maintenance supervisor role.

PMA describes itself as a company that encourages an entrepreneurial mindset and invests in its staff. For a technician who wants to grow past the wrench, a large third-party management portfolio like this one provides exposure to a range of property types, ownership structures, and operational challenges that a smaller operator simply can't offer. The technicians who advance here tend to be the ones who treat inventory management and resident communication with the same seriousness as the physical repair work itself.

Compensation and Benefits

Full-time employees receive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with an employer contribution, a 401(k) with discretionary company match after one year, short-term and long-term disability coverage, and paid time off covering vacation, sick time, and holidays. Critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity plans are also available.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Bozzuto builds and manages properties with a reputation for quality that's visible at the unit level, and this role sits right at the center of protecting that reputation. As an Assistant Maintenance Manager at their Alexandria community, you're the person who keeps asset value intact, turns make-readies efficiently, and builds the kind of maintenance culture where residents actually notice the difference.

What You'll Actually Do

The make-ready process will be a significant part of your rhythm. You'll manage apartment turns from punch list to final walk, keeping units moving through the pipeline so leasing can do its job. Beyond turns, you'll handle HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repairs directly while also coaching the team around you. Preventative maintenance programs are yours to execute consistently, not just schedule. You'll also take responsibility for the building's mechanical systems, which at a Bozzuto property may include central plant equipment, split systems, boilers, and chillers. Grounds upkeep, snow removal, and code compliance round out the scope. Weekend availability and participation in an on-call emergency rotation are part of the role year-round.

What You Bring

  • At least five years working in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • Hands-on proficiency in HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • HVAC, EPA, or NAPE certification
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards, MSDS, and risk management principles
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Some supervisory or leadership experience, even informal
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office and property management technology platforms
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently and work in variable weather conditions

Where This Role Leads

The Assistant Maintenance Manager title is a real stepping stone in this industry. People who do this job well tend to move into Building Maintenance Manager or Portfolio Maintenance Manager positions within a few years. The skills that compound fastest here are the leadership ones: learning to delegate repairs you could do yourself, building accountability into a team's daily habits, and communicating maintenance status clearly to property management. Those skills transfer directly into senior operations roles where you're less hands-on-tools and more hands-on-systems.

What separates strong candidates from average ones at this level is the ability to think about asset preservation proactively rather than reactively. Anyone can respond to a work order. The people who advance are the ones who catch the HVAC inefficiency before it becomes a capital expense, or who keep a turn on schedule when a vendor falls through. If that mindset already describes how you work, this position is a natural fit.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
This role puts three skill sets to work every day: financial analysis, tenant relationship management, and team leadership. If any one of those is weak, the job gets hard fast. Lincoln Property Company is looking for a Property Manager in Los Angeles to run commercial assets, which may include office, retail, and industrial properties, and to do it at a level that serves both the client and the tenants well.

The Skills This Role Leans On Most

Financial fluency sits at the center of this position. You'll own the monthly reporting cycle, build annual operating and capital budgets, and track CAM and OpX recovery charges with enough precision to hold up under client scrutiny. Variance analysis and ROI recommendations are part of the regular workflow, not occasional asks. Intermediate to advanced Excel is a baseline requirement. Yardi or MRI experience will save you significant ramp time.

Tenant management is the other constant. You'll handle move-ins, move-outs, space walk-throughs, and ongoing tenant care with the goal of keeping retention high. That means being responsive, communicating clearly under pressure, and running a proactive AR process before delinquency becomes a client-level issue. Your ability to read a lease and translate its financial implications matters here because you'll also be coordinating lease administration and flagging expiration risk to ownership.

On the leadership side, you'll direct a team, manage vendor relationships and procurement, run the bid process, and hold contractors accountable to contract terms. You'll recruit, coach, and conduct performance reviews. The expectation is that you're the subject matter expert your team turns to, and the owner representative your clients rely on.

Qualifications Worth Noting

  • 3 to 5 years of commercial property management experience, ideally across office, retail, or industrial assets
  • Bachelor's degree preferred; relevant experience considered
  • California Real Estate License required
  • CPM or RPA designation, or active candidacy, preferred
  • Strong Excel skills; Yardi, MRI, and Kardin familiarity are a plus
  • Ability to be on-site at assigned properties regularly and available after hours when situations demand it

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Commercial PM in Los Angeles means managing properties where tenant expectations run high and lease structures can be complex. The managers who perform well here track covenant and encumbrance details proactively rather than reactively, and they build tenant relationships that reduce turnover before it shows up in the numbers. If you've delivered insightful variance reports that actually changed a client's capital decision, that experience translates directly to this role. Lincoln Property Company operates at institutional scale, so comfort working within structured processes while still driving results independently is a real differentiator.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Weinstein Properties has been family-owned for over 70 years, and that tenure shows in how they run their sites. This is a hands-on assistant manager role at Bexley Steelecroft in south Charlotte, part of a portfolio that spans more than 60 communities across five states. The position covers the full operational spectrum: leasing, resident relations, renewals, move-outs, delinquency follow-up, and supporting the property manager on day-to-day decisions.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A typical day here won't be spent behind a desk. You'll work internet leads and phone inquiries, schedule and conduct tours, process applications, and execute lease paperwork from start to signature. On the resident services side, you'll handle renewals, notices to vacate, early terminations, transfers, pet addendums, and account questions. You'll also post rent, chase open balances, and coordinate with maintenance on make-readies, walking units to confirm punch list completion before move-in. Move-out processing and security deposit dispositions are part of the role, as is helping plan and host resident events. The schedule includes rotating Saturdays and occasional evenings for those events.

Weinstein is direct about expectations: this is a high-output position with real accountability. If you've managed a team in hospitality, retail, or sales and you're organized under pressure, they'll train you on the property management specifics. Prior PM experience is a plus, but it's not a hard requirement if your management fundamentals are solid.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The candidates who thrive here tend to have genuine fluency in difficult conversations. Renewals, delinquency calls, security deposit disputes, and early termination requests all require someone who can hold firm while keeping the resident relationship intact. That's a skill set you either bring or you build quickly. Weinstein provides structured training and coaching, but the job moves fast, and the learning curve is real.

  • Demonstrated leadership or supervisory experience in a service-heavy environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to handle tense conversations professionally
  • Comfort with multitasking across leasing, operations, and administrative tasks in the same shift
  • Detail orientation, particularly around lease documents and financial transactions
  • Flexibility to work rotating Saturdays and occasional evening hours

Growth and Compensation

The role starts at $21 per hour with increases based on experience, plus quarterly bonuses. Benefits include a rent discount, health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with company match, paid holidays, birthday time off, and an employee assistance program.

Weinstein has a track record of promoting from within. The assistant manager role is a genuine entry point into property management leadership. Many site managers and regional staff at companies like this started exactly here, handling leasing and operations before moving into full management responsibilities. If you want a defined path rather than a vague promise of growth, this structure tends to deliver it.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Prelude at the Park
job.description:
Maintenance Supervisors at well-run apartment communities do a lot more than fix things. They set the standard for how a property runs day to day, how residents feel about where they live, and how well the maintenance team performs under pressure. This opening at Prelude at the Park in Henderson, NV with MG Properties is a good example of a role where those responsibilities are real and taken seriously.

What You'll Actually Do

The work here spans three distinct areas: hands-on technical work, team oversight, and administrative accountability. On any given day, you might be diagnosing an HVAC issue in one unit, reviewing a punch list from a make-ready, and checking in with a technician on a pending service request. You'll manage the system for tracking resident work orders, coordinate scheduling for your maintenance staff, and make sure preventive maintenance records stay accurate and current. You'll also run regularly scheduled safety meetings, which matters more than it sounds. A team that takes safety seriously has fewer injuries, fewer liability issues, and better morale.

MG Properties operates across the Western U.S. with over three decades in acquisition, development, rehab, and management. They're not a startup figuring things out. The infrastructure exists. Your job is to run the maintenance operation at this specific community with competence and consistency.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of experience in a Maintenance Supervisor role, preferably at a community of 150 units or more
  • Demonstrated experience across multiple trades, including HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general repair
  • A track record of managing and directing a maintenance team, not just working alongside one
  • Strong customer service instincts and the ability to communicate clearly with residents and property management staff
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation

Where This Role Fits in a Maintenance Career

Supervisors who do this job well build skills that transfer directly into Regional Maintenance Director roles or Facilities Manager positions at larger portfolios. What compounds fastest here is the administrative side: managing expenditures, maintaining records, and coordinating with property management on capex planning. Those skills separate candidates who stay at the site level from those who move up. Henderson is also a market with consistent multifamily growth, which means experienced maintenance leadership stays in demand. If you're thinking about your next two or three moves, this is a role that puts useful things on your resume and keeps options open.

MG Properties offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, profit sharing, monthly bonuses, paid holidays, paid sick time, and rental discounts. They're an equal opportunity employer and participate in E-Verify.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager (Kiku Crossing)
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning and a resident has questions about their recertification paperwork, the maintenance request from unit 14 still needs a follow-up, and the bank deposit has to go out before noon. That's a normal hour in this role.

Kiku Crossing is part of MidPen Housing's portfolio of more than 130 affordable communities across Northern California, serving working families, seniors, and residents with special needs. This Assistant Community Manager position supports the day-to-day operations of the property under the direction of the Community Manager, with real responsibility across leasing administration, fiscal tasks, compliance, and resident relations.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A significant part of this role is compliance-driven. Affordable housing operates under layered regulatory requirements, and you'll be helping process recertifications, welfare exemption documents, and reviews tied to programs like TCAC and HUD's Management and Occupancy Review process. If you haven't worked in affordable housing before, that learning curve is real. The income verification and waitlist management side of the job requires accuracy and consistency, not just effort.

Beyond compliance, you'll handle the operational rhythm of the property: scheduling turns, monitoring turnover forms, processing work orders with the facilities team, collecting rents, managing petty cash logs, and preparing bank deposits. You'll also conduct property inspections to flag maintenance and security concerns, which means you're not just behind a desk. Resident communication is a steady part of the job too, from emergency preparedness procedures to coordinating resident meetings.

  • Leasing administration: income verification appointments, lease preparation, waitlist management
  • Compliance support: recertifications, MOR and TCAC review preparation, exemption documents
  • Fiscal tasks: rent collection, security deposit processing, petty cash logs, bank deposit preparation
  • Facilities coordination: work order tracking, property inspections, maintenance follow-up
  • Resident relations: notices, meeting coordination, emergency communication
  • File maintenance: resident and property records, handled with confidentiality

Who Fits This Role

MidPen is looking for someone with at least a high school diploma or GED and one year of experience in residential property management, customer service, or administrative work. Familiarity with RealPage is a plus. Strong written and verbal communication matter here because you're dealing with residents who may be navigating stressful housing situations, and how you communicate directly affects their experience.

What separates stronger candidates in affordable housing administration isn't just organization, though that's essential. It's the ability to hold firm on compliance requirements while still treating residents with patience and respect. Those two things can feel like they pull in opposite directions on a hard day. The candidates who thrive here find a way to do both.

Pay runs from $21.15 to $23.80 per hour depending on experience. MidPen offers a full benefits package including health, dental, vision, life and disability coverage, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, FSA options, an employee education reimbursement program, and pet insurance, among others.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor (Trestle)
job.description:
It's 7 AM and a resident just flagged a water heater failure in one of the units. Your team lead is already fielding two other work orders, and you're deciding in real time whether to pull in a vendor or handle it in-house. That's a normal Tuesday at Trestle.

The Role at Trestle in San Carlos

Prometheus Real Estate Group is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor (internally called a Neighborhood Service Manager) for Trestle, one of their Bay Area communities in San Carlos. Prometheus is the largest privately held apartment owner in the Bay Area, with over 13,000 units across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle. They're vertically integrated, which means decisions about capex, renovations, and operations run through the same organization. That structure matters for this role because you're not waiting on a distant corporate office to approve every vendor call or repair budget. You have real responsibility for physical operations, and you're accountable to outcomes.

The day-to-day covers the full range: scheduling and supervising your maintenance team, managing vendors and contractors, keeping up with safety training, overseeing capital projects, and controlling costs through the maintenance budget. You'll own the punch list culture on your property. Make-readies, preventive maintenance cycles, inventory management, and on-call response all fall within your scope. The on-call piece is real. This position requires genuine availability outside standard business hours when the property needs it.

Leadership is a meaningful part of the job. You'll hire, train, and mentor your team. When problems come up between staff or between staff and residents, you're the one working through them. Prometheus uses their own operating standards, so you'll also be the person your team looks to for answers on compliance, safety rules, and company policy.

What Prometheus Is Looking For

  • At least five years of apartment maintenance experience
  • At least two years in a supervisory capacity
  • A minimum of three certificates from recognized maintenance or trade programs (BOMA, IREM, or vocational equivalents)
  • Working knowledge of federal, state, and local safety regulations
  • Ability to read and apply safety rules, operating manuals, and maintenance instructions
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 lbs. occasionally, with the stamina the role requires
  • High school diploma or GED

Strong candidates will have experience in California specifically. The state's regulatory environment around habitability, safety inspections, and contractor licensing adds a layer of complexity that someone newer to California maintenance supervision will feel immediately. If you've already managed vendors and capex projects under California requirements, that experience will show quickly in this role.

Compensation runs from $40.25 to $44.00 per hour, with a discretionary semi-annual bonus and additional standby and on-call premium pay. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, vision, and dental coverage for eligible employees and dependents, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, and tenure-based housing discounts. Prometheus also offers paid volunteer time and recognizes employee birthdays as a paid holiday, which is a small detail that tends to say something about a company's culture.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

The Assistant Community Manager role at Hawthorne Residential Partners sits at the intersection of leasing performance and financial accountability. You're reading ledgers, posting payments, monitoring delinquency, and chasing down aged balances one hour, then walking a prospect through an available home the next. The skill set that makes someone effective here is genuinely dual: you need enough leasing instinct to move traffic through the funnel and enough financial discipline to keep the books clean week to week.

Evolve at Wildwood is located in Wildwood, FL, a market that's seen steady residential growth tied to the broader Villages corridor. Communities in this area compete on both price and experience, which means occupancy goals don't get hit by accident. Renewal rates matter here. Concessions need to be managed carefully. The person in this seat needs to understand how renewal performance connects directly to NOI, not just treat renewals as paperwork.

What You'll Be Managing Day to Day

On the leasing side, you'll handle inbound leads, conduct tours, and shepherd prospects through the application and move-in process. Lease documents need to be accurate and timely. You'll also manage social media content for the community, which in practice means staying current on resident events and knowing how to present the property in a way that generates genuine interest.

On the financial side, your responsibilities include:

  • Rent collection, check scanning, and payment posting
  • Weekly delinquency follow-up calls and coordination of eviction procedures when required
  • Ledger audits to verify billing accuracy and correct payment application
  • Financial reporting support for the Community Manager and regional leadership

You'll also step into the Community Manager role during absences, which means you can't be passive about understanding how the community operates at a leadership level. That coverage responsibility is where a lot of ACMs either develop fast or get exposed. Hawthorne's Career Path Program is built around exactly that progression, with a direct track from ACM to Community Manager for people who earn it.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Two years of property management experience is preferred, along with at least six months in an ACM or similar role. A CALP accreditation is a plus. But beyond credentials, the candidates who thrive in this position are the ones who can read a delinquency report and feel urgency, not just process it as a task. They follow up on aged balances the same way they follow up on a warm lead: with intention and a clear next step.

Conflict resolution is a real daily variable in this role.
